blueline-park-sky-capsule.name: Haeundae Blueline Park Sky Capsule (Mipo - Cheongsapo)
blueline-park-sky-capsule.summary: Small private pastel pods that run on an elevated rail 7-10 m above the old Donghae Nambu coastal railway. They carry 2-4 riders from Mipo to Cheongsapo at about 4 km/h, roughly 30 minutes one way, with the sea right below.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.why: The closest Busan match to the Enoden coastal train in Kamakura: a slow ride along the sea past fishing villages and lighthouses. One capsule fits all 3 travelers.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.autumn_note: October is shoulder season: clear, dry air with good visibility and less heat-haze than summer. Late-afternoon departures catch golden light on Cheongsapo's twin lighthouses.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.time_needed: 30 min ride + 1.5-2.5 h combined with the Beach Train and Cheongsapo
blueline-park-sky-capsule.hours: October (shoulder season, also Mar/Apr): 08:30-18:30. Hours can shift on busy weekends and holidays. Normal rain does not stop service; extreme weather does.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.cost_note: Price is per capsule, one way. Official regular fares: 2 riders 50,000; 3 riders 55,000 (about 18,300 each); 4 riders 60,000. Discounted resident/senior fares (40k/45k/50k) do not apply to foreigners. No round-trip fare is listed. Package of Sky Capsule one way + Beach Train all-stations is 103,000 for 3 adults (55,000 + 3 x 16,000), so no saving over buying separately. Some blogs quote older or discounted prices of 30-45k; trust the official site.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.booking: Official site bluelinepark.com (Korean UI; checkout may need Korean phone verification), at the Mipo or Cheongsapo ticket office on the day, or via Klook, KKday or Trip.com, which foreigners can use easily. Book as soon as the target date opens: an unverified 2026 blog says bookings open weekly about 4 weeks ahead (Tuesdays 07:00). Weekend and holiday slots sell out; weekday mornings are the easiest.
blueline-park-sky-capsule.tips: Ride Mipo to Cheongsapo by capsule, walk Cheongsapo and its Daritdol Skywalk, then take the Beach Train on to Songjeong (or back). Sit facing the sea; the right side heading east. Bring the booking QR, and arrive 10-15 min before the slot. During BTS-concert week (Jun 2026) the park ran a promo with 3-4 riders at the 2-rider price, so watch for similar promos.

blueline-park-beach-train.name: Haeundae Blueline Park Beach Train (Mipo - Songjeong)
blueline-park-beach-train.area: Mipo - Dalmaji Tunnel - Cheongsapo - Daritdol Skywalk - Gudeokpo - Songjeong
blueline-park-beach-train.summary: Tram-like sightseeing train with sideways sea-facing seats. It runs 4.8 km along the coast with 7 stops from Mipo (Haeundae) to Songjeong Beach, and you can hop on and off.
blueline-park-beach-train.why: The second half of the Enoden analog: hop off at Cheongsapo (fishing village and lighthouses), Daritdol Skywalk and Gudeokpo, then finish at the surf beach in Songjeong, much like Enoden ending at Enoshima and Shichirigahama.
blueline-park-beach-train.autumn_note: Comfortable October temperatures, roughly 15-22 C. The sun sets around 17:45 in late October, so aim for a 16:00-17:00 run.
blueline-park-beach-train.time_needed: About 25-30 min end to end, or 2-3 h with stops
blueline-park-beach-train.hours: October: departures from Mipo and from Songjeong 09:00-19:30. Times may change on weekends and holidays.
blueline-park-beach-train.cost_note: Official: single ride 10,000 boarding at Mipo or Songjeong, 8,000 boarding at Cheongsapo or other intermediate stops; 2-ride ticket 14,000; all-stations hop-on pass 16,000.
blueline-park-beach-train.booking: Same as the Sky Capsule: bluelinepark.com, station counters, Klook/KKday. It sells out less often than the capsule, but time slots fill on weekends.
blueline-park-beach-train.tips: The all-stations pass makes sense if you want to stop at Cheongsapo and Daritdol. Some Visit Busan Pass versions have included the beach train in the past; check before buying separately.

cheongsapo.name: Cheongsapo Village, Twin Lighthouses and Daritdol Skywalk
cheongsapo.summary: Small fishing harbour between Haeundae and Songjeong, known for red and white twin lighthouses, grilled clam shacks, cafes and a glass-floored skywalk out over the rocks.
cheongsapo.why: Feels like the small fishing coves near Kamakura and Enoshima: low-key, salty air, seafood and sea-view cafes.
cheongsapo.autumn_note: October is a good month for grilled shellfish (jogae-gui) here.
cheongsapo.hours: Village open always. The Daritdol skywalk is roughly 09:00-18:00 (2024-25 info; unverified for 2026).
cheongsapo.closed: Skywalk may close in bad weather
cheongsapo.cost_note: Free. Grilled clam platters for 3 people run about 50,000-70,000 KRW (2025 level).
cheongsapo.tips: Reach it by Sky Capsule or Beach Train; bus 2 or 141 from Haeundae as a fallback.

dalmaji-gil.name: Dalmaji-gil (Moontan Road)
dalmaji-gil.summary: Winding cliff road above Mipo with sea-view cafes, galleries and the Haewoljeong pavilion. A boardwalk trail (Moontan-ro) runs through the pines.
dalmaji-gil.why: A calm, upscale counterpart to the Shibuya-like bustle of Haeundae, similar to the hilltop cafe roads around Kamakura and Hayama.
dalmaji-gil.autumn_note: Cherry trees here turn red-orange in late October to November, earlier than Busan's mountain foliage.
dalmaji-gil.tips: Walk up from Mipo or take a taxi to Haewoljeong, then walk down to Cheongsapo through the forest boardwalk.

haedong-yonggungsa.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
haedong-yonggungsa.summary: Rare seaside Buddhist temple on rocks above the waves, with a sea-facing Haesu Gwaneum Daebul statue, stone lanterns and the 108-step approach.
haedong-yonggungsa.why: The most Kamakura/Enoshima-like temple moment in Korea: temple + surf in one frame. Busy like Hase-dera.
haedong-yonggungsa.autumn_note: Mild October weather; go at opening to avoid tour buses; sunrise from the rocks is the classic shot.
haedong-yonggungsa.tips: Bus 181/1001 or taxi from Haeundae/Songjeong (~15-20 min). Combine with Ananti Cove or Gijang Daebyeon harbor seafood lunch.

huinnyeoul-culture-village.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village and Jeollyeong Coastal Walk
huinnyeoul-culture-village.summary: White cliffside houses stacked above the sea on Yeongdo, with narrow lanes, cafes looking over the anchored ships, a seaside tunnel and a coastal walk below. Film set for 'The Attorney'.
huinnyeoul-culture-village.why: Probably the most Kamakura-like neighbourhood in Busan: small lanes, cafes and the ocean at every turn, much like the cliffside lanes of Enoshima.
huinnyeoul-culture-village.autumn_note: Sunset over the anchored ships is spectacular in October and the weather is mild.
huinnyeoul-culture-village.hours: Village always open; cafes about 10:00-19:00. Many shops close one weekday, often Monday or Tuesday.
huinnyeoul-culture-village.closed: Village none. Residents live here, so keep quiet.
huinnyeoul-culture-village.tips: Combine with Taejongdae (10 min taxi) and the Samjin Eomuk flagship on Yeongdo. Bus 7, 71 or 508 from Nampo.

taejongdae.name: Taejongdae Park
taejongdae.summary: Wooded headland of sea cliffs with a lighthouse, the Sinseon rock platform, an observatory and a 4.3 km loop road served by the Danubi road train.
taejongdae.why: The rugged-nature counterpart to Izu's coastal cliffs.
taejongdae.autumn_note: Evergreen forest, so little foliage colour, but cool weather makes the loop walk pleasant.
taejongdae.hours: Park roughly 04:00-24:00. Danubi train about 09:30-17:30 (2024-25 info).
taejongdae.closed: Danubi may not run in bad weather; no fixed closing day confirmed
taejongdae.cost_note: Park entry free. Danubi road train about 4,000 KRW for adults (2024-25 price, unverified for 2026). Walking the loop is free.
taejongdae.booking: Danubi tickets on site only; queues form at weekends
taejongdae.tips: Walk down to the lighthouse and Sinseon rock. Bus 8, 30, 66 or 101 from Nampo or Busan Station.

gamcheon-culture-village.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
gamcheon-culture-village.summary: Hillside settlement of postwar refugees, painted in pastel colours, with art installations, small galleries, a 'Little Prince' photo spot and maze-like alleys.
gamcheon-culture-village.why: Colourful stair-and-alley wandering, but busier and more touristy than Huinnyeoul. If you only have time for one, Huinnyeoul feels more like Kamakura.
gamcheon-culture-village.hours: Village always open; shops and info centre about 09:00-18:00 (Nov-Feb to 17:00)
gamcheon-culture-village.cost_note: Free; the stamp map is about 2,000 KRW
gamcheon-culture-village.tips: Take a taxi or maeul bus 1-1, 2 or 2-2 up from Toseong station (Line 1) and walk downhill. Go before 10:00 or late afternoon.

oryukdo-skywalk.name: Oryukdo Skywalk
oryukdo-skywalk.summary: Glass-floored horseshoe platform on a 35 m cliff overlooking the Oryukdo islets, at the meeting point of the East Sea and the South Sea. Southern start of the Igidae coastal walk.
oryukdo-skywalk.why: A short, dramatic seaside viewpoint to pair with the Igidae walk.
oryukdo-skywalk.autumn_note: Late October is the end of the season for the cosmos and silver grass on the Oryukdo Haemaji Park slope beside the skywalk (2025 pattern).
oryukdo-skywalk.closed: Closes in rain, strong wind and snow
oryukdo-skywalk.tips: Bus 27 or 131 from Kyungsung Univ/Pukyong station. Start here and walk north on Igidae toward Gwangalli.

igidae-coastal-walk.name: Igidae Coastal Walk (Galmaet-gil section 2)
igidae-coastal-walk.summary: About 4.7 km of cliffside boardwalks, suspension bridges and rocky coves from Oryukdo Skywalk to Dongsaengmal, with continuous views of Gwangan Bridge and the Haeundae skyline.
igidae-coastal-walk.why: Matches the coastal hiking of the Izu peninsula, but ends at a city skyline, mixing nature and the bustling city.
igidae-coastal-walk.autumn_note: October is the best month for it: cool and dry. Some silver grass grows on the headlands.
igidae-coastal-walk.tips: Walk south to north (Oryukdo to Dongsaengmal) so the Gwangan Bridge view is ahead of you, then continue to Gwangalli for dinner and the night view. Wear proper shoes; there are many stairs.

gwangalli-beach.name: Gwangalli Beach and Gwangan Bridge
gwangalli-beach.summary: Urban beach facing the lit-up Gwangan suspension bridge, lined with bars, cafes and raw-fish restaurants. Busan's liveliest night-time waterfront.
gwangalli-beach.why: Shibuya energy meets the seaside: buzzing at night with a light show over the water.
gwangalli-beach.autumn_note: The drone show season continues on Saturdays. The Busan Fireworks Festival here is on Nov 7 2026, after the trip.
gwangalli-beach.hours: Bridge lighting nightly (about sunset to midnight)
gwangalli-beach.tips: Millak Waterfront Park and the Millak raw fish centre are at the north end. Metro Line 2 to Gwangan or Geumnyeonsan station.

gwangalli-drone-show.name: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
gwangalli-drone-show.summary: Free show of about 1,100 drones over Gwangalli Beach every Saturday, roughly 12 minutes per show. Oct-Feb times are 19:00 and 21:00.
gwangalli-drone-show.why: A one-of-a-kind neon-and-sky spectacle, the Busan equivalent of a Shibuya night.
gwangalli-drone-show.autumn_note: October 2026 programme: Oct 17 'Dimensional Station' with lasers; Oct 24 'Forest's Melody' (enchanted-forest theme with a violin-playing fox). Only Oct 24 is realistic for this trip, since Oct 17 is arrival day in Incheon.
gwangalli-drone-show.closed: Cancelled in bad weather or strong wind
gwangalli-drone-show.booking: None; arrive 30 min early for a beach spot in the centre
gwangalli-drone-show.tips: Watch from the sand in front of 219 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro, or book a restaurant or hotel room with a bridge view. The 21:00 show is less crowded.

busan-x-the-sky.name: BUSAN X the SKY (Haeundae LCT Landmark Tower observatory)
busan-x-the-sky.summary: Observatory on floors 98-100 of the 411 m LCT tower, with views over Haeundae beach, Gwangan Bridge and the coastline, plus a high-altitude cafe.
busan-x-the-sky.why: The Shibuya Sky equivalent of Busan.
busan-x-the-sky.autumn_note: Clear October days give long visibility; aim for sunset (about 17:45 late Oct).
busan-x-the-sky.hours: About 10:00-21:00, last entry 20:30 (2024-25 info, unverified for 2026)
busan-x-the-sky.cost_note: Adult about 27,000 KRW (2024-25 price); usually cheaper on Klook. Included in some Visit Busan Pass versions. Unverified for 2026: official site would not load.
busan-x-the-sky.booking: Walk up, official site busanxthesky.com, or Klook/KKday
busan-x-the-sky.tips: Skip it if you already do the Seoul Sky / N Seoul Tower, or if a sea-view hotel room already gives you the view.

jagalchi-market.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
jagalchi-market.summary: Korea's largest seafood market on the Nampo harbour front. Pick live fish downstairs and have it cut and served as hoe (sashimi) at an upstairs restaurant.
jagalchi-market.why: The Tsukiji-style counterpart for sushi-omakase lovers: the freshest raw fish in Busan, eaten on the spot.
jagalchi-market.autumn_note: Autumn favourites: jeon-eo (gizzard shad), galchi (hairtail) and flatfish. The Jagalchi Festival is usually in October (2025: Oct 23-26), but 2026 dates are unconfirmed.
jagalchi-market.hours: Roughly 05:00-22:00. Individual stalls and floors vary.
jagalchi-market.closed: The main Jagalchi Market building historically closes on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month (Oct 20 2026 is a 3rd Tuesday). Unverified for 2026.
jagalchi-market.cost_note: Assorted hoe for 3 is about 60,000-120,000 KRW plus a 4,000-5,000 KRW per-person table and side-dish charge.
jagalchi-market.tips: Agree on the price and weight before the fish is cut. Pair with BIFF Square and Gukje Market, both 5 min away.

biff-square-gukje-market.name: BIFF Square, Gukje Market and Bosu-dong Book Alley
biff-square-gukje-market.summary: Old-downtown market district: the film-festival plaza with ssiat hotteok (seed-stuffed pancake) and eomuk stalls, plus the sprawling postwar Gukje Market and the Kkangtong night market.
biff-square-gukje-market.why: Retro, crowded and full of street food: the Ameyoko-style side of Busan.
biff-square-gukje-market.autumn_note: BIFF 2026 runs Oct 6-15, so it ends before this trip.
biff-square-gukje-market.hours: Shops about 09:00-20:00; street food until about 22:00
biff-square-gukje-market.closed: Many Gukje stalls close on the 1st and 3rd Sunday (pattern before 2026, unverified)
biff-square-gukje-market.tips: Combine with Jagalchi, Yongdusan Park / Busan Tower and the Songdo cable car.

haeundae-market.name: Haeundae Traditional Market
haeundae-market.summary: Short covered market street near Haeundae station with tteokbokki, eomuk, fried snacks, grilled eel and seafood.
haeundae-market.why: An easy street-food dinner near the Haeundae hotels.
haeundae-market.tips: Sangguk-ine (상국이네) for tteokbokki and eomuk is a long-time favourite.

jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.name: Jeonpo Cafe Street and Seomyeon
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.summary: Former tool-shop alleys turned into dozens of indie cafes, bakeries and bars, next to Seomyeon, Busan's main downtown nightlife and shopping hub with its underground malls, pocha (tent bars) and the Seomyeon Market dwaeji gukbap (pork soup) alley.
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.why: The closest thing to Shibuya and Shimokitazawa in Busan: neon, youth crowds and late nights.
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.autumn_note: The Jeonpo Coffee Festival is on Oct 17-18 2026 (opening day = arrival day in Incheon; Sunday Oct 18 is only possible if already in Busan).
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.hours: Cafes about 11:00-22:00; Seomyeon bars until late
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.closed: Many cafes close one weekday, often Monday
jeonpo-cafe-street-seomyeon.tips: Metro Line 1/2 Seomyeon station; Jeonpo station on Line 2. Dwaeji gukbap alley is at Seomyeon Market.

songdo-cable-car.name: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car) and Songdo Skywalk
songdo-cable-car.summary: 1.62 km cable car crossing the bay from Songdo Beach to Amnam Park, with optional glass-floor 'Crystal' cabins. The Songdo Cloud Trail sea walkway is beside it.
songdo-cable-car.why: A playful seaside ride, much like the Enoshima-area attractions.
songdo-cable-car.autumn_note: The night views are good in October.
songdo-cable-car.hours: October: 09:00-21:00; ticket sales close 30 min before
songdo-cable-car.closed: No regular closing day listed; stops in high wind
songdo-cable-car.cost_note: Official, round trip adult: Air Cruise (standard) 19,000; Crystal Cruise (glass floor) 24,000
songdo-cable-car.booking: On site, busanaircruise.co.kr, or Klook (usually discounted)
songdo-cable-car.tips: Near the Fairfield by Marriott Songdo Beach. 15 min taxi from Nampo/Jagalchi.

hurshimchung.name: Hurshimchung Spa (Dongnae Hot Springs, Hotel Nongshim)
hurshimchung.summary: Natural hot-spring bathhouse attached to Hotel Nongshim, said to be the largest in Asia: about 40 baths under a glass dome, including cave, cypress and open-air baths. Fed by the 1,300-year-old Dongnae hot spring. Renovated for about 2 months; full operation resumed 1 May 2026.
hurshimchung.why: The closest thing in the city to a traditional onsen soak; Dongnae has been Busan's hot-spring town since the Silla era. Bathing is single-sex and nude, as at Japanese onsen.
hurshimchung.autumn_note: The Dongnae Eupseong History Festival runs Oct 16-18 2026 next door. Pleasant soaking weather.
hurshimchung.cost_note: 2026 prices: adult weekday 15,000; Sat/Sun/holidays 18,000. Jjimjilbang add-on 4,000.
hurshimchung.tips: Oncheonjang station (Line 1), about 10 min walk. Hotel Nongshim guests get access. Tattoos are generally tolerated in Korean bathhouses.

spa-land-centum.name: Spa Land Centum City (Shinsegae)
spa-land-centum.summary: Upscale jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse with sauna rooms) inside the world's largest department store, with 18 hot-spring baths fed by water from 1,000 m underground and 13 themed sauna rooms.
spa-land-centum.why: Polished bathhouse and sauna culture, an easy rainy-day choice. Still open in 2026.
spa-land-centum.autumn_note: Good for a rainy or chilly day.
spa-land-centum.cost_note: Official: adult 26,000 every day of the week, 4-hour limit; overtime 5,000/hour; stay up to 6 h if you spend 10,000+ inside. Bring luggage-free (outside lockers 3,000 for 5 h).
spa-land-centum.booking: Walk in; Klook/Waug sometimes slightly cheaper
spa-land-centum.tips: Centum City station (Line 2). Hurshimchung is cheaper and more onsen-like; Spa Land is newer and design-led.

ananti-water-house.name: Ananti at Busan Cove: Water House and seaside promenade
ananti-water-house.summary: Clifftop resort complex with a hot-spring spa (Water House) and an infinity pool by the sea, plus the 'Ananti Town' promenade with the Eternal Journey bookstore and cafes.
ananti-water-house.why: The most Izu-ryokan-like spot in Busan: a seaside hot-spring soak in a calm, design-led resort.
ananti-water-house.autumn_note: Water House hot-spring baths with sea views suit chilly October evenings.
ananti-water-house.hours: Water House hours vary by season (not verified for 2026)
ananti-water-house.cost_note: Water House admission is separate even for hotel guests in many rate plans. Earlier prices were about 40,000-80,000 KRW; not verified for 2026.
ananti-water-house.booking: Via ananti.kr; non-guest access may be restricted
ananti-water-house.tips: Free to walk the town and bookstore. A guest shuttle from Busan Station exit 9 has run since 11 Jul 2026. Check whether your rate includes Water House.

gijang-jukseong-ilgwang.name: Gijang coast: Jukseong Cathedral set and Ilgwang Beach
gijang-jukseong-ilgwang.summary: A small white and red church (built as a drama set) on a rock at Jukseong-ri, plus quiet Ilgwang beach with its fishing harbours and seafood shacks.
gijang-jukseong-ilgwang.why: Quiet, photogenic seaside-village feel, like the small coves near Kamakura and Hayama.
gijang-jukseong-ilgwang.autumn_note: Gijang is known for anchovies (spring) and for sea squirt and conger eel. October is pleasant and uncrowded.
gijang-jukseong-ilgwang.tips: Ilgwang station on the Donghae Line; Jukseong is easiest by taxi. Combine with Haedong Yonggungsa and Ananti Cove.

seunghaksan-silver-grass.name: Seunghaksan silver grass field
seunghaksan-silver-grass.summary: Large field of eulalia (silver grass) on the upper slopes of 496 m Seunghaksan, with views over the Nakdong River estuary and the sea.
seunghaksan-silver-grass.why: The autumn silver-grass experience, like Hakone's Sengokuhara, inside the city.
seunghaksan-silver-grass.autumn_note: Peaks mid-October to early November, so late October is ideal. Best in afternoon backlight.
seunghaksan-silver-grass.tips: Start from Dong-A University Seunghak campus (Hadan station area); taxi up to the campus shortens the climb.

daejeo-pink-muhly.name: Daejeo Ecological Park (pink muhly and cosmos)
daejeo-pink-muhly.summary: Riverside park with large pink muhly grass and cosmos fields in autumn.
daejeo-pink-muhly.why: Seasonal flower-field colour, but out of the way.
daejeo-pink-muhly.autumn_note: Pink muhly peaks late September to mid-October and is usually fading by Oct 20. Lower priority for this trip.
daejeo-pink-muhly.tips: Gangseo-gu Office station (Busan-Gimhae light rail). Only worth it if you are already near Gimhae Airport.

tongyeong-day-trip.name: Tongyeong: Hallyeosu cable car (Mireuksan), Dongpirang mural village, Jungang market
tongyeong-day-trip.name_ko: 통영 한려수도 조망 케이블카 / 동피랑 벽화마을 / 통영중앙시장
tongyeong-day-trip.summary: Harbour town known as 'Korea's Naples'. A 1,975 m cable car runs up Mireuksan (461 m) for island-studded views of the Hallyeo waterway; Dongpirang is a mural hillside above the harbour; Jungang market sells fish and oysters; there is also the Skyline Luge.
tongyeong-day-trip.why: The best Kamakura-plus-Izu combination on the trip: harbour, hills, island views and seafood. Worth an overnight.
tongyeong-day-trip.autumn_note: Fresh oyster season opens in October (peak Nov-Feb). Autumn haze is low, so island views are sharp.
tongyeong-day-trip.hours: Cable car roughly 09:30-17:00/18:00 in October (2024-25 pattern); maintenance closures happen several times a year
tongyeong-day-trip.closed: Some maintenance days, often a Monday; check ttdc.kr / cablecar notices
tongyeong-day-trip.cost_note: Cable car adult round trip about 15,500-17,000 KRW (2024-25 level; official site blocked, so unverified). Skyline Luge about 14,000-17,000 per ride (2024-25 level).
tongyeong-day-trip.booking: On site; arrive by 10:00 on weekends to avoid long waits
tongyeong-day-trip.tips: Intercity bus from Busan Seobu terminal (Sasang) about 1h40-2h. Try Chungmu gimbap and kkul-ppang (honey bread). Overnight at Stanford Hotel & Resort.

geoje-windy-hill-oedo.name: Geoje: Windy Hill and Oedo Botania
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.summary: Windy Hill is a grassy headland with a Dutch-style windmill over the sea. Oedo Botania is a private island garden reached by tourist ferries, with about 1.5 h on the island.
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.why: Seaside and garden scenery comparable to Izu's coast.
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.autumn_note: Mild weather; Oedo's gardens are less colourful in autumn than in spring.
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.cost_note: Ferry about 20,000-25,000 KRW round trip plus Oedo admission about 11,000 KRW (2024-25 level, unverified)
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.booking: Ferry companies at each port; foreigners can book by phone or on site. Bring a passport.
geoje-windy-hill-oedo.tips: Lower priority than Tongyeong if time is short. A car or taxi helps a lot here.

tongdosa.name: Tongdosa Temple (Yangsan)
tongdosa.summary: One of Korea's three 'Jewel' temples, founded in 646. It enshrines relics of the Buddha (so there is no Buddha statue in the main hall). UNESCO World Heritage site (Sansa).
tongdosa.why: Comparable to Kenchō-ji or Engaku-ji in Kamakura: an old, serene head temple with a forest approach.
tongdosa.autumn_note: The forest path (Muppungyosong) turns gold in late October to November.
tongdosa.cost_note: Cultural-property admission was abolished nationwide in May 2023, so entry is free (parking is paid)
tongdosa.tips: Intercity bus from Busan Nopo terminal (Line 1 terminus) to Tongdosa/Sinpyeong, about 25-30 min.

gyeongju-day-trip.name: Gyeongju (from Busan)
gyeongju-day-trip.summary: Former Silla capital, with royal tumuli (Daereungwon), Cheomseongdae, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at night, Hwangnidan-gil, Bulguksa and Seokguram.
gyeongju-day-trip.why: The Kyoto/Nara layer of the trip. May be covered in more depth by the Gyeongju researcher.
gyeongju-day-trip.autumn_note: Late October brings silver grass around the tumuli and pink muhly near Cheomseongdae; foliage at Bulguksa starts in late October.
gyeongju-day-trip.tips: Busan Station to Singyeongju by KTX about 30 min; or ITX/Mugunghwa on the Donghae line from Bujeon or Haeundae-area stations.

gyeongbokgung.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
gyeongbokgung.summary: Main Joseon palace with Geunjeongjeon throne hall, Gyeonghoeru pavilion and Hyangwonjeong.
gyeongbokgung.why: Anchor historic site. Hanbok rental makes entry free and is a fun group activity.
gyeongbokgung.autumn_note: Ginkgo and maple around Hyangwonjeong and behind the National Folk Museum turn late Oct.
gyeongbokgung.hours: Sep-Oct 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00). Royal guard changing at Gwanghwamun 10:00 and 14:00 (not Tue). Sumunjang patrol ceremony Saturdays 15:00 (Mar-Nov, not Jun-Aug).
gyeongbokgung.closed: TUESDAYS. Oct 2026 note: Geunjeongjeon courtyard/foundation access restricted Sep 2 - Oct 31 (works); Jibokjae small library open to Oct 31 (closed Mon-Tue).
gyeongbokgung.cost_note: Free in hanbok. Integrated palace pass KRW 10,000 (Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung + Huwon, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung, Jongmyo; valid 3 months).
gyeongbokgung.tips: Starlight Night Walk foreigner-only sessions Oct 21-24 (see events). Saenggwabang tea program through Oct 26.

changdeokgung-huwon.name: Changdeokgung Palace & Huwon (Secret Garden)
changdeokgung-huwon.summary: UNESCO palace with a wooded rear garden (Buyongji pond, Aeryeonji, Ongnyucheon).
changdeokgung-huwon.why: The Secret Garden in autumn is Seoul's closest thing to a Kyoto/Kamakura temple garden.
changdeokgung-huwon.autumn_note: Huwon foliage usually peaks late Oct - early Nov.
changdeokgung-huwon.cost_note: Palace KRW 3,000 + Huwon guided tour KRW 5,000 (or integrated pass KRW 10,000).
changdeokgung-huwon.booking: Huwon tours: online booking opens about 6 days ahead (sells out in autumn), plus limited on-site tickets. English tours run at set times daily.
changdeokgung-huwon.tips: Book Huwon the moment the window opens for the chosen date. Seongjeonggak 'crown prince' program Sundays (Korean, 10 pax).

changgyeonggung.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
changgyeonggung.summary: Quieter palace with Chundangji pond and a 1909 glass botanical house.
changgyeonggung.why: Evening palace option (open to 21:00) with the Mulbit Yeonhwa media-art show Oct 7 - Nov 1.
changgyeonggung.autumn_note: Chundangji pond maples are among the best palace foliage spots.
changgyeonggung.cost_note: A royal-palace notice indicates free admission on Wednesdays under 'Culture Day' in 2026 (unverified).
changgyeonggung.tips: Connected on foot to Changdeokgung and Jongmyo.

deoksugung.name: Deoksugung Palace (evening)
deoksugung.summary: Evening palace walk; open until 21:00. The 'Night at Seokjojeon' program ends Oct 18.
deoksugung.why: Fallback night palace; walk-up entry with no booking needed.
deoksugung.autumn_note: Stone-wall-road ginkgos turn in late Oct to early Nov.
deoksugung.cost_note: 1,000 KRW. Free every Wednesday since Aug 2026 (weekly Culture Day), so Wed Oct 21 is free. Also free in hanbok.
deoksugung.tips: On Wed Oct 21 you can do Deoksugung at dusk for free, then take a taxi to Changgyeonggung for a 19:30/20:00 Mulbit show (also free that day), or the other way round.

jongmyo.name: Jongmyo Shrine
jongmyo.summary: UNESCO royal ancestral shrine; Jeongjeon hall reopened in 2025 after a 5-year restoration.
jongmyo.why: Solemn, minimalist; a counterpoint to the palaces.
jongmyo.hours: Feb-May & Sep-Oct 09:00-18:00. Weekdays by guided tour only (English tours at set times); free-roaming on Saturdays and the last Wednesday of the month.
jongmyo.tips: Saturday Oct 24 allows free self-guided wandering.

national-museum-of-korea.name: National Museum of Korea
national-museum-of-korea.summary: Korea's flagship museum (Silla gold, Goryeo celadon, the 'Room of Quiet Contemplation' with two pensive Buddhas).
national-museum-of-korea.autumn_note: Mirror pond garden and outdoor stone pagoda garden.
national-museum-of-korea.closed: Open Mondays. Closed only Jan 1, Seollal, Chuseok, and the first Monday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec. No closure in the trip window.
national-museum-of-korea.cost_note: Permanent galleries free; special exhibitions paid.
national-museum-of-korea.tips: Very crowded on weekends since 2025; go Wed or Sat evening.
national-museum-of-korea.image_query: National Museum of Korea pensive bodhisattva room

leeum.name: Leeum Museum of Art
leeum.summary: Samsung's museum: Korean classical art plus contemporary.
leeum.why: Design-forward architecture (Botta, Nouvel, Koolhaas); pairs with Hannam/Itaewon.
leeum.autumn_note: Oct 2026 shows: Koo Jeong-A 'Usmose' (to Dec 27), 'Inside Other Spaces: Environments by Women Artists 1956-1976' (to Nov 29), Gabriel Orozco garden.
leeum.cost_note: Permanent collection by free timed reservation (in recent years); special exhibitions paid (about KRW 12,000-18,000). Verify.

haneul-park.name: Haneul Park (Sky Park)
haneul-park.summary: Hilltop silver-grass meadow over the Han River.
haneul-park.why: Peak-autumn Seoul nature without leaving the city; festival Oct 17-23.
haneul-park.tips: Go for sunset; weekday crowds are lighter.

bukchon-hanok-village.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
bukchon-hanok-village.summary: Lived-in hanok lanes between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung.
bukchon-hanok-village.hours: Red-zone lanes (Bukchon-ro 11-gil) open to tourists only 10:00-17:00
bukchon-hanok-village.closed: Tourist curfew 17:00-10:00 in the red zone since Mar 2025; fines about KRW 100,000.

gyeongju-night-heritage.name: Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond + Woljeonggyo
gyeongju-night-heritage.summary: Silla palace pond and a reconstructed covered bridge, both lit at night.
gyeongju-night-heritage.why: Gyeongju is the Kamakura/Nara analog; the night-lit pond is its showpiece.
gyeongju-night-heritage.autumn_note: Silla Culture Festival was Oct 9-11 (missed), but the lighting is nightly.
gyeongju-night-heritage.hours: Donggung & Wolji 09:00-22:00 (last entry 21:30); Woljeonggyo lit nightly
gyeongju-night-heritage.cost_note: Wolji KRW 3,000; Woljeonggyo free. Bulguksa/Seokguram admission free since May 2023 (national heritage fees abolished).
gyeongju-night-heritage.tips: Gyeongju National Museum open daily (closed Jan 1, Seollal, Chuseok), free.
gyeongju-night-heritage.image_query: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond night

seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.name: Seoraksan National Park - Sogongwon to Biseondae valley walk
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.summary: Mostly flat, wide valley path from Sogongwon (Sinheungsa, giant bronze Buddha) along the Cheonbuldong stream to Biseondae rock pools under granite spires. About 3 km one way, 1 h each way; extendable 1 km uphill to Geumganggul cave (steep stairs) or further up Cheonbuldong valley toward Yangpok shelter (3-4 h round trip).
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.why: The single best moderate foliage walk in Korea for the trip window: granite peaks, clear stream, red/yellow maples. Analog to Kamakura's temple-in-nature feel (Sinheungsa) but far more dramatic.
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.autumn_note: Valley (Sogongwon/Biseondae, ~200-400 m) color peaks ~Oct 20-27 in 2026; ridges Oct 15-20. KFS peak Oct 20, Weather i Oct 25. Prime time exactly during the trip.
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.hours: Park entrance usually open from ~05:00-06:00 to ~19:00 in autumn; trail entry cut-off times apply to upper trails (check KNPS).
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.cost_note: No park/temple entrance fee (cultural heritage admission fees abolished May 2023). Parking at Seorak-dong ~5,000-7,000 KRW per car per day (unverified for 2026).
seoraksan-sogongwon-biseondae.tips: Go on a weekday (Mon Oct 19-Thu Oct 22). Take Sokcho city bus 7 or 7-1 (20-40 min) from Sokcho terminal/downtown to the Seorak-dong terminus; arrive by 07:00-08:00 on peak days. Combine with the Gwongeumseong cable car (get the cable car ticket first, then walk to Biseondae while you wait).

seoraksan-ulsanbawi.name: Seoraksan - Ulsanbawi Rock hike (via Heundeulbawi rocking stone)
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.summary: Classic half-day climb from Sogongwon past Sinheungsa and Gyejoam hermitage/Heundeulbawi (rocking stone) to the 873 m granite massif. About 3.8 km one way; the last ~1 km is steep steel staircases (~800+ steps). Views to the East Sea and over Seorak's outer ridges.
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.why: Big payoff for moderately fit adults: sea-and-mountain panorama (a dramatic cousin to Kamakura's hill-to-sea views).
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.autumn_note: Lower forest colors ~Oct 18-27; the summit is rock so views of colored ridges are the draw.
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.hours: Trail entry cut-off typically early afternoon in autumn (KNPS posts seasonal entry limits; be on trail by ~12:00-13:00).
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.closed: Open daily except during weather warnings
seoraksan-ulsanbawi.tips: Start by 08:00. Stairs are narrow two-way; weekend queues on the stairs. Bring a windbreaker: summit wind is strong and temps can be 5-10 C colder than Sokcho.

seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.name: Seorak Cable Car to Gwongeumseong Fortress
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.summary: 5-minute cable car (10 min round trip) from Sogongwon to a rocky summit near Gwongeumseong fortress ruins, then ~15-20 min scramble on bare rock for 360-degree views of Seorak's spires.
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.why: Lowest-effort way to see Seorak's peaks in color; good for a mixed-energy group.
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.autumn_note: Views of the colored ridges are best Oct 15-25.
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.hours: Varies daily with weather and conditions; check the homepage on the day. Roughly 08:00/08:30 to ~17:00-18:00 in October (unverified).
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.cost_note: Adult round trip 16,000 KRW, child 12,000 KRW (official guide). One-way tickets not sold. Senior discount not available Sep 19-Nov 15, 2026.
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.booking: Same-day on-site ticket only; no online/advance booking. Ticket shows an assigned boarding time. Refund allowed until 10 min before departure (20% fee after).
seoraksan-gwongeumseong-cable-car.tips: Notorious queue problem: on autumn weekends boarding times printed on tickets can be 2-4 hours out or sell out by late morning. Buy tickets at opening, then walk to Biseondae while waiting. Weekday is strongly preferred. Live info: Tel 033-636-4300.

seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.name: Seoraksan Nam(South)-seorak: Heullimgol to Jujeongol valley traverse
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.summary: One-way traverse, mostly downhill after a steep first section: Heullimgol trailhead (on Route 44 below Hangyeryeong pass) - Yeosim falls - Deungseondae viewpoint - Sibi (Twelve) falls - Yongso falls junction - Jujeongol gorge - Osaek. About 6 km, 3.5-4.5 h. Jujeongol alone (Osaek to Yongso falls and back, ~3 km each way, nearly flat) is the easy option.
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.why: Considered the most colorful canyon in Seoraksan in autumn: red maples against narrow granite gorge and waterfalls. Ends at Osaek mineral springs village (onsen-town analog to Izu).
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.autumn_note: Jujeongol/Heullimgol typically peak in the last third of October; good fit for Oct 19-25, 2026.
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.time_needed: Half day (3.5-4.5 h traverse) or 2 h for Jujeongol round trip from Osaek
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.hours: Trail entry limited to morning/early afternoon (check KNPS).
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.closed: Heullimgol was closed ~2015-2024 after a rockfall; it reopened in 2024 and has operated with an advance reservation system in peak autumn. Status for Oct 2026 not verified.
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.cost_note: Free; taxi from Osaek back to Heullimgol trailhead ~10-15 min.
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.booking: Heullimgol section: verify on KNPS reservation site (reservation.knps.or.kr) whether 2026 autumn reservation applies (it did in recent seasons). Jujeongol from Osaek: no reservation.
seoraksan-heullimgol-jujeongol.tips: Intercity buses Seoul (Dong Seoul) - Osaek - Yangyang stop on Route 44; or taxi from Sokcho/Yangyang (~40 min). Very crowded on weekends with tour buses.

odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.name: Odaesan National Park - Woljeongsa fir forest path and Seonjae-gil
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.summary: Woljeongsa temple's 1 km fir-tree avenue (flat, 20-30 min) plus Seonjae-gil, a gentle streamside forest trail of ~9 km from Woljeongsa to Sangwonsa temple (~3-3.5 h one way, very small elevation gain). Can walk any portion and return by bus between Woljeongsa and Sangwonsa.
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.why: Gentle 'temple pilgrimage path' feel like Kamakura's temple walks, with a big Zen-style monastery and wooden bridges; zero technical difficulty.
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.autumn_note: Odaesan peak: Weather i Oct 16; other summaries Oct 17-20. The lower Seonjae-gil valley is typically a few days behind the summit, so Oct 17-21 should be at or just past peak; one of the safest bets for color on the trip.
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.hours: Daylight; Woljeongsa open early morning to evening.
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.cost_note: Temple admission abolished in May 2023; parking at Woljeongsa ~5,000-6,000 KRW (unverified).
odaesan-seonjae-gil-woljeongsa.tips: KTX Seoul/Cheongnyangni to Jinbu (Odaesan) station, then local bus to Woljeongsa/Sangwonsa (~25-40 min) or taxi. Woljeongsa parking fills by ~10:00 on autumn weekends; weekday visit preferred. Woljeongsa also runs a templestay.

chiaksan-guryongsa.name: Chiaksan National Park - Guryongsa valley
chiaksan-guryongsa.summary: Easy valley walk from the Guryong entrance to Guryongsa temple (~1 km) and on to Seryeom falls (~3 km one way, 1.5-2 h round trip). The summit Birobong is a hard climb, not recommended.
chiaksan-guryongsa.why: Accessible from Seoul (KTX to Wonju) but color will be early during the trip.
chiaksan-guryongsa.autumn_note: Weather i peak Oct 31; KWeather central peak Oct 19-Nov 1. Expect first color/partial only Oct 17-25.
chiaksan-guryongsa.tips: Lower priority than Odaesan/Seoraksan for this trip.

bukhansan-baegundae.name: Bukhansan National Park - Baegundae via Bukhansanseong
bukhansan-baegundae.summary: Seoul's signature granite summit (836 m). Popular route: Bukhansanseong Visitor Center - Daeseomun - Wonhyobong junction - Wiryeongmun - Baegundae, ~4.2 km one way, 2.5 h up, 2 h down. Final 300 m is bare rock with steel cables. Easier option: Ui-dong - Baegundae shelter route (shorter, steeper) or just the lower valley to Jungseongmun.
bukhansan-baegundae.why: Mountain hike inside a megacity; summit view over Seoul's sprawl (Shibuya-scale city seen from wild granite).
bukhansan-baegundae.autumn_note: 2026 Bukhansan forecasts vary: first color Oct 15-23, peak Oct 28-30 (secondary summaries) or Nov 4 (Weather i/KTO). Upper slopes partial color Oct 20-25; lower valleys still mostly green.
bukhansan-baegundae.hours: Trails open ~04:00-sunset; summit-bound entry cut-off about 2 h before sunset (KNPS rule).
bukhansan-baegundae.tips: Bus 704/34 from Gupabal station (Line 3) to Bukhansanseong entrance (~10 min). Weekend summit queues on the cable section can be 30-60 min; go on a weekday morning. Needs proper shoes.

seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.name: Seoul City Wall Trail - Baegaksan (Bugaksan) and Inwangsan sections
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.summary: Baegak section: Changuimun gate - Baegak summit (342 m) - Sukjeongmun - Malbawi - Waryong park / Hyehwamun, ~4.7 km, 2.5-3 h, many stairs. Inwang section: Changuimun / Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum - Inwangsan summit (338 m) - Sajik park, ~2.5 km, 1.5-2 h. Whole of Bugaksan has been open to the public since April 2022.
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.why: Walk a 600-year-old Joseon fortress wall above Gyeongbokgung and the Blue House with the whole city (incl. Namsan Tower) below; a 'city meets nature' half-day close to downtown.
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.autumn_note: Seoul-area foliage in 2026 runs late; expect early color (sumac, cherry leaves) Oct 20-25 with Seoul's main peak ~late Oct to early Nov. Inwangsan at sunset (17:43-17:53) is excellent regardless.
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.hours: Baegak section has seasonal entry hours (roughly 07:00-17:00 in Nov-Feb, longer Mar-Oct, check). Inwangsan open at all times.
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.closed: Baegak section: Mondays historically (verify; may have changed since full opening)
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.cost_note: Free; no ID or permit required since 2022.
seoul-baegak-inwang-fortress-wall.tips: Bus 7212/1020/7022 to Jahamun Pass (Changuimun). Combine Inwangsan sunset with Seochon dinner. Good on a weekend because it doesn't need traffic.

seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.name: Haneul Park (World Cup Park) silver grass fields - Seoul Eulalia Festival
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.summary: Former landfill turned ~200,000 m2 hilltop grassland of silver grass (억새) above the Han River. The 25th Seoul Eulalia Festival 2026 runs Oct 17-23 with evening lighting, photo zones, busking and a recycled-crafts market.
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.why: Iconic Seoul autumn scene; festival dates line up exactly with the trip; night opening means it can be combined with a day elsewhere.
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.autumn_note: Silver grass at peak silver plumes mid-to-late October; best light 1 h before sunset (~16:45-17:50).
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.hours: Festival Oct 17-23, 2026: 10:00-21:00 (extended night opening). Outside festival, Haneul Park closes around sunset.
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.cost_note: Free. 'Maengkkongi' electric cart from Nanji-cheon Park parking lot up the hill (small fare, ~2,000-3,000 KRW; not confirmed for 2026), or climb the 291-step Haneul staircase (~15 min).
seoul-haneul-park-eulalia.tips: Subway Line 6 World Cup Stadium Station (exit 1), ~20 min walk to the stairs (official says ~40 min to the fields). Avoid weekend afternoons (Oct 17-18); weekday evening is best. Contact 02-300-5574.

seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.name: Seoul city foliage: Changdeokgung Huwon, Deoksugung stone-wall road, Namsan, Seoul Forest
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.name_ko: 창덕궁 후원 · 덕수궁 돌담길 · 남산 · 서울숲
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.summary: Seoul's classic urban autumn walks: the Secret Garden (Huwon) of Changdeokgung (guided tour), the Deoksugung stone-wall road (ginkgo and zelkova lined), Namsan's north-side walking path and Namsan Tower, and Seoul Forest's ginkgo and deer park.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.why: Palace-and-garden foliage closest to the Kamakura temple-garden feel within Seoul.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.autumn_note: These peak late: Seoul maples typically late Oct-early Nov and ginkgo ~early-mid Nov; KFS national ginkgo average Oct 30 and Bukhansan peak Nov 4 (Weather i) imply Seoul city is mostly green-to-early-color on Oct 17-25. Huwon maples are usually the earliest in central Seoul (late Oct).
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.time_needed: Huwon tour 90 min; each walk 1-2 h
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.hours: Changdeokgung 09:00-18:00 (Feb-May, Sep-Oct; last entry 17:00); Huwon tours by time slot.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.closed: Changdeokgung closed Mondays; Deoksugung closed Mondays; Gyeongbokgung closed Tuesdays.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.cost_note: Changdeokgung 3,000 KRW + Huwon 5,000 KRW (verify 2026). Deoksugung 1,000 KRW; Namsan, Seoul Forest free.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.booking: Huwon: online booking opens about 6 days ahead on the Changdeokgung site; foreigners can book; some same-day tickets on site.
seoul-palaces-deoksugung-namsan.tips: Treat Seoul foliage as a bonus; prioritize Gangwon for color.

nami-island.name: Nami Island
nami-island.summary: Half-moon river island reached by ferry or zipline, famous for tree-lined avenues (Songpa ginkgo road, metasequoia lane, red maples).
nami-island.why: Very popular, photogenic tree avenues; easy to pair with the Garden of Morning Calm on a Gapyeong day.
nami-island.autumn_note: Typical peak window Oct 20-Nov 5; in a late 2026 season the ginkgo road is likely best ~Oct 28-Nov 5, so on Oct 23-25 expect mixed green/yellow with red maples starting.
nami-island.cost_note: Admission incl. round-trip ferry ~16,000 KRW adult (2025 price; 2026 not verified). Zipline ~50,000 KRW.
nami-island.booking: Walk-up ferry ticket at Gapyeong wharf; zipline book ahead.
nami-island.tips: Arrive before 09:30 or after 15:00 to avoid tour-bus crowds; weekends extremely busy. ITX-Cheongchun Yongsan/Cheongnyangni to Gapyeong, then taxi (~5 min) or Gapyeong tour bus.

garden-of-morning-calm.name: The Garden of Morning Calm
garden-of-morning-calm.summary: Large private garden in a mountain bowl with Korean-style gardens, a bonsai garden, chrysanthemum displays, and a maple-lined valley.
garden-of-morning-calm.why: Most 'Japanese garden'-like foliage experience near Seoul; elevation (~400-650 m) means it colors earlier than Seoul.
garden-of-morning-calm.autumn_note: Usually best mid-to-late October, a week or so ahead of Nami Island; good fit Oct 18-25, 2026. Autumn chrysanthemum exhibition typically runs through October.
garden-of-morning-calm.cost_note: Adult ~11,000-12,000 KRW (2025 level; official site did not load, 2026 unverified).
garden-of-morning-calm.booking: Walk-up; online discount tickets on Korean platforms.
garden-of-morning-calm.tips: Gapyeong tour bus or taxi from Cheongpyeong/Gapyeong station (~25-30 min). Winter light festival starts in December, not relevant.

hwadam-botanic-garden.name: Hwadam Botanic Garden (Hwadamsup)
hwadam-botanic-garden.summary: LG-funded forest garden on a hillside with 400+ maple varieties on a gently sloping deck path (~5 km loop) plus a monorail.
hwadam-botanic-garden.why: The most refined maple-garden experience in Korea, close to a Kyoto-style momiji garden.
hwadam-botanic-garden.autumn_note: 2026 autumn peak season runs Oct 23-Nov 15; maple peak usually late Oct-early Nov. Only Oct 23-25 of the trip falls inside the season.
hwadam-botanic-garden.hours: Oct 23-Nov 1: 08:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00); Nov 2-15: 08:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00). No closing days during peak season.
hwadam-botanic-garden.closed: Normally Mondays, but no closure days during the Oct 23-Nov 15 peak season
hwadam-botanic-garden.cost_note: Adult 11,000 KRW; monorail extra: station 1-2 5,000, 1-3 7,000, full loop 9,000 KRW.
hwadam-botanic-garden.booking: 100% advance online booking by time slot (no on-site sales) on NOL (Yanolja/Interpark platform); booking opened Sep 16, 2026 13:00. Free cancel until 23:59 the day before; 30% fee same day. Weekend slots and monorail sell out; foreign-card/foreigner booking may require Interpark Global/NOL global - verify.
hwadam-botanic-garden.tips: Konjiam station (Gyeonggang line) then resort shuttle/taxi (~10 min). Book a weekday slot (Fri Oct 23) and the monorail at the same time.

mingdongsan-silver-grass.name: Mingdongsan silver grass ridge
mingdongsan-silver-grass.summary: Bald 1,119 m summit covered by ~660,000 m2 (200,000 pyeong) of silver grass. Main route from Jeungsan Elementary School (near Mingdongsan station) ~1.5 h up via the shelter; allow 3-4 h total.
mingdongsan-silver-grass.why: Vast rolling silver-grass ridge with mountain views; the most dramatic eulalia hike in Korea.
mingdongsan-silver-grass.autumn_note: Festival Sep 18-Nov 8, 2026; silver grass fullest mid-to-late October, so on peak for the trip.
mingdongsan-silver-grass.time_needed: 3-4 h hike, plus long travel (~3 h each way from Seoul)
mingdongsan-silver-grass.tips: Vehicle access to the Balgudeok area is fully closed during the festival and the linked shuttle stopped; park at Mingdongsan sports complex or Neungjeon lot. Remote: only worth it if routing through Jeongseon/Gangwon.

yeongnam-alps-ganwoljae.name: Yeongnam Alps - Ganwoljae and Sinbulsan silver grass plains
yeongnam-alps-ganwoljae.summary: Silver grass saddle at ~900 m between Ganwolsan and Sinbulsan. Easiest approach: Baenaegol / Ganwoljae forest road (~5.5 km gentle road walk, 2 h up) or steeper Ganwol valley trail from Deungeok (~2.5-3 h up). Sinbulsan plateau above has 1.98 km2 of grass.
yeongnam-alps-ganwoljae.why: Huge golden grass ridges; good if the itinerary includes Gyeongju/Busan/Ulsan.
yeongnam-alps-ganwoljae.autumn_note: Silver grass peaks early to late October; on peak during trip. Ulju Odyssey concert held Oct 3, 2026 (past).
yeongnam-alps-ganwoljae.tips: Bus from Ulsan/Eonyang to Deungeok/Yeongnam Alps Complex Welcome Center; taxi easier. Weekend crowds and parking full by 09:00.

hwangmaesan-silver-grass.name: Hwangmaesan silver grass
hwangmaesan-silver-grass.summary: High plateau (~800-900 m) reached by car; short walks through silver grass with views. Known for spring azaleas and autumn silver grass.
hwangmaesan-silver-grass.why: Silver grass with minimal hiking, but very remote from Seoul.
hwangmaesan-silver-grass.autumn_note: Typically peaks early-to-late October (2026 festival dates not verified).
hwangmaesan-silver-grass.tips: Car required. Low priority for this route.

jeju-saebyeol-oreum.name: Saebyeol Oreum
jeju-saebyeol-oreum.summary: 519 m volcanic cone covered in silver grass; steep 30-40 min climb to the top and loop down. Sunset views to the sea.
jeju-saebyeol-oreum.why: Jeju's signature autumn silver-grass landscape; volcanic scenery akin to Izu's coastal hills.
jeju-saebyeol-oreum.autumn_note: Silver grass peaks mid-October to mid-November; on peak during trip (2026 not specifically confirmed).
jeju-saebyeol-oreum.tips: Windy; go near sunset (~17:50-18:00 Jeju). Car or taxi needed.

hallasan-yeongsil.name: Hallasan - Yeongsil trail to Witse Oreum
hallasan-yeongsil.summary: Most scenic non-summit Hallasan trail: ~5.8 km one way (from Yeongsil parking; 3.7 km from the upper trailhead) past Byeongpungbawi cliffs to Witse Oreum shelter, ~2.5 h up. No reservation needed (only Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa summit routes require one).
hallasan-yeongsil.why: Volcano walk with alpine shrubs and sea views.
hallasan-yeongsil.autumn_note: KFS Hallasan peak Nov 6 (1100 m point Nov 6), Weather i Nov 13. Upper-elevation shrubs (~1,400-1,700 m) can color by late October; lower forests still green.
hallasan-yeongsil.tips: Only if the itinerary includes Jeju.

naejangsan.name: Naejangsan National Park
naejangsan.summary: Korea's most famous maple tunnel to Naejangsa temple.
naejangsan.why: Famous, but timing is wrong for this trip.
naejangsan.autumn_note: Peak Nov 4 (KFS) / Nov 11 (Weather i); first color ~Oct 20-27. Not worth it Oct 17-25.

jirisan-piagol.name: Jirisan National Park - Piagol valley
jirisan-piagol.summary: Valley famous for red maples; Jikjeon village to Piagol shelter ~4 km one way, ~2 h up. Alternatively drive to Seongsamjae/Nogodan (1,507 m) for ridge views (Nogodan summit by reservation).
jirisan-piagol.why: Classic Jirisan red valley, but remote and timing marginal.
jirisan-piagol.autumn_note: KFS Jirisan peak Oct 27; Weather i first Oct 28, peak Nov 5. Upper Piagol could show good color Oct 24-25; lower valley later.

juwangsan-jusanji.name: Juwangsan National Park - Daejeonsa to Yongchu Falls, and Jusanji pond
juwangsan-jusanji.summary: Easy flat gorge walk from Daejeonsa temple to Yongchu waterfall (~2 km, 40 min each way) between sheer cliffs; Jusanji is a nearby pond with 150-year-old willows standing in water (misty at dawn).
juwangsan-jusanji.why: Cinematic gorge and pond scenery; feasible from Gyeongju/Andong by car (~1.5 h).
juwangsan-jusanji.autumn_note: KFS Juwangsan peak Oct 26; expect strong color at Jusanji and the gorge Oct 22-25.
juwangsan-jusanji.tips: Car needed realistically. Very crowded on weekends; Cheongsong is also known for apples (harvest season).

gayasan-haeinsa.name: Gayasan National Park - Haeinsa and Sorigil
gayasan-haeinsa.summary: Haeinsa temple (UNESCO Tripitaka Koreana) and the 6 km Sorigil valley path to it (~2 h one way, gentle).
gayasan-haeinsa.why: Great temple + valley walk, but color will be early.
gayasan-haeinsa.autumn_note: Weather i first Oct 22, peak Nov 5 (9 days late). Mostly pre-peak during trip.

palgongsan-donghwasa.name: Palgongsan - Donghwasa and the Palgongsan ring road
palgongsan-donghwasa.summary: Daegu's big mountain (national park since 2023); maple-lined loop road, Donghwasa temple, cable car to Sinmubong.
palgongsan-donghwasa.why: Accessible from Daegu, but late this year.
palgongsan-donghwasa.autumn_note: KFS peak Oct 30; Weather i first Oct 26 (9 days late), peak Nov 12 (15 days late). Pre-peak during trip.

gyeongju-autumn-spots.name: Gyeongju autumn: Bulguksa maples, Tongiljeon ginkgo road, Gyerim forest, Cheomseongdae fields
gyeongju-autumn-spots.name_ko: 경주 불국사 · 통일전 은행나무길 · 계림 · 첨성대 핑크뮬리
gyeongju-autumn-spots.summary: Bulguksa's maple-framed stone bridges; the ginkgo avenue to Tongiljeon (lat 35.804, lon 129.253 approx.); Gyerim's ancient zelkova grove; Cheomseongdae observatory surrounded by pink muhly, silver grass and cosmos fields (35.8347, 129.2190).
gyeongju-autumn-spots.why: Kamakura analog city (ancient capital, temples, walkable heritage). Great regardless of peak color.
gyeongju-autumn-spots.autumn_note: Gyeongju maples/ginkgo usually peak ~Nov 1-10 (Tongiljeon ginkgo early Nov); expect early yellowing only Oct 17-25. Cheomseongdae pink muhly was forecast to fully bloom in early October and stays viewable 'for about a month', so by Oct 17-25 it is late-season (fading). Gyerim zelkovas turn ~late Oct-early Nov.
gyeongju-autumn-spots.hours: Bulguksa ~07:00-18:00 (Mar-Oct); Cheomseongdae/Gyerim area open always (night lighting).
gyeongju-autumn-spots.tips: Shift expectations to heritage + early color; the Bomun lake cherry trees turn red earlier (late Oct).

unmunsa-ginkgo.name: Unmunsa temple 450-year-old ginkgo
unmunsa-ginkgo.summary: Bhikkhuni (nuns') monastery with a huge ginkgo inside the closed sangha college; opened to the public only ~2 days a year when golden. Also an ancient drooping pine and a pine-lined approach.
unmunsa-ginkgo.why: Special-access temple moment; but dates fall after the trip.
unmunsa-ginkgo.autumn_note: 2025 opening was Nov 8-9 (13:00-16:00). 2026 dates not announced as of Oct 6; almost certainly early-mid November, i.e. after the trip. Temple itself is still visitable.
unmunsa-ginkgo.closed: Ginkgo courtyard closed except the 2 opening days
unmunsa-ginkgo.tips: Skip for ginkgo; only worth it as a quiet temple stop.

yangju-nari-park.name: Yangju Nari Park (globe amaranth + pink muhly)
yangju-nari-park.summary: ~66,000 m2 flower farm with 10 million globe amaranth, pink muhly and 20+ autumn flowers.
yangju-nari-park.why: Pink-field photo stop near Seoul, but late in its season during the trip.
yangju-nari-park.autumn_note: Park open Sep 18-Oct 25, 2026; festival weekends Sep 26-28 and Oct 3-4; flowers peak Sep 25-Oct 10. By Oct 17-25 it is fading, last days before closing.
yangju-nari-park.closed: Closes for the season after Oct 25, 2026
yangju-nari-park.cost_note: ~5,000 KRW, refunded as local voucher (per 2025-2026 reports; verify).

busan-daejeo-eco-park.name: Daejeo Ecological Park (pink muhly, pampas)
busan-daejeo-eco-park.summary: Huge riverside park with pink muhly beside parking lot 2, pampas grass and silver grass along a bamboo path.
busan-daejeo-eco-park.why: Free, easy; pampas/silver grass still good in late Oct even when muhly fades.
busan-daejeo-eco-park.autumn_note: Pink muhly Sep-early/mid Oct; past peak by Oct 17-25. Pampas and silver grass fine.
busan-daejeo-eco-park.tips: Busan Gimhae Light Rail Daejeo station nearby. Low priority.

seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.name: Seoraksan National Park – Seorak-dong (Sogongwon) entrance & Sinheungsa Temple
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.summary: This is the main eastern gateway to Seoraksan. A flat 1 km walk passes the 14.6 m bronze Unification Buddha (통일대불) and reaches Sinheungsa, the head temple of the Jogye Order's 3rd parish. Every classic low-level hike starts here: Ulsanbawi, Biseondae, Gwongeumseong cable car, and Yukdam/Biryong falls.
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.why: This is Korea's answer to a Kamakura temple set against mountains, with a giant outdoor Buddha. The difference is the granite peaks that rise right behind it.
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.autumn_note: The 2026 forecast puts first foliage at Seoraksan on Oct 3 and the peak at about Oct 16-25. Low valleys around Sogongwon usually peak in the last week of October, which is exactly when these travelers arrive.
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.time_needed: 1-1.5 h for the temple and Buddha; a full day with hikes
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.hours: The park is open all day. Trail entry has time limits: for ridge trails the gates generally close in the early afternoon, and you must be off the trail by sunset.
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.closed: Open in October. High-altitude trails such as Gongnyong ridge and routes up to Daecheongbong close for wildfire season from about Nov 15 to Dec 15 (2025 pattern), so they are unaffected in October. The Sogongwon-area trails (Biseondae, Ulsanbawi, Gwongeumseong) stay open even during that closure.
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.cost_note: Park entry is free, and the Sinheungsa cultural-heritage fee was abolished in May 2023. Sogongwon parking costs 6,000 KRW/day for a car (2026 source).
seoraksan-sogongwon-sinheungsa.tips: Sokcho runs a special foliage traffic plan from Oct 3 to Nov 8, 2026. Cars are held back in stages, overflow goes to free parking lots B and C, and free shuttles run from there. Arrive before 07:00 on weekends, or take city bus 7/7-1. Avoid Sat Oct 17, Sun Oct 18 and Sat Oct 24 if you can, or go at dawn.

gwongeumseong-cable-car.name: Seorak Cable Car to Gwongeumseong Fortress
gwongeumseong-cable-car.summary: A 5-minute gondola ride climbs to about 700 m. From the top it is a 10-15 minute rocky scramble to the Gwongeumseong fortress ruins, which look out over Ulsanbawi, the Seorak peaks and the East Sea.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.why: This is the easiest way to get a big Seorak view without a long hike.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.autumn_note: This is peak demand season. On October weekends the wait after buying a ticket can be 1-2+ hours, because your ticket carries an assigned boarding time.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.hours: Hours change with season and weather and are posted daily at the top of sorakcablecar.co.kr. Typical October hours are about 08:30-17:30, with ticket sales stopping earlier (not confirmed). If you take the last car up, you only get about 20 minutes at the top.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.closed: Runs daily but stops in strong wind.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.cost_note: 2026 round-trip fares: adult 16,000, child 12,000. Seniors pay 14,000 except during peak periods (Jul 18-Aug 23 and Sep 19-Nov 15). Only round-trip tickets are sold.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.booking: Tickets are sold on-site only, for the same day; there is no advance booking. Buy them first thing, then hike Biseondae or visit Sinheungsa while you wait for your boarding time.
gwongeumseong-cable-car.tips: Get there before about 08:30, or buy tickets on arrival and do Biseondae while you wait. Cabins have no heating, and the top is windy and cold in late October. The real-time wait shows on Sokcho's electronic signboards.

ulsanbawi.name: Ulsanbawi Rock hike
ulsanbawi.summary: This is a 3.8 km one-way hike from Sogongwon past Heundeulbawi (the rocking stone) and Gyejoam hermitage. It finishes with about 800+ steel stairs up the 873 m granite massif, which has a 360° view of Seorak and Sokcho down to the sea.
ulsanbawi.why: This is the signature Seorak summit view and a satisfying half-day hike for fit adults.
ulsanbawi.autumn_note: Foliage is best on the approach (about Oct 15-25). Above the stairs it is mostly bare granite.
ulsanbawi.hours: Trail entry closes in the early afternoon in autumn (check the gate sign). Start by about 09:00.
ulsanbawi.tips: The stairs are steep and exposed and get very windy. Bring gloves and a layer.

biseondae-geumganggul.name: Biseondae Rock & Geumganggul Cave
biseondae-geumganggul.summary: A gentle 3 km valley walk from Sogongwon leads to Biseondae, where broad granite slabs sit in a clear stream under the Jangguseong cliffs. A steep extra 0.6 km climbs to Geumganggul, a cliffside cave hermitage.
biseondae-geumganggul.why: This is the best 'easy and gorgeous' foliage walk in Seorak. It feels like a mountain version of a temple-town stroll.
biseondae-geumganggul.autumn_note: The valley peak usually falls in the last 10 days of October. It is crowded on weekends.
biseondae-geumganggul.time_needed: 2-2.5 h round trip; +1 h for Geumganggul
biseondae-geumganggul.tips: It pairs well with the cable car: buy cable car tickets first, then walk Biseondae while you wait.

heullimgol-juongol-osaek.name: Heullimgol → Yongso Falls → Juongol valley (Osaek / Nam-Seorak)
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.summary: This is a classic downhill foliage gorge walk. You start at the Heullimgol trailhead on Route 44 below Hangyeryeong pass, go over Deungseondae, past Yongso Falls, and down the Juongol gorge to Osaek hot-spring village (about 6 km, 3-4 h). A shorter option is Osaek to Yongso Falls and back on the flat Juongol trail (about 3 km each way, 2-2.5 h).
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.why: This is the most spectacular red-maple gorge on the east coast. The finish at Osaek mineral spring and hot springs echoes an Izu onsen-valley walk.
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.autumn_note: Juongol is one of Korea's most famous foliage spots, peaking about Oct 18-28. Route 44 and Osaek are badly jammed on October weekends.
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.time_needed: 3-4 h one way (Heullimgol), 2-2.5 h (Juongol out and back)
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.hours: Heullimgol works on reservations with timed entry. Juongol from Osaek is open during the day without a reservation.
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.closed: The spring (about Mar 2 to May 15) and autumn (about Nov 15 to Dec 15) wildfire closures do not apply in late October.
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.booking: Heullimgol needs advance reservation in the KNPS system (reservation.knps.or.kr), capped at 5,000 people a day with time slots. Foreigners can usually book through the English KNPS reservation site. Juongol from Osaek needs no reservation.
heullimgol-juongol-osaek.tips: Heullimgol has had rockfall closures before (closed 2015-2022, reopened Sep 6, 2022). Check KNPS notices. Without a car, take an intercity bus toward Hangyeryeong or Osaek from Yangyang or Sokcho, or use a taxi.

naksansa.name: Naksansa Temple (Uisangdae pavilion, Hongnyeonam hermitage)
naksansa.summary: This seaside temple was founded in 671 by the monk Uisang. It has a 16 m white Haesu Gwaneum statue facing the sea, the Uisangdae pavilion on a pine-clad cliff (Scenic Site), and the Hongnyeonam hermitage built over a sea cave, with a floor hole through which you can see waves. It was rebuilt after the 2005 forest fire.
naksansa.why: This is the closest Korean match to Kamakura's seaside temples and Hase-dera's sea views. It is the top pick for these travelers. Uisangdae at sunrise is iconic.
naksansa.autumn_note: Mild late-October weather and clear sea air. Sunrise is about 06:40.
naksansa.hours: Roughly 06:00-18:00 (open from about 04:00 for sunrise worshippers); not confirmed for 2026.
naksansa.cost_note: Admission has been free since the May 2023 abolition of the heritage fee. Parking is about 4,000 KRW.
naksansa.booking: None. Naksansa also runs a templestay program.
naksansa.tips: Combine with Naksan beach and Yangyang. Bus 9 or 9-1 from Sokcho takes about 30 min.

hyuhyuam.name: Hyuhyuam seaside temple (likely the 'Hyujeonsa' in the brief)
hyuhyuam.summary: A small modern temple on flat sea rocks, with a natural 'reclining Buddha' rock formation, a big Jibong Gwaneum statue, and fish-feeding from the rocks.
hyuhyuam.why: A rocky-coast temple stop that could be in Kamakura or Enoshima, and easy to combine with Jukdo and Surfyy beaches.
hyuhyuam.tips: It is 10 minutes by car from Jukdo and Ingu beaches. Bus service is sparse, so a taxi from Hajodae, Ingu or Jumunjin works better.

hajodae.name: Hajodae pavilion & lighthouse
hajodae.summary: A hexagonal Joseon-era pavilion and a white lighthouse on pine-covered sea cliffs, with a lone pine growing out of a rock.
hajodae.why: A quiet 30-minute coastal stop with a Kamakura or Enoshima cliff feel.
hajodae.tips: Pair it with Hyuhyuam and Jukdo.

jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.name: Jukdo Beach & Surfyy Beach – Yangyang surf coast
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.summary: Korea's surf capital. Jukdo and Ingu have surf shops, cafés, bars and a laid-back 'Korean Shonan' vibe. Surfyy Beach (Hajodae) is a private surf beach with a beach-bar look.
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.why: This is the Shonan or Enoshima side of Kamakura: young, beachy and full of good cafés. Lessons are a fun active day.
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.autumn_note: Late October water is about 17-19 °C, so a full wetsuit is supplied. Autumn swells are good. Beach-bar activity winds down after September.
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.hours: Surf shops run lessons at about 10:00 and 14:00. Surfyy operating hours shrink in the off-season.
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.closed: Some Surfyy facilities cut back after mid-October (not confirmed for 2026).
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.cost_note: A 2-hour group surf lesson with board and wetsuit typically costs 50,000-70,000 KRW (2024-25 pricing, not confirmed for 2026).
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.booking: Book through Naver booking, Instagram or KakaoTalk with the shops. Some shops have English-speaking instructors.
jukdo-surfyy-yangyang.tips: Bus 9-1 runs along the coast, but a taxi is easier. Yangyang Station (on the Donghae line? No: there is no rail; see transport) is not a rail station. Reach it by bus from Sokcho or Gangneung, or from Seoul's Yangyang buses.

abai-village-gaetbae.name: Abai Village & Gaetbae hand-pulled ferry
abai-village-gaetbae.summary: A sandbar village founded by North Korean refugees from Hamgyeong Province during the Korean War. You cross the harbor channel on the Gaetbae, a barge that passengers pull along a cable themselves. It is known for Abai sundae (stuffed squid and sausage) and Hamheung naengmyeon.
abai-village-gaetbae.why: This is the 'little charming quirk' moment, like the Enoden: a tiny human-powered ferry ride, plus refugee history and fishing-port food.
abai-village-gaetbae.cost_note: The Gaetbae fare has historically been 500 KRW per crossing in cash (could be 1,000 by 2026; not verified).
abai-village-gaetbae.tips: Walk on to Jungang market (10 min) and the Seorak Bridge.

sokcho-jungang-market.name: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market (Jungang Market)
sokcho-jungang-market.summary: A big covered market famous for dakgangjeong (sweet-spicy fried chicken boxes, such as Manseok), squid sundae, hotteok, and a basement live-seafood floor where you choose fish and get sashimi cut to order.
sokcho-jungang-market.why: This is the energy of Tsukiji's outer market, Korean style. It is the best cheap food stop in Sokcho.
sokcho-jungang-market.autumn_note: Autumn means red snow crab (홍게), saury and fat flatfish.
sokcho-jungang-market.hours: About 08:00-21:00 (stalls vary). The basement fish floor is open late.
sokcho-jungang-market.closed: Some stalls close on the 1st and 3rd Monday.
sokcho-jungang-market.tips: Buy dakgangjeong to eat later; the boxes travel well. Lines at Manseok move fast.

sokcho-eye-beach.name: Sokcho Beach & Sokcho Eye Ferris wheel
sokcho-eye-beach.summary: A 65 m beachfront Ferris wheel lit in neon at night, overlooking Sokcho beach, the harbor and the Seorak range.
sokcho-eye-beach.why: A small dose of the neon-city mood, by the sea.
sokcho-eye-beach.autumn_note: Clear October evenings are good for views of Seorak at sunset.
sokcho-eye-beach.cost_note: About 15,000 KRW adult for a standard cabin (2024-25 figure, not verified for 2026). The official site refused fetches.

yeonggeumjeong-lighthouse.name: Yeonggeumjeong pavilion & Sokcho Lighthouse Observatory
yeonggeumjeong-lighthouse.summary: A pavilion on a bridge over sea rocks, the classic Sokcho sunrise spot, next to a lighthouse with a free observatory deck that looks at Seorak and the coast. Dongmyeong port's red-crab restaurants are next door.
yeonggeumjeong-lighthouse.hours: The pavilion is always open. The lighthouse observatory is open about 06:00-18:00.
yeonggeumjeong-lighthouse.tips: Go at sunrise if you stay in Sokcho.

daepohang.name: Daepo Port
daepohang.summary: A fishing harbor with a raw-fish center and stalls of fried shrimp and squid. It is next to Oeongchi seaside trail and Lotte Resort Sokcho.
daepohang.why: A casual seafood-port grazing stop, and a contrast to omakase.
daepohang.tips: The Oeongchi Bada Hyanggi-ro trail (about 1.7 km) links Daepo to Sokcho beach along the rocks. It is a great short walk.

cheongchoho.name: Cheongchoho Lake park & Expo Tower
cheongchoho.summary: A lagoon in central Sokcho with a lakeside promenade and the Expo Tower viewpoint, which looks across to Seorak.
cheongchoho.why: An easy evening walk and a city-plus-mountain view.

anmok-coffee-street.name: Anmok Beach Coffee Street
anmok-coffee-street.summary: A beachfront row of multi-storey cafés with sea-view rooftops. Gangneung is Korea's 'coffee city' (Terarosa, Bohemian Bak Yi-chu, and others).
anmok-coffee-street.why: It is like a Shonan seaside café strip. It's a relaxed coastal stroll.
anmok-coffee-street.autumn_note: The Gangneung Coffee Festival is historically held in October (2026 dates not verified).
anmok-coffee-street.tips: It is 15 minutes by taxi from Gangneung Station (about 10,000-12,000 KRW).

gyeongpo.name: Gyeongpo Lake, Gyeongpodae & Gyeongpo Beach
gyeongpo.summary: A lagoon with a 4.3 km cycling and walking loop, the Joseon-era Gyeongpodae pavilion (a National Treasure since 2019) on a hill, and Gyeongpo beach backed by pines. You can rent bikes around the lake.
gyeongpo.why: A gentle lakeside-plus-sea day, with Ojukheon and Seongyojang nearby.
gyeongpo.autumn_note: The cherry trees around the lake turn color in late October, and reeds and silver grass line the shore.
gyeongpo.hours: Always open. Gyeongpodae pavilion is open about 09:00-18:00.
gyeongpo.cost_note: Free. Bike rental is about 5,000-10,000 KRW per hour, or more for tandems.
gyeongpo.tips: Chodang tofu village is 1 km south.

ojukheon.name: Ojukheon (birthplace of Yulgok and Shin Saimdang)
ojukheon.summary: A late-15th-century scholar-gentry house surrounded by black bamboo. It is one of Korea's oldest residential buildings (Treasure) and appears on the 5,000 and 50,000 won notes. The site includes the Gangneung city museum.
ojukheon.why: Quiet Joseon heritage with gardens, like Kamakura's old residences.
ojukheon.autumn_note: Persimmons and ginkgo turn color in late October.
ojukheon.closed: Believed to be open year-round (some sources list Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok closures).
ojukheon.tips: Combine with Seongyojang (1 km) and Gyeongpo.

seongyojang.name: Seongyojang House
seongyojang.summary: A 300-year-old aristocratic estate with 102 kan of buildings, the Hwallaejeong lotus-pond pavilion, and pine woods. It also offers hanok stays.
seongyojang.why: This is the most ryokan-like traditional lodging option on this coast (see lodging).
seongyojang.autumn_note: The pine-and-maple backdrop and the pond pavilion are lovely in autumn.

chodang-tofu-village.name: Chodang Sundubu (soft tofu) Village
chodang-tofu-village.summary: A cluster of restaurants making tofu with seawater brine (a 400-year tradition). Famous for jjamppong-sundubu (Donghwa Gaden) and plain white sundubu (Chodang Halmeoni).
chodang-tofu-village.why: This is the Gangneung signature meal, much as yudofu is in Kamakura and Kyoto.
chodang-tofu-village.cost_note: Meals are 11,000-16,000 KRW. Tofu-gelato cafés are nearby.
chodang-tofu-village.booking: None. Donghwa Gaden uses a queue tablet.
chodang-tofu-village.tips: Go before 11:00 to avoid the queues.

jumunjin-bts-bus-stop.name: Jumunjin Port fish market & BTS bus stop (Hyangho Beach)
jumunjin-bts-bus-stop.summary: A lively fishing port with a fish market, and nearby the bus-stop set from BTS's 'You Never Walk Alone' album at Hyangho beach (about 37.9218, 128.7980). The Goblin (Dokkaebi) drama breakwater is close too.
jumunjin-bts-bus-stop.why: A fun pop-culture photo stop, plus a seafood market.
jumunjin-bts-bus-stop.cost_note: The bus stop is free (there may be a small photo-zone fee).
jumunjin-bts-bus-stop.tips: It is on the way between Gangneung and Yangyang/Sokcho. Bus 300 or the intercity bus stops at Jumunjin.

jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.name: Jeongdongjin & Jeongdong Simgok Badabuchae-gil coastal trail
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.summary: Jeongdongjin station sits right on the beach and is famous as one of the closest stations to the sea in the world. The 2.9 km Badabuchae-gil boardwalk runs along the 23-million-year-old coastal terrace cliffs between Jeongdongjin and Simgok. There is also the Sun Cruise ship-shaped hotel on the cliff.
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.why: This is the 'little coastal train' moment, like the Enoden. The KTX and local trains stop right on the beach.
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.hours: The Badabuchae-gil boardwalk is typically open about 09:00-17:30 in October.
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.closed: It closes in high waves or wind and has had rockfall closures. Check the same day.
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.cost_note: Badabuchae-gil was about 5,000 KRW, partly refunded as a local voucher (2024-25 figure, not verified for 2026).
jeongdongjin-badabuchaegil.tips: Some Gangneung-line KTX trains run on to Jeongdongjin (about 2 h from Seoul). The local Donghae-line trains (Nuriro or ITX-Maeum) from Gangneung take about 15 min.

haslla-art-world.name: Haslla Art World
haslla-art-world.summary: A clifftop sculpture park, museum and art hotel looking over the sea, including a Pinocchio and marionette museum.
haslla-art-world.why: An art-and-sea stop with a Hakone Open-Air Museum vibe.
haslla-art-world.cost_note: About 12,000-18,000 KRW adult depending on the package (not verified). The official site refused fetches.
haslla-art-world.tips: It pairs with Jeongdongjin and Badabuchae-gil.

woljeongsa-fir-forest.name: Woljeongsa Temple & Fir Forest Path (Odaesan)
woljeongsa-fir-forest.summary: A 1 km path through about 1,700 fir trees, some 300+ years old, leads to Woljeongsa. The temple was founded in 643, and its 15 m octagonal nine-storey pagoda is a National Treasure.
woljeongsa-fir-forest.why: This is the closest match to a Japanese cedar-avenue temple approach (like Hakone's old road or Nikko). It is serene and green, with maples along the stream.
woljeongsa-fir-forest.autumn_note: The 2026 forecast puts Odaesan's peak at about Oct 16-25, with the valley maples along the stream turning in the second half of October.
woljeongsa-fir-forest.hours: The temple is open about 05:00-21:00. Museum about 09:00-18:00 (closed Tuesdays).
woljeongsa-fir-forest.cost_note: Free since May 2023. Parking is about 4,000-5,000 KRW.
woljeongsa-fir-forest.booking: None. Woljeongsa templestay can be booked via eng.templestay.com.
woljeongsa-fir-forest.tips: Take the KTX to Jinbu (Odaesan) station (about 1h20 from Seoul, 20 min from Gangneung), then a local bus or taxi (about 20 min, roughly 20,000 KRW).

seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.name: Seonjae-gil trail (Woljeongsa → Sangwonsa)
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.summary: A 9 km gently rising streamside forest trail used by monks, from Woljeongsa to Sangwonsa. Sangwonsa holds Korea's oldest bronze bell (725 AD, a National Treasure). Bus 223 runs on the road alongside, so you can walk one way and ride back.
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.why: One of Korea's best foliage walks: easy, quiet and spiritual.
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.autumn_note: The peak along the stream is about Oct 18-28. Weekends are busy.
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.closed: Trails can close temporarily in heavy rain.
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.cost_note: Free. The bus between the two temples is about 1,000-2,000 KRW.
seonjae-gil-sangwonsa.tips: Ride the bus up to Sangwonsa and walk downhill to Woljeongsa.

seorak-waterpia-spa.name: Seorak Waterpia (hot-spring water park, Hanwha Resort Seorak)
seorak-waterpia-spa.summary: A hot-spring water park and spa fed by Seorak's alkaline hot-spring water. It has outdoor hot-spring pools with Ulsanbawi views, plus a sauna (bathhouse).
seorak-waterpia-spa.why: This is the nearest thing to an onsen soak after hiking, though it is a water park rather than a ryokan. Bring swimsuits.
seorak-waterpia-spa.autumn_note: Outdoor hot pools on cool October evenings are lovely.
seorak-waterpia-spa.hours: About 09:00-18:00 (spa and sauna run longer); not confirmed for 2026.
seorak-waterpia-spa.cost_note: About 40,000-55,000 KRW adult in the shoulder season (2024-25 figure, not verified). Hanwha Sorano guests get discounts. The sauna-only ticket is much cheaper (about 10,000-15,000).
seorak-waterpia-spa.booking: On-site or through the Hanwha app or Naver.
seorak-waterpia-spa.tips: Swimsuit required. Korean bathhouse rules apply in the sauna section: nude, single-sex. Tattoos are generally tolerated.

cheoksan-hot-spring.name: Cheoksan Hot Spring (public baths)
cheoksan-hot-spring.summary: A natural alkaline hot spring at about 53 °C. It has a public bathhouse with an outdoor rotenburo-style bath set in pines, plus simple lodging rooms.
cheoksan-hot-spring.why: The most onsen-like public bath in the Sokcho and Seorak area: single-sex, nude, with an outdoor bath, as in Japan.
cheoksan-hot-spring.autumn_note: The outdoor bath under autumn foliage is great after a Seorak hike.
cheoksan-hot-spring.hours: Daily 05:30-20:00 for the sauna and baths. Outdoor rotenburo 08:30-19:00, jjimjil building 10:00-19:00.
cheoksan-hot-spring.cost_note: Adult about 9,000-10,000 KRW (2024-25 figure, not verified).
cheoksan-hot-spring.tips: It is 10 minutes by taxi from Seorak-dong. Pair it with a Seorak hike day.
cheoksan-hot-spring.price_krw: Adult 11,000 (10,290 prepaid on Waug, valid to Dec 31, 2026). Sauna plus jjimjilbang 20,000. Private family hot-spring room, 3 hours: 50,000 for 2 people or 70,000 for 4, plus 15,000 per extra person. Family rooms are booked by phone on the same day from 09:00.
cheoksan-hot-spring.notes: 53°C alkaline water drawn from 4,000 m down. Confirmed by the official rate page and a Waug ticket sold for 2026, with reviews dated Sep 2026. The nearby Cheoksan Foot-bath Park (free entry, 1,000 KRW foot bath) is open Mar-Nov, 10:00-17:30.

arte-museum-gangneung.name: ARTE Museum Gangneung (immersive media art)
arte-museum-gangneung.summary: An immersive digital-art exhibition in the teamLab mold, near Gyeongpo.
arte-museum-gangneung.why: A rainy-day option with Tokyo teamLab vibes.

bulguksa.name: Bulguksa Temple
bulguksa.summary: UNESCO-listed 8th-century Silla temple with stone stairway-bridges (Cheongungyo/Baegungyo) and the Dabotap and Seokgatap pagodas. Korea's most famous temple.
