bulguksa.why: The Kamakura analog: a grand historic temple on wooded hills, best early morning before tour buses. Pairs with Seokguram like Kamakura's Hase-dera + Daibutsu.
bulguksa.autumn_note: Maples around the entrance pond and Cheongungyo turn red. trip.com Korea's 2026 forecast puts Bulguksa/Seokguram peak at Oct 22-29 (+/- 3-10 days); weatheri.co.kr (Sep 4 2026) says 2026 foliage runs later than normal, so expect early-to-partial color on Oct 18-24 rather than full peak.
bulguksa.cost_note: Free since May 2023 (cultural-heritage admission abolished). Parking fee charged for cars.
bulguksa.tips: Arrive at opening on a weekday; weekend afternoons in late October are packed with school and tour groups. City bus 10/11 (or 700 from Gyeongju Station) reaches the Bulguksa stop; taxi from downtown ~15,000-18,000 KRW. Free English guided tours are offered at the info center at set times (check on arrival).

seokguram.name: Seokguram Grotto
seokguram.summary: UNESCO-listed artificial granite grotto (8th c.) holding a seated Buddha facing the East Sea; viewed through glass. Short forest walk (~600 m) from the parking lot.
seokguram.why: Kamakura Daibutsu analog, but intimate and mountaintop; the ridge walk has East Sea views.
seokguram.autumn_note: Tohamsan ridge colors before the valley; 2026 forecasts suggest late October color here.
seokguram.time_needed: 1-1.5 h (plus 20 min bus each way); or 1 h hike from Bulguksa via the Tohamsan trail (~3.2 km, uphill)
seokguram.cost_note: Free since May 2023. Bus 12 Bulguksa <-> Seokguram 1,500 KRW (cash/card), ~20 min, about hourly.
seokguram.tips: Photography inside is prohibited. Check bus 12 departure board at Bulguksa parking lot; if you just miss it, taxis wait at Bulguksa (~10,000 KRW). Hiking up the old trail is a nice nature leg in autumn.

daereungwon-cheonmachong.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex & Cheonmachong
daereungwon-cheonmachong.summary: Park of 23 grassy Silla royal burial mounds; Cheonmachong is the one you can enter (excavated tomb with the Heavenly Horse painting replica and gold crown replicas).
daereungwon-cheonmachong.why: Uniquely Gyeongju: walking among giant green tumuli is the signature image of the city; next to Hwangridan-gil (the 'Komachi-dori' of Gyeongju).
daereungwon-cheonmachong.autumn_note: Mounds turn golden-brown; the lone magnolia/photo spot between tombs is famous. Evening lighting.
daereungwon-cheonmachong.hours: 09:00-22:00, last entry 21:30 (per Wikivoyage; extended hours since 2023)
daereungwon-cheonmachong.cost_note: Adult 3,000 KRW (Wikivoyage, 2025-era). Some reports say parts of the complex have become free; verify at gate.
daereungwon-cheonmachong.tips: Combine at dusk with Cheomseongdae and Donggung/Wolji (all within 1.5 km).

cheomseongdae.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory & flower fields
cheomseongdae.summary: 7th-century stone astronomical observatory, oldest surviving in East Asia, set in open fields planted seasonally.
cheomseongdae.why: Short, iconic stop on the walking/biking loop between the tombs, Gyerim and Wolji Pond.
cheomseongdae.autumn_note: Pink muhly (핑크뮬리) field and cosmos east of the observatory; pink muhly is typically best late Sep to mid-Oct, so by Oct 18-20 it will be past peak but still pinkish-brown. Silver grass and cosmos fill in.
cheomseongdae.hours: Grounds open 24 h; lit after sunset
cheomseongdae.tips: Go at golden hour then walk 10 min to Donggung & Wolji for lights.

donggung-wolji.name: Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond
donggung-wolji.summary: Reconstructed pavilions of a Silla crown-prince palace beside an ornamental pond; Gyeongju's signature night view with mirror reflections.
donggung-wolji.why: The night-lit, reflective-water moment; a calmer counterpoint to Shibuya neon.
donggung-wolji.autumn_note: Trees around the pond turn in late Oct-early Nov; reflections best on still evenings.
donggung-wolji.booking: None; expect a ticket queue 18:00-19:30 on weekends
donggung-wolji.tips: Arrive 30-40 min before sunset (~17:45 in late Oct) to see dusk and lights. Flat, accessible path.

woljeonggyo-gyochon.name: Woljeonggyo Bridge & Gyochon Traditional Village
woljeonggyo-gyochon.area: Gyeongju downtown - Gyo-dong, by Namcheon stream
woljeonggyo-gyochon.summary: Reconstructed covered Silla bridge (lit at night) next to the hanok village of the wealthy Gyeongju Choi family, with the old Confucian school (Hyanggyo) and Gyochon gimbap shops.
woljeonggyo-gyochon.why: Lantern-lit wooden bridge reflected in the stream, close to a ryokan-street mood; ideal for an evening stroll after dinner at Yoseokgung.
woljeonggyo-gyochon.autumn_note: Silla Culture Festival 2026 used Woljeonggyo as a stage on Oct 9-11 (before your visit).
woljeonggyo-gyochon.hours: Bridge open roughly 09:00-22:00 with night lighting; village always accessible (shops ~10:00-18:00); Choi family house typically closed Mondays
woljeonggyo-gyochon.tips: Cross the stepping stones (징검다리) just downstream for the classic photo. Walk Gyerim forest on the way from Cheomseongdae.

gyerim.name: Gyerim Forest
gyerim.area: Gyeongju downtown, between Cheomseongdae and Gyochon
gyerim.summary: Ancient grove of zelkova and willow trees tied to the founding myth of the Gyeongju Kim clan.
gyerim.why: Short shaded walk connecting the night-view sites.
gyerim.autumn_note: Old zelkovas turn yellow-orange late Oct-early Nov; lit at night.
gyerim.tips: Part of the 2 km Cheomseongdae -> Gyerim -> Woljeonggyo -> Wolji evening loop.

hwangridan-gil.name: Hwangridan-gil
hwangridan-gil.summary: Hanok-lined street of cafes, bakeries, photo studios, small bars and shops along the west side of Daereungwon.
hwangridan-gil.why: Closest thing to Kamakura's Komachi-dori: charming low-rise street snacking and browsing.
hwangridan-gil.autumn_note: Seasonal menus (chestnut, persimmon); hanbok rentals popular for foliage photos.
hwangridan-gil.cost_note: Free to wander; hanbok rental ~15,000-30,000 KRW for 2-4 h (low confidence)
hwangridan-gil.tips: Very crowded on weekends; weekday mornings are pleasant. Try Hwangnam-ppang and Gyeongju-ppang red-bean pastries.

gyeongju-national-museum.name: Gyeongju National Museum
gyeongju-national-museum.summary: Best Silla collection in Korea: gold crowns, the Emille Bell (Divine Bell of King Seongdeok), Wolji artifacts.
gyeongju-national-museum.why: Context for everything else in Gyeongju; good rainy-day option. Hosted the Korea-US summit venue during APEC 2025 and a Silla gold crown special exhibit.
gyeongju-national-museum.autumn_note: Garden has ginkgo and maple; check 2026 autumn special exhibition on arrival.
gyeongju-national-museum.hours: 10:00-18:00 typical; extended evening hours on some days (low confidence for 2026)
gyeongju-national-museum.closed: Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok days (open other days)
gyeongju-national-museum.cost_note: Permanent galleries free; special exhibits may charge
gyeongju-national-museum.tips: 5 min walk from Wolji Pond; do museum late afternoon then Wolji at dusk.

yangdong-village.name: Yangdong Folk Village
yangdong-village.area: Gyeongju - Gangdong-myeon (~20 km NE of downtown)
yangdong-village.summary: UNESCO-listed living Joseon clan village (Son and Yi clans) of ~150 hanok and thatched houses on wooded hills; people still live here.
yangdong-village.why: Quieter and more authentic than Hahoe; strolling lanes and hillside houses echo Kamakura's back streets.
yangdong-village.autumn_note: Persimmon trees fruiting and rice harvested in late October; very photogenic.
yangdong-village.tips: City buses 200-208 to Yangdong-maeul stop are infrequent; taxi from downtown ~25,000 KRW. Respect residents' privacy.

bomun-lake.name: Bomun Lake Resort area
bomun-lake.area: Gyeongju - Bomun (6 km east of downtown)
bomun-lake.summary: Lakeside resort zone with a ~8 km walking/cycling loop, hotels, the HICO convention center that hosted APEC 2025, and Gyeongju Expo Park.
bomun-lake.why: Resort-and-lake evening walk near the hot-spring hotels (Izu-resort mood). Post-APEC, Gyeongbuk is adding night trails, a media wall and Waterwheel Square night lighting in H2 2026.
bomun-lake.autumn_note: Cherry trees along the loop turn red-orange late Oct. APEC Memorial Festa and the APEC Summit Memorial Hall opening are Oct 30-31 2026, after your trip.
bomun-lake.cost_note: Free; duck boats and bike rentals extra
bomun-lake.tips: Bus 10/11 connect downtown and Bomun. Night lighting improving through 2026; exact completion of new night trail not confirmed.

golgulsa.name: Golgulsa Temple (Sunmudo)
golgulsa.area: Gyeongju - Yangbuk/Munmudaewang-myeon (~35 min east of downtown)
golgulsa.summary: Cliffside cave temple with a rock-carved Buddha, home of Sunmudo (Zen martial arts). Daily Sunmudo demonstration and templestay programs (~7,000 foreign participants a year).
golgulsa.why: A genuinely Korean temple experience with martial-arts performance; can be combined with Gampo coast and the underwater tomb of King Munmu.
golgulsa.autumn_note: Hamwolsan forest color late Oct-early Nov.
golgulsa.hours: Temple open daylight hours; Sunmudo demonstration historically daily 15:00 (Mon often off) - re-confirm
golgulsa.tips: Bus 100/150 from Gyeongju terminal to Andong-ri stop then 20 min walk; taxi ~30,000 KRW from downtown. Combine with Gameunsa site and Munmu underwater tomb (Bonggil beach).

tongiljeon-ginkgo.name: Tongiljeon Ginkgo Road
tongiljeon-ginkgo.summary: About 1 km avenue of ginkgo trees leading to Tongiljeon shrine at the foot of Namsan; Gyeongju's famous yellow-tunnel road.
tongiljeon-ginkgo.why: Pure autumn foliage spot; easy to add on the way to/from Bulguksa by taxi or bike.
tongiljeon-ginkgo.autumn_note: Usually peaks late Oct to early Nov; in a late 2026 season it may still be greenish-yellow around Oct 20-24.
tongiljeon-ginkgo.tips: Nearby Seochulji pond and Namsan trailheads. Go late in the trip for better color.

gyeongju-bike.name: Bike / e-bike loop of central Gyeongju
gyeongju-bike.area: Gyeongju downtown (rentals near Intercity/Express Bus Terminal and Hwangridan-gil)
gyeongju-bike.summary: Flat central heritage zone is ideal by bike: terminals -> Daereungwon -> Cheomseongdae -> Wolji -> Museum -> Gyochon (~6 km).
gyeongju-bike.why: Like cycling around Kamakura: covers spread-out sites cheaply.
gyeongju-bike.cost_note: Regular bike ~7,000-10,000 KRW/day (Wikivoyage); e-bike or e-scooter ~10,000-20,000 KRW per few hours (low confidence)
gyeongju-bike.tips: Bomun/Bulguksa are uphill and far; take bus/taxi for those.

gyeongju-city-tour.name: Gyeongju City Tour Bus
gyeongju-city-tour.summary: Guided day and evening bus loops (e.g. Bulguksa-Seokguram day course; night course to Wolji/Woljeonggyo).
gyeongju-city-tour.why: Saves transport hassle for Bulguksa/Seokguram/Golgulsa which are spread out.
gyeongju-city-tour.autumn_note: Night course useful for lit sites.
gyeongju-city-tour.cost_note: Roughly 12,000-20,000 KRW plus admissions (prior-year; unverified for 2026)
gyeongju-city-tour.booking: Online in Korean; English commentary limited
gyeongju-city-tour.tips: For 3 people, a taxi-tour (~4 h ~150,000-200,000 KRW per car) or KakaoT taxis may be as cost-effective.

hahoe-village.name: Andong Hahoe Folk Village
hahoe-village.area: Andong - Pungcheon-myeon (~25 km west of downtown)
hahoe-village.summary: UNESCO-listed Pungsan Ryu clan village in a bend of the Nakdong River; thatched and tiled houses, pine grove Mansongjeong, mask-dance performances.
hahoe-village.why: Korea's archetypal historic village with river and cliffs; overnighting here (Rakkojae or a minbak) is the most ryokan-like rural stay.
hahoe-village.autumn_note: Harvest fields, persimmons and riverside foliage. Hahoe Seonyu Julbul-nori (rope-fire festival) runs on Sat Oct 17 and Sat Oct 24 2026, 18:00-20:00.
hahoe-village.time_needed: Half day (+ evening if staying for the fire show)
hahoe-village.cost_note: Adult ~5,000 KRW incl. shuttle from the parking/ticket area (prior-year rate)
hahoe-village.tips: Bus 246 from Andong Station/Bus Terminal (~50 min, ~1,700 KRW, roughly every 1-1.5 h). Free Hahoe Byeolsingut Talnori mask-dance show Tue-Sun 14:00-15:00.

buyongdae.name: Buyongdae Cliff
buyongdae.area: Andong - across the river from Hahoe
buyongdae.summary: 64 m cliff overlooking the whole Hahoe river bend; Okyeonjeongsa and Gyeomamjeongsa pavilions nearby.
buyongdae.why: The classic aerial view of Hahoe; also the launch point of the julbul fire ropes.
buyongdae.autumn_note: Best at late-afternoon light; colors late Oct.
buyongdae.cost_note: Free; reaching it requires a short ferry across the river from Hahoe (seasonal, ~3,000-5,000 KRW, low confidence) or a drive around
buyongdae.tips: Ferry operates when river levels allow; otherwise taxi around (~15 min).

byeongsanseowon.name: Byeongsanseowon Confucian Academy
byeongsanseowon.area: Andong - Pungcheon-myeon, 4 km east of Hahoe by dirt road
byeongsanseowon.summary: UNESCO Seowon; its open Mandaeru pavilion frames the river and Byeongsan cliff - one of Korea's most admired wooden architecture views.
byeongsanseowon.why: Contemplative wooden-architecture-meets-nature moment akin to Kamakura's Zen temples.
byeongsanseowon.autumn_note: Byeongsan cliff foliage and crepe myrtle trees turning.
byeongsanseowon.tips: Bus service is rare; taxi from Hahoe (~10 min) or walk the 4-5 km riverside trail (~1.5 h).

woryeonggyo.name: Woryeonggyo Bridge
woryeonggyo.area: Andong - near Andong Folk Museum / Andong Dam
woryeonggyo.summary: Korea's longest wooden footbridge (387 m) over the Nakdong with a pavilion in the middle; illuminated at night.
woryeonggyo.why: Night-lit wooden bridge walk, easy from Gurume Resort; Andong's evening highlight.
woryeonggyo.autumn_note: Riverside trees color late Oct; fountain shows typically run only through October (unconfirmed for 2026).
woryeonggyo.hours: Always open; lights after sunset to ~23:00
woryeonggyo.tips: Eat heotjesabap at Kkachigumeongjip nearby; 10-15 min walk from Gurume Resort; taxi ~10 min from Andong Station.

jeonju-hanok-village.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
jeonju-hanok-village.summary: About 700 hanok in a walkable district with craft workshops, hanok cafes, street food and Jeondong Cathedral.
jeonju-hanok-village.why: Kamakura-like charm streets plus strongest food culture in Korea (bibimbap, makgeolli).
jeonju-hanok-village.autumn_note: Ginkgo on Gyeonggijeon grounds and Hyanggyo (late Oct-early Nov).
jeonju-hanok-village.tips: Very busy on weekends; Jeonju Hyanggyo (향교) ginkgo is the best autumn photo spot. Nambu Market night market Fri-Sat evenings.

gyeonggijeon.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine
gyeonggijeon.summary: Shrine holding the portrait of Joseon founder Taejo, with Royal Portrait Museum and bamboo groves.
gyeonggijeon.why: Historic heart of the hanok village.
gyeonggijeon.autumn_note: Ginkgo and maple inside the walls color late Oct-early Nov.
gyeonggijeon.tips: Free English tours are offered several times daily (low confidence).

omokdae.name: Omokdae & Imokdae
omokdae.summary: Hilltop pavilion with the classic rooftop view over the hanok village.
omokdae.why: Short climb for the postcard sunset view.
omokdae.tips: Go just before sunset, then dinner in the village.

hallasan-yeongsil-trail.name: Hallasan Yeongsil Trail (to Witse-oreum)
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.summary: Shortest, most scenic Hallasan route: from Yeongsil rest area (1,280 m) 3.7 km / ~1.5 h one-way up past the Byeongpung-bawi cliffs and Obaek-nahan (500 Arhats) rock spires to the alpine plateau at Witse-oreum shelter (1,700 m). Does not reach the summit crater.
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.why: The single best half-day mountain experience on Jeju; like hiking in Hakone/Izu highlands but with a volcanic alpine plateau and sea views. No reservation needed.
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.autumn_note: 2026 Korea Forest Service forecast: Hallasan foliage peak ~Nov 6. A jeju.com Sept 30, 2026 post said foliage had not begun as of Sept 28 and projected first color ~Oct 31 (another source cited KMA first color Oct 14). Expect early-to-partial color on the Yeongsil cliffs Oct 20-24, not peak. Silver grass and alpine shrubs on the plateau are attractive regardless.
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.time_needed: 4-5 h round trip from upper rest area (add ~40-50 min each way if walking the 2.4 km road from the lower Yeongsil ticket office)
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.hours: No booking. Entry control times vary by season; Sep-Oct trailhead entry cutoff reported as ~14:00 (moved from 15:00), with earlier cutoffs to continue beyond Witse-oreum toward Nambyeok junction. Go before 10:00.
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.closed: Closed in heavy rain/strong wind or snow advisories
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.cost_note: Free entry; upper Yeongsil parking is small and fills early (car park fee ~KRW 1,800 per car historically, unverified 2026). Bus 240 reaches the lower Yeongsil entrance.
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.booking: None required (only Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa summit routes require booking).
hallasan-yeongsil-trail.tips: Descend via Eorimok for a traverse only if you have a taxi arranged. Bring layers: plateau is 8-10°C colder than the coast. Witse-oreum shelter has toilets but no food sales.

hallasan-eorimok-trail.name: Hallasan Eorimok Trail
hallasan-eorimok-trail.summary: 4.7 km (~2 h one-way) to Witse-oreum via a steeper forest section then Sajebi-dongsan plateau viewpoint (1,423 m). No reservation.
hallasan-eorimok-trail.why: Alternative to Yeongsil; good as a one-way traverse (Eorimok up, Yeongsil down) with a taxi.
hallasan-eorimok-trail.autumn_note: Lower deciduous forest colors later than Yeongsil cliffs; Oct 20-24 likely early color only.
hallasan-eorimok-trail.tips: Bus 240 from Jeju City stops at Eorimok entrance.

hallasan-summit-seongpanak.name: Hallasan summit via Seongpanak / Gwaneumsa (Baengnokdam crater)
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.summary: The only routes to the 1,947 m summit crater. Seongpanak 9.6 km one-way (gentle, long, forest); Gwaneumsa 8.7 km (steeper, better views; Samgakbong). 8-10 h round trip.
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.why: Korea's highest peak; worth it only for keen hikers. For these travelers it costs a full day for modest foliage; Yeongsil gives more scenery per hour.
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.autumn_note: Upper slopes may show color by Oct 22-24 in a normal year; 2026 forecast peak is Nov 6.
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.hours: Winter-season rules (Oct-Mar) per 2026 guide: trailhead entry by 11:30 (many sources advise starting by ~07:00); Jindallaebat/Samgakbong shelter passage cutoff ~12:30 in some seasons; summit descent by 13:30.
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.booking: Mandatory free reservation at visithalla.jeju.go.kr, opens 09:00 on the first business day of the prior month (October slots opened Sept 1). Caps: Seongpanak 1,000/day, Gwaneumsa 500/day. Foreigners can book with email authentication/passport; QR + passport checked at gate; no transfers. Watch for cancellations (no penalty for cancelling).
hallasan-summit-seongpanak.tips: Late-October weekdays sometimes still have slots or cancellations; check now. Bus 281 serves Seongpanak.

saebyeol-oreum.name: Saebyeol Oreum
saebyeol-oreum.summary: Grassy volcanic cone (519 m) whose slopes turn silver with eulalia (eoksae) in October; 20-30 min steep climb to the ridge with views to the sea and Hallasan. Free, public parking at the base.
saebyeol-oreum.why: Jeju's signature autumn landscape; nothing like it in Japan trip so far. Golden-hour sunset walk.
saebyeol-oreum.autumn_note: Jeju silver grass peaks mid-Oct to early Nov; Oct 17-24 is prime. Visit after 16:00 for backlit grass at sunset.
saebyeol-oreum.tips: West slope is steeper; go up one side and down the east route. Windy; no shade. Pair with Arte Museum (10 min) or nearby cafe strip.

sangumburi.name: Sangumburi Crater
sangumburi.summary: Maar-type crater with a broad silver-grass field around the rim; easy paved walk, ~40 min.
sangumburi.why: The easiest, most photogenic silver-grass field; no climbing.
sangumburi.tips: On the way between Jeju City and Seongsan; combine with Saryeoni forest road.

ttarabi-oreum.name: Ttarabi Oreum
ttarabi-oreum.summary: Called the 'queen of oreum': three craters ringed by silver grass; 1-1.5 h round-trip walk.
ttarabi-oreum.why: Wilder, less crowded alternative to Saebyeol near Haevichi/Pyoseon.

yongnuni-oreum.name: Yongnuni Oreum
yongnuni-oreum.summary: Gentle, soft-contoured oreum (15 min to top), reopened July 2023 after rest period; silver grass and Seongsan views.
yongnuni-oreum.why: Easy add-on on the east loop between Bijarim and Seongsan.
yongnuni-oreum.autumn_note: Silver grass mid-Oct to early Nov.
yongnuni-oreum.tips: Stick to the marked path; restoration rules enforced.

seongsan-ilchulbong.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak)
seongsan-ilchulbong.summary: UNESCO World Natural Heritage tuff cone rising from the sea; ~25-30 min stair climb to a crater rim at 182 m. Iconic sunrise spot. Haenyeo diving demonstrations on the beach below (west side).
seongsan-ilchulbong.why: Jeju's must-see; the east-coast fishing villages and haenyeo give a seaside village feel similar to the Kamakura/Enoshima coast vibe.
seongsan-ilchulbong.autumn_note: Late-October sunrise ~06:50; the spring/fall schedule opens before dawn.
seongsan-ilchulbong.hours: Conflicting 2026 sources: jeju.com (Aug 2026) lists spring/fall 05:00-19:00, summer 04:30-20:00, winter 06:00-18:00; other listings show 04:30-20:00 with last ticket 19:00. Either way it opens before sunrise in late October.
seongsan-ilchulbong.closed: First Monday of each month (Nov 2, 2026 next; not within Oct 17-25)
seongsan-ilchulbong.tips: Haenyeo show historically 13:30 and 15:00 daily (weather permitting, free) at the beach below the peak's west side; verify on the day. Gwangchigi Beach (1 km) for low-tide sunrise reflections.

udo-island.name: Udo Island
udo-island.summary: Small island of stone-walled fields, white coral-sand Seobin Baeksa beach, Udo peanut ice cream and cliffs; explored by circular bus or rented e-bike/scooter.
udo-island.why: The closest Jeju equivalent of a quaint seaside island day like Enoshima.
udo-island.autumn_note: Mild late-Oct weather is ideal; ferries can be cancelled in high wind/waves.
udo-island.hours: Ferries every ~30 min from Seongsan port; summer first sailing 08:00, last return 18:30; autumn last sailings earlier (check day-of).
udo-island.cost_note: Adult round trip KRW 11,000 (2026, includes ferry, terminal and marine park entry). E-bike/tour bus extra (not verified for 2026).
udo-island.booking: Buy at Seongsan Port terminal; fill boarding forms; passport required.
udo-island.tips: Rental cars are banned from Udo in principle (exceptions: overnight lodging proof, elderly/infants/disabled, some EVs). Go early (08:00-09:00) to beat tour groups.

sanbangsan-yongmeori.name: Sanbangsan & Yongmeori Coast
sanbangsan-yongmeori.summary: Bell-shaped lava dome (395 m) with Sanbanggulsa cave temple, and at its foot the Yongmeori 'dragon head' coast: layered sandstone tuff cliffs on a 30-60 min tidal walkway.
sanbangsan-yongmeori.why: Most dramatic coastal geology on Jeju; feels like Izu's Jogasaki coast. Combine with the carbonated hot spring nearby.
sanbangsan-yongmeori.autumn_note: Clear autumn air; Yongmeori opens only at suitable tides.
sanbangsan-yongmeori.hours: Yongmeori 09:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30) BUT opening depends on tide/waves daily; often closed.
sanbangsan-yongmeori.cost_note: Combined Sanbanggulsa + Yongmeori adult KRW 2,500; Yongmeori alone KRW 2,000
sanbangsan-yongmeori.booking: Walk-in; check Seogwipo city's daily Yongmeori open notice (or call) that morning
sanbangsan-yongmeori.tips: Olle Route 10 passes here; Hamel ship exhibit at the entrance.

sanbangsan-hot-spring.name: Sanbangsan Carbonated Hot Spring
sanbangsan-hot-spring.summary: Rare carbonated hot spring: gender-separated indoor baths (nude, Japanese-onsen style) plus a swimsuit outdoor pool area and jjimjilbang.
sanbangsan-hot-spring.why: The best public onsen analog on Jeju; pair with Sanbangsan/Yongmeori.
sanbangsan-hot-spring.autumn_note: Outdoor pool pleasant in mild late-Oct evenings.
sanbangsan-hot-spring.cost_note: Indoor KRW 14,000; outdoor KRW 5,000; jjimjilbang KRW 2,000 (ktriptips, updated 2026-05-22)
sanbangsan-hot-spring.tips: Bring swimsuit for the outdoor section. Dammora Hotel & Resort is ~700 m away.

jusangjeolli-daepo.name: Jungmun Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff
jusangjeolli-daepo.summary: Hexagonal basalt columns up to 25 m with waves crashing; short boardwalk.
jusangjeolli-daepo.why: Quick, spectacular stop near Jungmun hotels.
jusangjeolli-daepo.autumn_note: Best with swell on windy autumn days.
jusangjeolli-daepo.tips: Combine with Cheonjeyeon falls and Jungmun hotels; crowded with tour buses mid-day.

olle-route-7-oedolgae.name: Jeju Olle Route 7 (Oedolgae section)
olle-route-7-oedolgae.summary: Route 7 runs 17.6 km (5-6 h, medium) from the Jeju Olle Tourist Center in Seogwipo west to Wolpyeong. The first 3-5 km past Oedolgae sea stack, Dombe-nangkol and pine-cliff paths is the classic section.
olle-route-7-oedolgae.why: Coastal walking with cliffs, sea stacks and village lanes; the best 'Kamakura-to-Enoshima coastal stroll' analog on Jeju.
olle-route-7-oedolgae.time_needed: 2-3 h for the scenic first section
olle-route-7-oedolgae.tips: Walk Seogwipo Olle Market -> Cheonjiyeon -> Saeyeon Bridge -> Oedolgae; take taxi/bus back.

cheonjiyeon-saeyeongyo.name: Cheonjiyeon Falls & Saeyeon Bridge
cheonjiyeon-saeyeongyo.summary: 22 m waterfall in a subtropical gorge, open into the evening; nearby Saeyeon Bridge to Saeseom islet. Venue area for the Seogwipo Chilsimni Festival (Oct 23-25).
cheonjiyeon-saeyeongyo.why: Easy evening stroll from Seogwipo lodging/market.
cheonjiyeon-saeyeongyo.autumn_note: Seogwipo Chilsimni Festival parade/drone show Oct 23-25, 2026 at the Cheonjiyeon parking area.

bijarim.name: Bijarim Forest
bijarim.summary: Natural Monument forest of ~2,800 nutmeg-yew (bija) trees, some 500-800 years old, on red volcanic scoria paths; 1-1.5 h loop.
bijarim.why: Quiet, mossy, sacred-feeling forest walk akin to a Japanese cedar temple approach.
bijarim.autumn_note: Evergreen; atmospheric in any weather (good rain-day plan).
bijarim.tips: Combine with Yongnuni Oreum, Sehwa/Woljeong beaches, Haenyeo Museum.

hueree-park.name: Hueree Natural Park (pink muhly + tangerine picking)
hueree-park.summary: Garden park running a pink muhly festival through early November, plus walk-in tangerine picking.
hueree-park.why: Easy autumn-seasonal photo stop and the simplest way to do tangerine picking.
hueree-park.autumn_note: Pink muhly peak mid-to-late October. Tangerines are still greenish in October (fully orange from mid-Nov).
hueree-park.cost_note: Entry KRW 13,000 + tangerine picking ~KRW 8,000 (1 kg); online tickets up to 20% cheaper
hueree-park.tips: Gimgyul (Hyodon citrus) Museum offers cheaper picking: KRW 1,500 entry + KRW 5,000.

camellia-hill.name: Camellia Hill
camellia-hill.summary: Large camellia arboretum; in autumn known for pink muhly and silver grass patches, early camellias (sasanqua) from November.
camellia-hill.why: Near Podo Hotel/Sanbangsan; pretty garden stroll.
camellia-hill.autumn_note: Pink muhly mid-late Oct; main camellia festival is mid-Nov to Feb (not during trip).
camellia-hill.tips: Choose Hueree OR Camellia Hill, not both.

arte-museum-jeju.name: ARTE MUSEUM Jeju
arte-museum-jeju.summary: Immersive digital-art museum by d'strict in a converted factory; themed rooms (waves, flowers, garden) plus a tea bar.
arte-museum-jeju.why: Korea's answer to teamLab; a good rain-day stop near Saebyeol Oreum.
arte-museum-jeju.cost_note: Approx. adult KRW 17,000-19,000 (2025-era; official site blocked to fetch, unverified for 2026)
arte-museum-jeju.tips: If they did teamLab in Tokyo, this is optional.

haenyeo-kitchen.name: Haenyeo's Kitchen (dinner theatre with haenyeo)
haenyeo-kitchen.summary: 2-hour theatre in a converted fish auction house: young actors and a senior haenyeo (in her 90s) tell diver stories, then a buffet/course of freshly harvested seafood around a bulteok-style table. Small groups (~14 seats at Jongdal).
haenyeo-kitchen.why: Direct analog to Japan's ama divers; combines culture and a seafood meal. English site exists.
haenyeo-kitchen.hours: Show schedule not published on the site; booking line weekdays 10:00-18:00 KST (+82 70-5224-1828)
haenyeo-kitchen.cost_note: Price not shown on site at fetch time; historically roughly KRW 80,000-100,000+ pp (unverified).
haenyeo-kitchen.booking: Reserve via en.haenyeokitchen.com (locations page) or phone/Kakao; sells out.
haenyeo-kitchen.tips: Coordinates not verified (near Jongdal port, ~10 min north of Seongsan). Free alternative: haenyeo dive show below Seongsan Ilchulbong; Jeju Haenyeo Museum (KRW 1,100, closed Mondays).

jeju-haenyeo-museum.name: Jeju Haenyeo Museum
jeju-haenyeo-museum.summary: Museum of the UNESCO-listed haenyeo women-diver culture.
jeju-haenyeo-museum.why: Context for the haenyeo show; cheap and near Sehwa beach.
jeju-haenyeo-museum.tips: Sehwa 5-day market runs on dates ending in 5 and 0.

seogwipo-maeil-olle-market.name: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market
seogwipo-maeil-olle-market.summary: Covered daily market: hairtail, mackerel, tangerines, hallabong, street food (black pork skewers, sashimi boxes).
seogwipo-maeil-olle-market.why: Casual food crawl like a Japanese shotengai; good evening base if staying in Seogwipo.
seogwipo-maeil-olle-market.tips: Walkable to Cheonjiyeon and Olle 7 start.

dongmun-market.name: Dongmun Traditional Market & Night Market
dongmun-market.summary: Jeju's oldest/largest market (since 1945); night market with grilled black pork, abalone, lobster and tangerine snacks.
dongmun-market.why: Lively evening food scene before/after a CJU flight (15 min from airport).
dongmun-market.tips: Jeju Folk 5-day Market (near airport) runs on dates ending 2 and 7 - Oct 17 and Oct 22, 2026 qualify.

saryeoni-forest.name: Saryeoni Forest Path
saryeoni-forest.summary: 15 km cedar and broadleaf forest road; walk any portion from the Bijaebong entrance.
saryeoni-forest.why: Cool forest walk, partially deciduous (some autumn color in late Oct/Nov).
saryeoni-forest.autumn_note: Mixed forest; some color late Oct to mid-Nov.
saryeoni-forest.tips: On the way between Sangumburi and Seongpanak.

incheon-airport-t1.name: Incheon International Airport Terminal 1
incheon-airport-t1.summary: Arrival and departure airport. Air Premia is understood to operate from T1 (confirm on e-ticket; Asiana moved to T2 on Jan 14 2026, Air Busan and Air Seoul also moved to T2 in 2025).
incheon-airport-t1.why: Dawn arrival at 05:15 Sat Oct 17 and departure 21:55 Sun Oct 25.
incheon-airport-t1.time_needed: Arrival: allow 45-75 min for immigration + bags before heading into Seoul. Departure: be at the airport by ~19:00 (3h before).
incheon-airport-t1.hours: 24h; AREX Express first train from T1 05:23 (T2 05:15); all-stop trains from ~05:20
incheon-airport-t1.tips: Darakhyu capsule hotel (landside, transportation center of each terminal) rents rooms by the block: roughly 30,000-40,000 KRW for 3 hours or 60,000-80,000 KRW overnight per room (Wikivoyage snapshot, prices not 2026-verified). Spa on Air (T1 B1 sauna) listed at ~15,000 KRW overnight/27,000 private room, but its 2026 operating status could not be confirmed.

seoul-station.name: Seoul Station (KTX, AREX, City Airport Terminal)
seoul-station.summary: Main KTX hub for Gyeongbu (Busan, Gyeongju) and Gangneung lines; AREX terminus; T-Luggage storage counter.
seoul-station.why: Most of the trip's rail legs start or end here.
seoul-station.tips: City Airport Terminal check-in (B2) participating airlines per Sep 2026 source: Korean Air, Asiana, Jeju Air, Jin Air, T'way, Eastar Jet, Air Seoul. Air Premia is NOT on the list, so the travelers cannot check bags in at Seoul Station.

gyeongju-station-ktx.name: Gyeongju Station (formerly Singyeongju)
gyeongju-station-ktx.summary: KTX station for Gyeongju on the Gyeongbu HSR, Donghae Line and Jungang Line; booking sites may now list it as 'Gyeongju (경주)' rather than 'Singyeongju'. ~20-30 min by bus/taxi to the historic center.
gyeongju-station-ktx.why: Gateway to Gyeongju and junction for Busan-Bujeon and Gangneung east-coast trains.
gyeongju-station-ktx.tips: Search for both '경주' and 'Singyeongju' in apps. Taxi to Hwangnidan-gil roughly 20,000-25,000 KRW (estimate).

bukchon.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
bukchon.summary: Hillside lanes of lived-in hanok houses between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, plus the Samcheong-dong cafe street.
bukchon.why: The closest match to Kamakura's charming old lanes, but it is a residential neighborhood, so visit quietly.
bukchon.autumn_note: Clear autumn days give views over the tiled roofs toward Namsan.
bukchon.hours: Red zone (Bukchon-ro 11-gil, about 34,000 m2): tourists allowed only 10:00-17:00, enforced since Mar 1, 2025 and still in force in 2026. Orange zones (Bukchon-ro 5ga-gil, Gyedong-gil) and the yellow zone (Bukchon-ro 12-gil) have no curfew but are patrolled. Chartered tour buses have been banned on Bukchon-ro since 2026.
bukchon.closed: Red-zone lanes are closed to sightseeing 17:00-10:00
bukchon.cost_note: Free. Fine of up to 100,000 KRW for sightseeing in the red zone outside 10:00-17:00. This applies even to hanok-stay guests if they are judged to be sightseeing.
bukchon.tips: Be in the 11-gil lanes between 10:00 and 17:00. No loud talk or drones, and don't photograph through gates. Hanok-stay guests should walk straight to their door at night.

ikseon-dong.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Street
ikseon-dong.summary: A tight cluster of 1920s urban hanok turned into cafes, bakeries and bars.
ikseon-dong.why: Feels like Kamakura's Komachi-dori with hanok: small lanes full of food. Easy to pair with Jongmyo, Changdeokgung and the Jongno-3ga tents.
ikseon-dong.autumn_note: Courtyard cafes and makgeolli bars are pleasant on cool nights.
ikseon-dong.cost_note: Free to wander. Cafes cost about 7,000-10,000 per drink.
ikseon-dong.tips: Weekday afternoons are calmer. At night, walk 3 minutes to the Jongno-3ga pojangmacha tents.

seochon.name: Seochon and Tongin Market
seochon.summary: Lanes west of the palace with hanok, galleries, small restaurants and Tongin Market. At Tongin, you buy brass coins (yeopjeon) to pay for a dosirak (lunchbox) at the food stalls, and the oil-tteokbokki stall is the classic snack.
seochon.why: A calmer, local-feeling 'old town' and the start of the Inwangsan trail. Similar in feel to Kamakura's back streets.
seochon.autumn_note: Combine with the Inwangsan sunset hike or Suseong-dong Valley.
seochon.closed: Tongin Market: many stalls closed Mondays (dosirak cafe days vary; verify)
seochon.cost_note: About 10,000 in coins for a dosirak lunch
seochon.tips: Tosokchon samgyetang is here, and so are Onjium and wine bars for dinner.

inwangsan.name: Inwangsan and Seoul Fortress Wall (sunset hike)
inwangsan.summary: Short, steep hike along the 600-year-old fortress wall to the 338 m granite summit, with views over Gyeongbokgung, Bugaksan, Namsan and the city lights.
inwangsan.why: Kamakura's hiking trails above the temples, plus the best sunset view over the city.
inwangsan.autumn_note: Sunset is about 17:55 on Oct 17 and 17:47 on Oct 24. Start up about 75 min before.
inwangsan.hours: Open daily. Night descent is fine on lit stairs, but bring a headlamp.
inwangsan.closed: Can close during dry-season fire warnings (rare in October)
inwangsan.tips: Start from Sajik Park or Seochon. Suseong-dong Valley and the Inwangsan forest trail (Inwangsan Jarak-gil) make good add-ons. Walk down into Seochon for dinner.

bugaksan.name: Bugaksan (Baegaksan) Fortress Wall trail
bugaksan.summary: Wall section behind the former presidential Blue House. It has been fully open since 2022 and no longer needs ID registration.
bugaksan.why: Quieter hike with views, history and an armed-guard past. Can be linked to the Cheong Wa Dae grounds.
bugaksan.hours: Daytime only. Entry usually closes mid-afternoon (verify on the day).
bugaksan.tips: Start at Changuimun (bus from Gyeongbokgung station). Finish via Malbawi to Samcheong-dong.

naksan-park.name: Naksan Park and Ihwa Mural Village wall walk
naksan-park.summary: Easy wall walk with a lit fortress wall at night and city views. It runs down to Heunginjimun and DDP.
naksan-park.why: The easiest night view in Seoul. Combine it with Hyehwa (Daehangno theater district) for dinner.
naksan-park.autumn_note: Cool nights are good for the 30-minute walk to DDP.
naksan-park.tips: Walk Hyehwa station → Naksan → wall → Heunginjimun → DDP after dark.
naksan-park.image_query: Naksan Park Seoul city wall night

national-museum-korea.name: National Museum of Korea
national-museum-korea.summary: Korea's flagship museum. Highlights include the 'Room of Quiet Contemplation' with two pensive bodhisattvas, Silla gold crowns and a 10-story pagoda in the hall. It set attendance records in 2025-26.
national-museum-korea.why: One sitting gives the whole story of Korean history and art. Like the Tokyo National Museum.
national-museum-korea.autumn_note: The special exhibition '우리들의 밥상' (Our Dining Table, on Korean food culture) runs Jul 1 - Oct 25, 2026, which suits food lovers.
national-museum-korea.hours: Since Mar 16, 2026: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun 09:30-17:30. Wed and Sat 09:30-21:00 (last entry 30 min before close).
national-museum-korea.closed: Jan 1, Lunar New Year, Chuseok. Open Mondays.
national-museum-korea.cost_note: Permanent galleries free. Special exhibitions are often 0-15,000.
national-museum-korea.tips: Good Monday choice when the palaces are closed. Go on Wed Oct 21 or Sat Oct 24 for the evening hours. The Ichon Hangang Park riverside is nearby.
national-museum-korea.image_query: National Museum of Korea pensive bodhisattva room

war-memorial.name: War Memorial of Korea
war-memorial.summary: Large museum on the Korean War, with aircraft and armor outside. Free.
war-memorial.why: Useful context before or after a DMZ tour.
war-memorial.autumn_note: The outdoor plaza is pleasant in fall.
war-memorial.tips: Go the day before the DMZ. Mongtan (BBQ) and the Yongridan-gil restaurants are a 5-minute walk away.

namsangol.name: Namsangol Hanok Village
namsangol.summary: Five relocated Joseon houses with a pond garden, a time capsule and traditional-game and craft programs. Free.
namsangol.why: A free, uncrowded hanok stop on the walk from Myeongdong up Namsan.
namsangol.autumn_note: The pond garden turns color in late Oct.
namsangol.tips: Walk from Chungmuro station. Continue up Namsan to N Seoul Tower on foot.

n-seoul-tower.name: Namsan and N Seoul Tower
n-seoul-tower.summary: TV tower on Namsan with an observatory, a love-lock terrace and Namsan's fortress wall trails.
n-seoul-tower.why: The Tokyo Tower of Seoul. The walk up is free and the view at dusk is classic.
n-seoul-tower.autumn_note: The Namsan circuit road (Namsan Sunhwan-ro) has strong foliage in late Oct.
n-seoul-tower.cost_note: Observatory adult 21,000 (cheaper on Klook, Creatrip and similar). The Namsan cable car round trip was quoted at 8,500 by one source, but older sources say about 14,000-15,000 (verify). The planned Myeongdong-Namsan gondola has NOT opened: construction has been halted by lawsuits, and Seoul lost again on appeal in Sept 2026.
n-seoul-tower.tips: Skip the paid observatory and enjoy the free terrace. Take Namsan circulator bus 01A or 01B, or walk the stairs from Namsangol.

lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.name: Lotte World Tower – Seoul Sky
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.summary: Observatory on floors 117-123 of the 555 m tower, with a glass-floor Sky Deck. Seokchon Lake is at its base.
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.why: The Shibuya Sky or Tokyo Skytree equivalent: a sunset-to-night view of the whole city.
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.autumn_note: The cherry trees around Seokchon Lake turn red in late Oct.
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.cost_note: Adult 29,000 per a 2026 Korean source (some older pages say 31,000; check). Fast pass 50,000. OTAs discount it.
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.booking: Walk-up or OTA. Book a sunset slot.
lotte-world-tower-seoul-sky.tips: Clear autumn evenings are best. Combine with Seokchon Lake, or take the Hangang Bus from Jamsil pier.

myeongdong.name: Myeongdong
myeongdong.summary: Dense shopping streets of K-beauty stores and street-food carts in the evening. Myeongdong Cathedral and the Lotte and Shinsegae flagship department stores are here.
myeongdong.why: Shibuya-style crowd energy and neon at night. The most convenient base for the airport.
myeongdong.autumn_note: Street-food stalls (hotteok, roasted chestnuts, sweet potatoes) get busier as nights cool.
myeongdong.hours: Shops about 10:00-22:00. Street stalls from about 16:00.
myeongdong.tips: Myeongdong Kyoja for kalguksu. Walk to Namsan or the Shinsegae main store's media facade.

hongdae-yeonnam.name: Hongdae and Yeonnam-dong (Gyeongui Line Forest Park)
hongdae-yeonnam.summary: University district with busking, clubs, live music, indie shops and photo booths. Yeonnam-dong's linear park ('Yeontral Park') is lined with cafes and restaurants.
hongdae-yeonnam.why: The closest match to Shibuya, Shimokitazawa and Harajuku: youth culture, street performers and late nights.
hongdae-yeonnam.autumn_note: Picnics on the Gyeongui Line forest park are good in October.
hongdae-yeonnam.hours: Busking from about 18:00. Clubs until dawn on weekends.
hongdae-yeonnam.cost_note: Club entry about 10,000-20,000. Live clubs about 15,000-30,000.
hongdae-yeonnam.tips: Friday or Saturday night is best for energy. Mangwon Market and the Han River are 15 minutes' walk.

seongsu.name: Seongsu-dong and Seoul Forest
seongsu.summary: Old shoe-factory district turned into Seoul's pop-up and concept-store capital (Seongsu 'Brooklyn'). Weekend pop-ups, specialty coffee, Dior Seongsu, and Seoul Forest park next door.
seongsu.why: Like Daikanyama or Kuramae: design, cafes and pop-up culture that changes weekly.
seongsu.autumn_note: Seoul Forest's ginkgos and metasequoias turn in late Oct to Nov. Picnic there.
seongsu.hours: Shops about 11:00-21:00. Pop-ups busiest on weekends.
seongsu.booking: Some pop-ups need a Naver or Catchtable reservation
seongsu.tips: Check Instagram for that week's pop-ups. Go Sat Oct 17 or Sat Oct 24. Ttukseom Hangang Park is close.

gangnam-coex-starfield.name: Gangnam / COEX Starfield Library / Bongeunsa
gangnam-coex-starfield.summary: COEX Mall's Starfield Library has 13 m bookshelves. The WAVE anamorphic LED screen is at the SM Town crossing. Bongeunsa, a 1,200-year-old Seon temple with a 23 m Maitreya statue, is directly across the street.
gangnam-coex-starfield.why: A modern 'Tokyo in Korea' contrast: glass towers next to an old temple, like Zojoji beside Tokyo Tower.
gangnam-coex-starfield.autumn_note: Bongeunsa's grounds turn color in late Oct. Its 'Temple Life' program (about 2 h) runs on set days.
gangnam-coex-starfield.cost_note: Free (Bongeunsa Temple Life is paid; check the temple's site)
gangnam-coex-starfield.tips: Do Bongeunsa first, then COEX. Lotte World Tower is 15 minutes away on Line 2.

garosugil-apgujeong.name: Garosu-gil, Apgujeong Rodeo, Dosan Park
garosugil-apgujeong.summary: A ginkgo-lined boulevard, Apgujeong Rodeo's boutiques and restaurants, and Dosan Park's flagship stores (Gentle Monster Haus Dosan and others).
garosugil-apgujeong.why: An Omotesando or Aoyama analog: polished shopping and dining.
garosugil-apgujeong.autumn_note: Garosu-gil literally means 'tree-lined street'. Its ginkgos go gold in late Oct to Nov.
garosugil-apgujeong.tips: Link it to the Hangang Bus Apgujeong pier or the Banpo fountain at night.

euljiro-hipjiro.name: Euljiro ('Hipjiro') and Nogari Alley
euljiro-hipjiro.summary: Print-shop and hardware-store alleys with hidden 2nd- and 3rd-floor bars. Nogari Alley spills plastic tables into the street for cheap draft beer and dried pollock.
euljiro-hipjiro.why: The Golden Gai, Yurakucho-under-the-tracks or Omoide Yokocho equivalent: gritty, retro and lively.
euljiro-hipjiro.autumn_note: Outdoor tables are best on cool October evenings.
euljiro-hipjiro.hours: Nogari Alley about 17:00-late. Some places close on Sundays.
euljiro-hipjiro.cost_note: Beer about 4,000-6,000. Nogari about 2,000-3,000 per stick.
euljiro-hipjiro.tips: The original Eulji OB Bear was evicted in 2022, but the alley lives on. Combine with the Euljiro Sewoon Plaza rooftop for a view.

jongno3ga-pojangmacha.name: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street
jongno3ga-pojangmacha.summary: A row of orange-tent street bars on Donhwamun-ro and around Ikseon-dong serving soju, grilled fish, sea snails and stir-fries.
jongno3ga-pojangmacha.why: The night-tent bar experience, like Fukuoka yatai or a Tokyo yokocho.
jongno3ga-pojangmacha.autumn_note: Tents are best on cool October nights.
jongno3ga-pojangmacha.closed: Some tents on Sundays or in rain
jongno3ga-pojangmacha.tips: Cash or card is fine at most. Pick a busy tent.

itaewon-hannam.name: Itaewon / Hannam-dong / Haebangchon
itaewon-hannam.summary: International bar and food scene. Hannam-dong has design-led shops and cafes, and Haebangchon is a hillside rooftop-bar village.
itaewon-hannam.why: Like Roppongi with Ebisu: global food and cocktail bars.
itaewon-hannam.autumn_note: Rooftop bars with a Namsan view in cool weather.
itaewon-hannam.tips: Leeum is in Hannam. Crowds are now well managed (crowd-control rules since the 2022 Halloween crush). Avoid the Halloween weekend, which is after the trip anyway.

mangwon.name: Mangwon-dong and Mangwon Market
mangwon.summary: Neighborhood market known for croquettes, dakgangjeong (crispy sweet chicken) and cheap street food. Indie cafes are nearby, and Mangwon Hangang Park is a 10-minute walk.
mangwon.why: Local, Shimokita-style everyday Seoul. Buy food and picnic by the river.
mangwon.autumn_note: Picnic at Mangwon Hangang Park at sunset. Hangang Bus Mangwon pier is here.
mangwon.tips: Get takeaway chicken and beer and walk to the river for chimaek.

gwangjang-market.name: Gwangjang Market
gwangjang-market.summary: Covered market from 1905, known for food stalls selling bindaetteok (mung-bean pancakes), yukhoe (beef tartare), mayak gimbap and kalguksu.
gwangjang-market.why: The Tsukiji Outer Market-style food crawl.
gwangjang-market.autumn_note: Hot pancakes and makgeolli suit cool evenings.
gwangjang-market.hours: Food stalls about 09:00-23:00. Fabric shops close earlier.
gwangjang-market.closed: Many non-food shops close on Sundays. Food alley open daily.
gwangjang-market.cost_note: About 20,000-30,000 per person for a crawl. Check prices before ordering: overcharging scandals in 2023-24 led to listed prices.
gwangjang-market.tips: Soonhee-ne bindaetteok and Buchon Yukhoe are the classics. Expect queues on weekend evenings.

noryangjin.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
noryangjin.summary: Seoul's huge seafood market. You choose live fish on the ground floor, then upstairs restaurants slice it as hoe (sashimi) and make maeuntang (spicy fish stew) for a setting fee.
noryangjin.why: The direct analog to their sushi-omakase love: Korean-style sashimi, DIY and lively.
noryangjin.autumn_note: Autumn seasonal seafood: jeoneo (gizzard shad, grilled), daeha (king prawns, salt-grilled), and fat autumn flounder and rockfish.
noryangjin.hours: General fish market about 01:30-22:00. The high-end live fish section runs 24 h.
noryangjin.cost_note: About 40,000-60,000 per person for a full sashimi meal. Upstairs setting fee about 5,000-15,000 per group or per person, plus maeuntang.
noryangjin.booking: None. A guided tour (about 2-3 h) is an option for first-timers.
noryangjin.tips: Compare a few stalls and agree on price and weight. Go for dinner. It is on Line 1 and Line 9 (Noryangjin station).

namdaemun-market.name: Namdaemun Market
namdaemun-market.summary: Huge old market with galchi-jorim alley (braised hairtail) and kalguksu alley. Next to Sungnyemun gate.
namdaemun-market.why: A cheap, old-school eating stop near a Seoul Station or Myeongdong base.
namdaemun-market.autumn_note: Hairtail (galchi) is in season in autumn.
namdaemun-market.tips: Go on a weekday. Pair with Deoksugung and Seoullo 7017.

jogyesa.name: Jogyesa Temple
jogyesa.summary: Headquarters of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, with ancient locust and white pine trees. Insadong is next door.
jogyesa.why: A working downtown temple and the easiest temple visit in Seoul.
jogyesa.autumn_note: Jogyesa usually holds its chrysanthemum festival (시월국화향기) from mid or late Oct into Nov. The 2026 dates were not confirmed.
jogyesa.cost_note: Free. Templestay information center across the street.

haneul-park-silver-grass.name: Haneul Park (Sky Park) – Seoul Silver Grass Festival
haneul-park-silver-grass.summary: A former landfill hill covered in eulalia silver grass. The 25th Seoul Silver Grass Festival (서울억새축제) is Oct 17-23, 2026, 10:00-21:00, with evening lighting.
haneul-park-silver-grass.why: The trip's autumn silver-grass moment inside Seoul, like Hakone Sengokuhara.
haneul-park-silver-grass.autumn_note: The festival dates overlap the trip almost exactly. The grass peaks mid-to-late Oct.
haneul-park-silver-grass.hours: Festival Oct 17-23, 10:00-21:00. Evening hours run later only during the festival.
haneul-park-silver-grass.cost_note: Free. The 'Maengkkongi' electric shuttle up the hill costs about 3,000 one way (verify).
haneul-park-silver-grass.tips: Go 1.5 h before sunset and stay for the lights. World Cup Stadium station (Line 6), then cross the footbridge and climb 291 stairs. Can be combined with Mangwon and Hongdae.

han-river-parks.name: Han River parks (Yeouido, Banpo, Ttukseom) and chimaek
han-river-parks.summary: Riverside parks for evening picnics with delivered fried chicken and beer (chimaek). Banpo Bridge has the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, and you can rent bikes. The Hangang Bus links the piers.
han-river-parks.why: A uniquely Seoul evening ritual and the city's big-river breathing space.
han-river-parks.autumn_note: October is the best month for river picnics. The Banpo fountain season normally ends Oct 31. Shows are usually 12:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00 (20 min each, based on 2025 pattern; verify).
han-river-parks.cost_note: Delivered chicken about 22,000-28,000 per bird. Bikes about 3,000 per hour.
han-river-parks.booking: Order chicken through Coupang Eats or Baemin to a 'delivery zone' (배달존), or buy at the convenience stores in the park.
han-river-parks.tips: Banpo for the fountain. Yeouido for the biggest lawn. Ttukseom near Seongsu.

hangang-bus.name: Hangang Bus (Han River water bus)
hangang-bus.area: Magok – Mangwon – Yeouido – Apgujeong – Oksu – Ttukseom – Jamsil
hangang-bus.summary: River commuter ferry launched Sept 18, 2025. It was partly suspended in late 2025 (groundings), then resumed in 2026. 603,293 riders by Sept 2026 and 99.3% on time in July 2026. Seoul plans 15-minute intervals, express and cross-river routes.
hangang-bus.why: A cheap, scenic river cruise between neighborhoods, like a Sumida River water bus.
hangang-bus.time_needed: Yeouido-Jamsil about 75 min. Full Magok-Jamsil about 2 h (verify).
hangang-bus.hours: One 2026 source listed Jamsil→Yeouido departures 10:00-17:30 and Magok→Yeouido 10:20-17:40, daily. Check the current timetable on hgbus.co.kr before going.
hangang-bus.closed: Suspended in fog, high water or strong wind
hangang-bus.cost_note: Adult 3,000. Covered by the Climate Card (기후동행카드) for an add-on fee (verify for the short-term tourist card).
hangang-bus.booking: Walk-up with a T-money or credit card. Seating is limited (about 199 seats), so arrive early on weekends.
hangang-bus.tips: Ride Yeouido → Apgujeong or Ttukseom to link the parks with Garosu-gil or Seongsu.

cheonggyecheon-ddp.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream and Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
cheonggyecheon-ddp.summary: An 11 km restored urban stream walk from Cheonggye Plaza east, ending at Zaha Hadid's DDP with its night LED rose garden or light shows and the late-night Dongdaemun fashion malls.
cheonggyecheon-ddp.why: A free night walk through the city, similar to Shibuya's mix of design and nightlife.
cheonggyecheon-ddp.autumn_note: The Seoul Lantern Festival on Cheonggyecheon is usually Nov-Dec, so it falls after the trip.
cheonggyecheon-ddp.hours: 24 h. The DDP building is about 10:00-20:00.
cheonggyecheon-ddp.tips: Walk from Gwanghwamun to Gwangjang Market along the stream.

hanbok-rental.name: Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung
hanbok-rental.summary: Dozens of rental shops near Gyeongbokgung station and Anguk. Hairstyling and accessories are extra.
hanbok-rental.why: Like a yukata or kimono rental in Kamakura or Kyoto. It also gets you into all palaces and Jongmyo free.
hanbok-rental.autumn_note: Autumn colors make for strong palace photos. Cool weather is comfortable in the layers.
hanbok-rental.cost_note: About 15,000-30,000 for 2-4 h basic. Premium 40,000-70,000. Hair about 5,000-15,000.
hanbok-rental.booking: Walk-in, or book on Creatrip, Klook or Naver for discounts
hanbok-rental.tips: Return times are strict. Choose a shop near the palace you will visit.

sparex-dongdaemun.name: Jjimjilbang: SPAREX Dongdaemun
sparex-dongdaemun.summary: 24-hour jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse and sauna) with gender-separated baths, themed sauna rooms and a shared lounge. It is the most central 24 h option now that Dragon Hill Spa, Itaewon Land and Siloam at Seoul Station have closed.
sparex-dongdaemun.why: The bathhouse culture that onsen lovers will enjoy. The atmosphere is urban, not nature.
sparex-dongdaemun.autumn_note: Good after a cold night walk.
sparex-dongdaemun.tips: Tattoo rules are relaxed compared with Japan. Bathing is nude and gender-separated. The shared lounge needs the provided clothes.

suwon-hwaseong.name: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (day trip)
suwon-hwaseong.summary: UNESCO-listed 1796 fortress with a 5.7 km wall loop, gates, Banghwasuryujeong pavilion and the rebuilt Hwaseong Haenggung palace. Haenggung-dong has cafes and the famous Suwon galbi.
suwon-hwaseong.why: A 'Kamakura-like' heritage day out from the capital: a walkable wall town with good food.
suwon-hwaseong.autumn_note: The Hwaseong Cultural Festival (Oct 4-11, 2026) and the media art event (to Oct 6) END before arrival. Foliage on the wall around Paldalsan is good late Oct.
suwon-hwaseong.hours: Haenggung about 09:00-18:00. The wall is open all the time.
suwon-hwaseong.cost_note: Fortress about 1,000 + Haenggung 1,500-2,000 (verify). Flying Suwon balloon about 20,000 and the Hwaseong trolley about 4,000 (2025-era prices, verify).
suwon-hwaseong.tips: Subway Line 1 from Seoul Station to Suwon is about 1 h. ITX or Mugunghwa trains take about 30 min. Bus 3000 runs from Gangnam. Suwon galbi: Bon Suwon Galbi or Yeonpo Galbi.

dmz-tour.name: DMZ tour (Imjingak, 3rd Tunnel, Dora Observatory)
dmz-tour.summary: Licensed group tours to Imjingak, the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory and Dorasan station. JSA (Panmunjom) civilian tours have been suspended since July 2023. Only special-category groups resumed, and general public and foreigner JSA tours are NOT running as of 2026.
dmz-tour.why: A history counterweight to the trip.
dmz-tour.autumn_note: Clear October skies give the best views from Dora Observatory.
dmz-tour.hours: Tours depart about 07:00-08:00 from central Seoul
dmz-tour.closed: Mondays (the 3rd Tunnel closes; some tours swap in the 2nd Tunnel). Also national holidays or military situations.
dmz-tour.cost_note: Standard DMZ tours about 55,000-95,000 per person. Be wary of anything sold as 'JSA'; some substitute a JSA museum.
dmz-tour.booking: Book 1+ week ahead via Klook, Viator, GetYourGuide or Creatrip. Passport required on the day.
dmz-tour.tips: Go Tue-Sat. Avoid tours that promise JSA. Pairs with the War Memorial.

nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.name: Nami Island + Garden of Morning Calm (Gapyeong day trip)
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.summary: Nami Island is a tree-lined river island, famous for its metasequoia and ginkgo lanes and the K-drama 'Winter Sonata'. The Garden of Morning Calm (37.7440, 127.3530) is a large garden in the hills.
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.why: Autumn foliage in a nature setting, an easy rail trip from Seoul.
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.autumn_note: Ginkgo and metasequoia lanes usually peak late Oct to early Nov. It is very crowded on weekends.
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.cost_note: Nami admission including the ferry about 16,000. Garden about 11,000-12,000. ITX-Cheongchun Yongsan or Cheongnyangni → Gapyeong about 8,000-9,600 one way (verify).
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.booking: Walk-up. Weekday ITX seats via Korail (letskorail.com).
nami-gapyeong-morning-calm.tips: Go on a weekday. Taxi from Gapyeong station to Nami wharf about 5 min. The zipwire is optional (about 50,000).

haeundae-blueline-park.name: Haeundae Blueline Park (Beach Train & Sky Capsule)
haeundae-blueline-park.summary: 4.8 km former Donghae Nambu Line rail along the cliffs between Mipo and Songjeong, converted into a slow sea-view Beach Train (all seats face the sea) and an elevated two-car Sky Capsule track (Mipo-Cheongsapo, 2 km, about 30 min one way).
haeundae-blueline-park.why: Direct analog to Kamakura's Enoden coastal train: little train, sea on one side, small fishing harbors (Cheongsapo, Gudeokpo) and cafes at each stop.
haeundae-blueline-park.autumn_note: October is off-season pricing/hours; clear autumn air and sunset light over Haeundae. Sky Capsule Oct hours 08:30-18:30.
haeundae-blueline-park.time_needed: 2-3 hours including a walk around Cheongsapo
haeundae-blueline-park.hours: Sky Capsule (Mar/Apr/Oct): 08:30-18:30. Beach Train roughly 09:30-19:00 in autumn (check traintime page).
haeundae-blueline-park.closed: Operates daily; suspended in strong wind/rain.
haeundae-blueline-park.cost_note: Official 2026 fares: Sky Capsule per capsule 2p 50,000 / 3p 55,000 (18,300 pp) / 4p 60,000 one way. Beach Train one-way 8,000-10,000 (by station), 2 rides 14,000, all-day pass 16,000 pp. For 3: capsule Mipo->Cheongsapo 55,000 + Beach Train back 3x10,000 = ~85,000 total.
haeundae-blueline-park.booking: bluelinepark.com (English site); Sky Capsule sells out on weekends - book online ahead (reported release every Tuesday 07:00 for 4 weeks ahead). Foreign cards generally accepted; Klook/KKday also resell.
haeundae-blueline-park.tips: Do Sky Capsule one way (Mipo->Cheongsapo) and walk/Beach Train onward to Cheongsapo Daritdol Skywalk and Songjeong. Pair with Haedong Yonggungsa (taxi 10 min from Songjeong).

cheongsapo-skywalk.name: Cheongsapo & Daritdol Skywalk
cheongsapo-skywalk.summary: Small fishing village with twin red/white lighthouses, grilled-clam shacks and a glass-floor skywalk over the sea; a stop on the Blueline Beach Train.
cheongsapo-skywalk.why: Feels like Koshigoe/Shichirigahama on the Enoden: small port, sea views, slow cafes.
cheongsapo-skywalk.autumn_note: Good sunset spot; grilled shellfish (jogae-gui) season.
cheongsapo-skywalk.tips: Jogae-gui (grilled shellfish) shacks: roughly KRW 50,000-70,000 for a platter for 2-3 (unverified 2026).

huinnyeoul-village.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
huinnyeoul-village.summary: White-walled houses and narrow lanes on a sea cliff with a coastal walking path below (Jeoryeong coastal road).
huinnyeoul-village.why: Small-streets-by-the-sea charm (Kamakura/Enoshima back alleys) with cafes facing anchored ships; calmer than Gamcheon.
huinnyeoul-village.autumn_note: Afternoon light; pair with Taejongdae cliffs and Yeongdo eomuk (fish cake) shops.
huinnyeoul-village.tips: Residents live here - keep quiet. Samjin Eomuk HQ is nearby in Bongnae-dong.

gamcheon-village.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
gamcheon-village.summary: Pastel hillside refugee-era village turned art village with staircases, murals and harbor views.
gamcheon-village.why: Colorful hillside lanes; more Instagram than temple-town but fills the 'charming streets' itch.
gamcheon-village.autumn_note: Fine in any weather; very crowded weekends.
gamcheon-village.tips: Go early; combine with Jagalchi Market lunch.

abai-village.name: Abai Village & gaetbae raft
abai-village.summary: Sandbar village built by North Korean refugees in 1950-51; reached by a hand-pulled cable raft (gaetbae) across the harbor channel; known for Abai sundae and Hamgyeong-style naengmyeon.
abai-village.why: Small-streets fishing-village charm with a quirky little ride - a Kamakura-like half day with Naksansa.
abai-village.autumn_note: October is squid/fish season on the east coast; Sokcho market at its liveliest.
abai-village.tips: Eat at Dancheon Sikdang (Abai sundae) then cross to Sokcho Jungang Market for Manseok dakgangjeong.

gangneung-anmok-gyeongpo.name: Gangneung: Anmok Coffee Street, Gyeongpo & Ojukheon
gangneung-anmok-gyeongpo.summary: Beachfront line of roasteries (Korea's coffee capital), Gyeongpo lake and beach, Ojukheon (birthplace of Yulgok and Sin Saimdang, Joseon hanok).
gangneung-anmok-gyeongpo.why: Small seaside city with culture: closest to Kamakura's mix of beach + heritage houses, plus tofu village (Chodang) like Kamakura's local specialties.
gangneung-anmok-gyeongpo.autumn_note: Gangneung Coffee Festival is traditionally in October (2026 dates not verified). Gyeongpo lake reeds and Ojukheon black bamboo in fall light.
gangneung-anmok-gyeongpo.tips: Gangneung is 1h50 from Seoul by KTX; Jeongdongjin (station on the beach) 15 min by train.

tongyeong-dongpirang.name: Tongyeong: Dongpirang mural village & Hallyeosu cable car
tongyeong-dongpirang.summary: Harbor town ('Naples of Korea') with hillside mural lanes above Jungang market, cable car up Mireuksan over the Hallyeo archipelago.
tongyeong-dongpirang.why: Seaside small-streets and harbor food culture; strongest for food (oysters, chungmu gimbap).
tongyeong-dongpirang.autumn_note: Tongyeong oyster harvest begins around October (peak Dec-Feb).
tongyeong-dongpirang.time_needed: 1 day (2h10 by bus from Busan Seobu terminal)
tongyeong-dongpirang.closed: Cable car closed some Mondays/maintenance days (verify).
tongyeong-dongpirang.cost_note: Cable car round trip ~KRW 17,000 adult (pre-2026 price; verify).
tongyeong-dongpirang.tips: Better as a south-coast detour than a core stop on a 8-night first trip.

yeosu-hyangiram.name: Yeosu Hyangiram Hermitage
yeosu-hyangiram.summary: Hermitage wedged into a sea cliff with rock tunnels, facing the sunrise over the South Sea.
yeosu-hyangiram.why: Very Kamakura/Enoshima - cliff temple above the sea; Yeosu adds night harbor pojangmacha and sea cable car.
yeosu-hyangiram.time_needed: 2 hours (+40 min drive from Yeosu city)
yeosu-hyangiram.cost_note: Hermitage entry ~KRW 2,000 (pre-2026; may now be free).
yeosu-hyangiram.tips: Out of the way for a Seoul-Gyeongju-Busan route (Yeosu-Expo is 2h50 by KTX from Seoul).

jeju-seogwipo.name: Seogwipo (Jeju) coast & Olle trail 6/7
jeju-seogwipo.summary: Seaside town with waterfalls (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon), Lee Jung-seob art street, Olle market, coastal cliff walks.
jeju-seogwipo.why: Seaside + small-town streets, but more Izu/Okinawa than Kamakura; adds black pork.
jeju-seogwipo.autumn_note: October silver grass (eulsae) on Saebyeol/Ttarabi oreum; tangerines start ripening.
jeju-seogwipo.tips: Rank last for this trip: costs a flight day.

hongdae.name: Hongdae & Yeonnam-dong
hongdae.summary: University district with busking on Eoulmadang-ro, clubs, noraebang, photo booths, character shops; Yeonnam-dong's Gyeongui Line Forest Park for cafes and bars.
hongdae.why: Best Shibuya analog: youthful street energy, neon, late nights. Yeonnam = Shimokitazawa.
hongdae.autumn_note: Friday/Saturday nights busiest; pleasant outdoor drinking weather in October.
hongdae.cost_note: Free to wander; noraebang ~KRW 15,000-30,000/hour per room.
hongdae.tips: Hongik Univ. Station (Line 2/AREX) - direct AREX from Incheon Airport.

myeongdong-euljiro.name: Myeongdong night street food + Euljiro Nogari Alley
myeongdong-euljiro.summary: Neon shopping streets with evening food stalls; 10 min walk to Euljiro 3-ga's nogari (dried pollock) beer alley with plastic tables on the street.
myeongdong-euljiro.why: Shibuya-level crowds/neon (Myeongdong) + Omoide Yokocho-style drinking alley (Euljiro).
myeongdong-euljiro.autumn_note: Outdoor beer-alley season ends as nights get cold in November - late October is ideal.
myeongdong-euljiro.closed: Nogari alley bars often closed Sundays
myeongdong-euljiro.cost_note: Street snacks KRW 4,000-10,000; nogari + beer ~KRW 10,000-15,000 pp.
myeongdong-euljiro.tips: Myeongdong food is pricier/touristy; Gwangjang Market is better food value.

gangnam-station.name: Gangnam Station & COEX Starfield Library
gangnam-station.summary: Office-tower crossing district with massive foot traffic, big screens, restaurants; COEX Mall's two-story bookshelf atrium and K-pop square screens nearby.
gangnam-station.why: Visually closest to Shibuya Scramble (towers, screens, crowds) but less street-level fun.
gangnam-station.tips: Sushi Kanesaka Seoul is in the InterContinental Parnas next to COEX.

busan-seomyeon.name: Seomyeon & Jeonpo Cafe Street
busan-seomyeon.summary: Busan's downtown: neon streets, underground shopping, clubs, dwaeji gukbap alley, and Jeonpo's hip cafe street in old hardware-shop lanes.
busan-seomyeon.why: Busan's Shibuya; smaller but with better pork-soup culture.
busan-seomyeon.tips: Seomyeon dwaeji gukbap alley; Choryang milmyeon a few stops away.

spaland-centum.name: Spaland Centum City
spaland-centum.summary: Upscale hot-spring jjimjilbang inside Shinsegae Centum City with natural spring baths, outdoor foot bath and themed sauna rooms.
spaland-centum.why: Most accessible jjimjilbang experience for first-timers; clean and well signed.
spaland-centum.cost_note: Pre-2026 price ~KRW 20,000-23,000 weekdays, higher weekends; website down when checked Oct 2026 - verify it is operating.

osaek-carbonated-spring.name: Osaek Carbonated Hot Spring and Pulse Bath (at Greenyard)
osaek-carbonated-spring.hours: Hot spring 06:00-22:00. Jjimjilbang 06:00-21:00. Some sources say weekends run to 23:00.
osaek-carbonated-spring.price_krw: Spring only: 18,000 (13,000 for hotel guests, valid until 15:00 after check-out). Spring plus pulse bath or jjimjilbang: 28,000 (20,000 for guests). Room-only 'Special Offer' guests pay 12,000.
osaek-carbonated-spring.notes: Operating as of Oct 2026: the live listing notices (basement B2) and an Aug 24, 2026 visit report both show it running. Day visitors are welcome, and the hotel validates parking. A good soak after hiking Jujeongol.

seorak-waterpia.name: Seorak Waterpia (hot-spring water park and spa)
seorak-waterpia.hours: Day 10:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30). Night spa 18:00-20:30 (last entry 20:00). Hours vary by date, so check hanwharesort.co.kr.
seorak-waterpia.price_krw: Guest rate, low season (Oct 12-Dec 10, 2026): day pass 49,000 per adult; night spa 27,000. Public prices are higher; the summer combined ticket was 99,000. Included for 2 adults in Sorano's ALL INCLUSIVE room rate.
seorak-waterpia.notes: Sorano guests are NOT given free entry with a room-only rate. They get the guest discount, or buy the all-inclusive package. The package voucher can be issued before check-in at the front desk on the day of arrival.

seorak-cable-car.name: Seorak Cable Car (Sogongwon to Gwongeumseong)
seorak-cable-car.summary: 5-min ride (10 min round trip) to about 700 m near Gwongeumseong fortress. Two 50-passenger cabins run every 5 min when busy and every 10-15 min otherwise.
seorak-cable-car.why: The core view of the Seorak day; Biseondae can be walked while waiting for the printed boarding time.
seorak-cable-car.autumn_note: No senior discount Sep 19-Nov 15 2026 (peak season). Waits of 1-3 h at foliage peak.
seorak-cable-car.time_needed: 1.5-2 h including time at the top (the last car leaves only about 10-20 min at the top)
seorak-cable-car.hours: Set daily. Oct 7-8 2026: 08:30-17:30; Oct 9 (holiday): 08:00-17:30. Expect about 08:00/08:30-17:30 on Oct 19-23; check the homepage the day before.
seorak-cable-car.closed: Open every day; suspended in high wind or for safety checks (unused tickets refunded)
seorak-cable-car.cost_note: Adult (middle school and older) round trip 16,000; child 12,000; under 36 months free. No one-way tickets, no group discount. Full refund until 10 min before boarding; 20% fee after.
seorak-cable-car.booking: Same-day on-site sale only (1st-floor counter or kiosk); no advance reservation. Each ticket carries a boarding time. No per-person limit is published.
seorak-cable-car.tips: Take Sokcho city bus 7 or 7-1 to Seorak-dong; be at the counter by 08:00-08:30 on a weekday. Buy tickets, then walk Biseondae (about 1 h each way) and come back for the slot. The Sinheungsa lot (033-636-4050) is full before 08:00 on peak days.

heullimgol-reservation-2026.name: Heullimgol trail (reservation section, Nam-Seorak)
heullimgol-reservation-2026.summary: A 3.1 km one-way reservation section from the Heullimgol Visitor Center past Yeosim Falls, Deungseondae and Sibi Falls to Yongso junction. It continues untimed down Juongol to Osaek, about 6.2 km and 3.5-4 h in total.
heullimgol-reservation-2026.why: South Seorak's best foliage gorge walk.
heullimgol-reservation-2026.autumn_note: Reservations Oct 1-Nov 30 2026. October entry is 08:00-15:00 in hourly slots; November entry is 09:00-14:00.
heullimgol-reservation-2026.closed: Closed on the day in rain or strong wind; there are 22 rockfall-risk points with warning lights. No 2026 rockfall closure found.
heullimgol-reservation-2026.booking: reservation.knps.or.kr (Korean site): 5,000/day with about 1,000 per hour; up to 10 people per booking; online booking closes at 14:00 the day before; leftovers registered on site at the Heullimgol Visitor Center. Fine for entering without a booking: 200,000 KRW for a first offence, up to 500,000. The foreigner portal does not offer trail bookings.
heullimgol-reservation-2026.tips: Foreigners without a Korean phone should plan on on-site leftover registration on a weekday (high chance given the cap) or have the hotel or a Korean contact book. One-way only: no walking up from Osaek past Yongso junction. The trailhead has no parking.

juongol-osaek-outback.name: Juongol valley out-and-back from Osaek
juongol-osaek-outback.summary: Flat gorge path from Osaek village to Yongso Falls and back, about 3 km each way.
juongol-osaek-outback.why: The no-booking fallback with the same autumn colours.
juongol-osaek-outback.autumn_note: Peak usually in the last third of October.
juongol-osaek-outback.booking: None required; two-way walking allowed (only the Heullimgol section is reservation-only and one-way).
juongol-osaek-outback.tips: Do not continue past Yongso junction up toward Heullimgol (forbidden direction).

paradise-hotel-busan.name: Paradise Hotel Busan
paradise-hotel-busan.room_for_3: Deluxe (2 adults + 1 extra adult at 72,600 per night, max 1 extra; extra bed or sofa bed on request), or Premium Deluxe Ocean Twin (3 adults standard)
paradise-hotel-busan.price_note: LIVE official site busanparadisehotel.co.kr, 'SPECIAL DEAL' A-type (room plus UNLIMITED all-day Ocean Spa CIMER and outdoor ocean spa pool), prices include 10% tax and 10% service. Per room per night: Thu Oct 22: Deluxe City (main building) 459,800, Deluxe Ocean (new wing) 520,300, Deluxe Ocean-Terrace 556,600, Premium Deluxe Ocean Twin 750,200. Fri Oct 23: 508,200 / 580,800 / 605,000 / 798,600. Sat Oct 24: UNAVAILABLE ('예약불가') for every room type and view. 3rd adult: +72,600 per night, which includes Cimer and pool. Totals for 3: Deluxe City Thu+Fri 1,113,200; Deluxe Ocean Thu+Fri 1,246,300; Thu only 532,400. Booking.com and Agoda also show the hotel sold out on all of Oct 22, 23 and 24. Cancellation: free until 18:00 five days before arrival; after that 50% of one night until 18:00 the day before; after that 100% of one night. Member rate is about 2% lower.
paradise-hotel-busan.highlights: Answer on Cimer: YES, the Special Deal includes unlimited Cimer and outdoor ocean pool access for all guests (the 3rd adult's fee covers it too). The B-type adds breakfast; the C-type adds Lounge Paradise and sauna. The Oct spa closure day is Oct 28, after the trip.
paradise-hotel-busan.drawbacks: No Saturday Oct 24 night is available, so it can't be the drone-show-night base. Ocean-view rooms have a side view with no terrace.
paradise-hotel-busan.image_query: Paradise Hotel Busan Cimer ocean spa

ananti-busan-cove.name: Ananti at Busan Cove
ananti-busan-cove.room_for_3: Cabin S (70 m2, max 3) + extra guest 50,000 + extra bed 44,000 per night (both VAT included), official site only. On Booking all rooms are max 2, so 2 rooms would be needed there.
ananti-busan-cove.price_note: LIVE official ananti.kr room search: Oct 23-25 Cabin S Forest View from 551,000 per night (2-night average); Sat Oct 24 alone 661,000, so Fri is about 441,000. Cabin S Ocean View: 611,000 average, 721,000 on Sat. For 3 with an extra bed: Cabin S Forest Fri+Sat = 1,102,000 + 188,000 = about 1,290,000; Ocean View about 1,410,000. Whether the room rate includes VAT was not shown; the extra-person fees are stated as VAT-inclusive. Booking.com cross-check (per room, plus 10% tax, max 2): Fri Cabin B Forest 436,091; Fri Cabin S 531,965; Sat Cabin B Ocean 705,747; 2 rooms on Booking would cost about 2.5M or more. Booking cancellation: free before about Oct 16-18. Official site: the 'hotel cancellation policy' applies, with details not shown (a card guarantee is required).
ananti-busan-cove.highlights: The only shortlisted Busan hotel open on both Fri Oct 23 and Sat Oct 24.
ananti-busan-cove.drawbacks: Expensive. Water House / McQueen's Pool and sauna cost an extra 35,000 per adult per visit. Gijang is about 30-40 min from Gwangalli for the drone show. The Ocean Infinity Pool season ended (it was listed through mid-Oct).
ananti-busan-cove.image_query: Ananti at Busan Cove Cabin S balcony

hotel-nongshim.name: Hotel Nongshim (Hurshimchung)
hotel-nongshim.room_for_3: Deluxe Ondol Twin / Family Ondol Twin + extra bed; SOLD OUT
hotel-nongshim.price_note: LIVE official hotelnongshim.com: 'no rooms available for the selected period' for each of Oct 21-22, 22-23, 23-24 and 24-25 (and Oct 23-25). Booking.com: no availability Oct 22, 23 or 24. For reference, Nov 10 (official, tax and service included): Deluxe Ondol Twin 165,000, High Family Twin 240,000, extra bed 50,000 per night, breakfast 30,600 per adult. Spa rooms: free cancellation until 24:00 fourteen days before.
hotel-nongshim.highlights: Hurshimchung hot-spring bath next door; can still be used as a day trip (not a stay).
hotel-nongshim.drawbacks: Fully booked for the trip dates.

shilla-stay-haeundae.name: Shilla Stay Haeundae
shilla-stay-haeundae.price_note: LIVE Booking.com, 3 adults: Thu Oct 22 and Fri Oct 23 NO AVAILABILITY (Agoda also sold out for Oct 23-25). Sat Oct 24 only: Standard Family Twin 379,000 + 10% VAT (+ small city tax) = about 417,000; Deluxe Family Twin Ocean View 444,000 + 10% = about 488,000. Breakfast 28,000 per person. Free cancellation before Oct 21.
shilla-stay-haeundae.highlights: Could fill the Saturday night after Paradise on Thu/Fri.
shilla-stay-haeundae.drawbacks: Only Saturday is available. It is in Haeundae, so the Gwangalli drone show is a 15-20 min taxi away.

westin-josun-busan.name: The Westin Josun Busan
westin-josun-busan.area: Dongbaek Island end of Haeundae Beach
westin-josun-busan.room_for_3: Deluxe Twin ocean view with extra bed
westin-josun-busan.price_note: Hotelscombined snapshot Oct 12-13: 216,816-930,608 KRW; deluxe from 216,816. Estimate for 3 in an ocean-view room: 300k-550k.
westin-josun-busan.highlights: Classic beachfront property with views of both Haeundae and Gwangan Bridge, next to the Dongbaek Island walk and Nurimaru. 9.1/10.

signiel-busan.name: Signiel Busan
signiel-busan.room_for_3: Ocean-view Deluxe with extra bed, or a suite
signiel-busan.price_note: The only snapshot found is old (Oct 11-12 2024: from 244k; queen 497k; 2 people). Estimate for 3 in Oct 2026: 550k-900k. Low confidence and a budget stretch.
signiel-busan.highlights: Floor-to-ceiling sea views from a skyscraper, a top-rated spa, outdoor pool. 9.4/10.
signiel-busan.drawbacks: Most expensive option; city-luxury rather than ryokan in feel.

hotel-aqua-palace.name: Hotel Aqua Palace (Gwangalli)
hotel-aqua-palace.room_for_3: Family Ondol (non-renovated, no view) or Deluxe/Ocean City Twin (sleeps 3); no bridge-view family room was offered
hotel-aqua-palace.price_note: LIVE Booking.com: Thu Oct 22 only. Family Ondol or Deluxe Twin (no view) 188,182 + 10% = 207,000; Ocean City Twin (partial ocean view) 216,409 + 10% = 238,050. Free cancellation before Oct 19; breakfast 25,000. Fri Oct 23 and Sat Oct 24: NO AVAILABILITY.
hotel-aqua-palace.drawbacks: Sold out for the drone-show Saturday. Rated 7.2.

hound-hotel-gwangalli.name: Hound Hotel Gwangalli
hound-hotel-gwangalli.price_note: Could not verify a 2026 price (aggregator page gone). Rough estimate only.
hound-hotel-gwangalli.highlights: Modern budget-to-midrange chain; check for bridge-view rooms.

fairfield-songdo.name: Fairfield by Marriott Busan Songdo Beach
fairfield-songdo.room_for_3: Family rooms available; or twin plus extra bed
fairfield-songdo.price_note: Hotelscombined snapshot: from 151,498; King 327,328 (2 people). Estimate for 3 in a family room: 160k-330k.
fairfield-songdo.highlights: Sea views next to the Songdo cable car; convenient for Nampo, Jagalchi, Gamcheon and Yeongdo (Huinnyeoul/Taejongdae).
fairfield-songdo.drawbacks: Not in Haeundae: 40+ min to the Blueline Park side. 3-star.

stanford-tongyeong.name: Stanford Hotel & Resort Tongyeong
stanford-tongyeong.area: Donam-dong (near the cable car and Mireuksan)
stanford-tongyeong.room_for_3: Resort (condo-type) rooms with floor bedding and kitchenette; or a hotel twin plus extra bed
stanford-tongyeong.price_note: Hotelscombined snapshot: from 112,132 (superior, 2 people). Estimate for 3 in a sea-view resort room: 140k-280k.
stanford-tongyeong.highlights: Sea and island views, outdoor pool, 2.6 km from the cable car. 9.0/10. Good for an overnight Tongyeong stay with oysters.
stanford-tongyeong.drawbacks: Outside the old town; needs taxis.

haeundae-grand-hotel-closed.name: Haeundae Grand Hotel (CLOSED)
haeundae-grand-hotel-closed.price_note: Closed since end of 2018 / early 2019. The site was bought by MDM in 2020 for redevelopment (planned to become a Josun Palace-operated hotel). Do not book any listing using this name.

seongyojang-hanok-stay.name: Seongyojang Hanok Stay
seongyojang-hanok-stay.room_for_3: Haengrangchae 1-5 (servants' wing): 2 small ondol rooms (plus a loft in #1 and #2), sleeps 4, shared outdoor toilet and shower. Jungsarang (random allocation): 4 bedrooms with private bathroom, 4/6. Choga 1/2 (thatched cottage): 2 bedrooms, kitchen, private bathroom, 6/6. Yeonjidang heritage house: 3 rooms plus daecheong maru, shared bathroom, 6/6. Seobyeoldang heritage house: big room, small room and nu-maru pavilion, private bathroom, 4/6.
seongyojang-hanok-stay.price_note: Live on mom-mom (Yanolja), Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Mon-Thu: Haengrangchae 78k; Jungsarang 168k (not offered Thu Oct 22); Choga or Yeonjidang 191k; Seobyeoldang 281k (Mon only). Fri Oct 23 and Sat Oct 24: Haengrangchae 112k; Jungsarang 191k; Choga or Yeonjidang 225k; Seobyeoldang 315k. Extra persons above standard cost 15,000 each.
seongyojang-hanok-stay.highlights: Sleep inside a 300-year-old noble estate. The grounds are quiet after the day visitors leave. This is the strongest 'ryokan' stand-in for atmosphere, though it has no bath culture. Seobyeoldang or Choga give a private bathroom.
