seongyojang-hanok-stay.drawbacks: Check-in is 16:00 and check-out 10:00. Haengrangchae rooms share an outdoor bathroom, so pick Jungsarang, Choga or Seobyeoldang for privacy. Floor bedding (yo). No onsen.
seongyojang-hanok-stay.booking: mom-mom.net or Yanolja; phone 050-703-8155. The knsj.co.kr/seongyojang site was unreachable on Oct 6, 2026.

hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.name: Hanwha Resort Seorak Sorano
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.area: Nohak-dong (Seorak entrance), next to Seorak Waterpia
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.room_for_3: Deluxe (FAM) family condo sleeps 4 as standard (max 4-6 depending on listing), so 3 adults pay no extra-person fee (the fee is 10,000 per person above standard). The condo types have a kitchen; the hotel-type and Teenieping rooms do not.
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.price_note: Live on Oct 6, 2026 (mom-mom/Webtour and yeogi, 3 adults). Room-only Deluxe FAM/FTB/FTL: 192,000 Mon-Thu Oct 19-22, 226,000 Fri Oct 23, 296,000 Sat Oct 24. The '[10월][추캉스 ALL INCLUSIVE]' rate adds Waterpia day passes and Arte breakfast buffet for 2 adults: 227,000 on weekdays, 256,000 Fri, 316,000 Sat. A third Waterpia pass is 49,000 (guest low-season rate) and a third breakfast about 30,000 (guest rate; the walk-in price is 37,000).
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.highlights: The weekday all-inclusive rate is the best value in Gangwon: room, 2 Waterpia hot-spring day passes and 2 breakfasts for 227k. Waterpia is a hot-spring water park with outdoor baths and a night spa looking at Ulsanbawi. It is the closest big resort to Seoraksan's Sogongwon entrance.
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.drawbacks: Older condo buildings and a family or kid-heavy crowd, with breakfast queues reported. Waterpia closes at 17:00 (last entry 16:30); the night spa runs 18:00-20:30. Only 1 room was left at some rates.
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.booking: mom-mom.net (Webtour), yeogi.com (property 6426 '한화리조트 설악 쏘라노 본관'), or hanwharesort.co.kr directly. Mobile coupons for package passes arrive by KakaoTalk after check-in, or ask at the front desk before check-in.
hanwha-resort-seorak-sorano.image_query: Hanwha Resort Seorak Sorano Waterpia Ulsanbawi

lotte-resort-sokcho.name: Lotte Resort Sokcho
lotte-resort-sokcho.room_for_3: Hotel Deluxe or Grand Deluxe Family Twin (3/3), Condo Deluxe 18평 (3/3), Condo Family 23평 (4/4), and Junior Family Suite (4/4).
lotte-resort-sokcho.price_note: Live on mom-mom, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Regular rates (Webtour): hotel Deluxe Family Twin or condo Family 23평 at 341k Mon/Tue/Thu and 330k Wed, 422k Fri Oct 23, 578k Sat Oct 24. Yanolja 'Sunset Check-in' rates (18:00 in, 10:00 out, single night only): 218-274k on weekdays, 288k Fri, 377k Sat. A one-off 'super deal' Deluxe Family Twin was 235k on Wed Oct 21.
lotte-resort-sokcho.highlights: Every room has an ocean view, and the heated infinity pool sits over the sea. Oeongchi coastal walk.
lotte-resort-sokcho.drawbacks: The water park costs extra: 65,000 per adult, or 33,000 for the infinity pool only. Regular rates run 1.7x Sorano.
lotte-resort-sokcho.booking: mom-mom.net (Yanolja and Webtour listings), yeogi, Agoda, lotteresort.com.
lotte-resort-sokcho.image_query: Lotte Resort Sokcho infinity pool sea

kensington-hotel-seorak.name: Kensington Hotel Seorak
kensington-hotel-seorak.area: Seorak-dong, inside the park entrance zone (5-minute walk to the park gate)
kensington-hotel-seorak.room_for_3: Deluxe Ondol (standard 3, max 4), Premier Twin or Premier Family Twin (3/3), Executive (Family) Twin (3/3), and Korean, Western or Diana suites (4/4). Standard rooms take only 2.
kensington-hotel-seorak.price_note: Live on yeogi, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults, room only. Mon Oct 19: 359,900 (Deluxe Ondol). Tue Oct 20: every room for 3+ sold out. Wed Oct 21: 359,900. Thu Oct 22: 459,900 (only Executive Family Twin left). Fri Oct 23: 379,900. Sat Oct 24: 479,900 (Executive Twin, 1 left). The '속초 온천여행' package adds 20,000 and includes 2 Cheoksan Hot Spring tickets, a cable-car discount and a 10k hotel voucher. Breakfast packages add about 60-85k.
kensington-hotel-seorak.highlights: The only hotel inside the park zone: walk to Sinheungsa and the cable car before the day-trippers' traffic arrives. Its British-heritage theme gives it character.
kensington-hotel-seorak.drawbacks: The most expensive of the set, about 1.9x Sorano on weekdays. Inventory is nearly gone (1-2 rooms left on most dates), so book now or drop it.

sono-delpino.name: Sono Calm/Sono Belle Delpino
sono-delpino.room_for_3: Family or suite rooms (bed plus ondol); the condo units have kitchens.
sono-delpino.highlights: Head-on views of Ulsanbawi and an outdoor infinity pool (Ocean Play) looking at the rock face.
sono-delpino.drawbacks: Car needed, and far from the beach and city.

sol-beach-yangyang.name: Sol Beach Yangyang (Sono)
sol-beach-yangyang.room_for_3: Resort Family (with kitchen, beds) is 4/6 and Resort Suite is 5/8. Hotel Executive Family Twin is 4/5. Hotel Family Superior and Suite Deluxe are 2/3 (an extra-person fee may apply).
sol-beach-yangyang.price_note: Live on mom-mom, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Resort Family condo: 189-194k Mon-Thu, 234-240k Fri Oct 23, 326k Sat Oct 24 (the Sono-direct listing was sold out Saturday). Add 45k for the 'Water-ful' package (2 water-park passes) or 59k for breakfast for 2. Hotel Executive Family Twin: 245-251k weekdays, 284-301k Fri, 387k Sat.
sol-beach-yangyang.highlights: Mediterranean-style beachfront, about 10 minutes to Naksansa for sunrise. The condo kitchen helps keep costs down.
sol-beach-yangyang.drawbacks: Kitschy styling, and you need a car or taxi. It is 25-30 minutes from the Seorak entrance.
sol-beach-yangyang.image_query: Sol Beach Yangyang resort Naksan beach

seamarq-gangneung.name: Seamarq Hotel Gangneung
seamarq-gangneung.room_for_3: Deluxe rooms take 3 with an extra bed (charged), or book a suite. The Hotel Hyundai annex (Hanok? No: the low-rise wing) has family rooms.
seamarq-gangneung.price_note: Estimate: Gangneung's most expensive hotel. Ocean-view rooms run about 400-550k on weekdays and up to 800k on weekends, plus about 50-80k for an extra bed. Not verified.
seamarq-gangneung.highlights: Richard Meier design, an infinity pool on the sea, and a sauna. The most luxurious stay on the coast.
seamarq-gangneung.drawbacks: Expensive, and too costly for a 3-person under-$1,000 budget if used for more than one night.

skybay-gyeongpo.name: Skybay Hotel Gyeongpo
skybay-gyeongpo.room_for_3: Most twins are set up for 2, with a max of 3: the 3rd person costs 22,000 per night, paid at the hotel. '[3인 전용]' Deluxe or Executive Twin rates already include the 3rd guest. Deluxe Family Twin is 4/4.
skybay-gyeongpo.price_note: Live on yeogi, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Executive Twin (ocean view) Goodchoice rate: 233-248k Mon-Thu, plus 22k for the 3rd person, so about 255-270k. '[3인 전용]' Deluxe Twin (pine or lake view): 300,300 on weekdays and Fri. Fri Oct 23: cheapest Deluxe about 256k + 22k = 278k. Sat Oct 24: about 323k + 22k = 345k, and 3-person-only Deluxe 343-373k. The rooftop infinity pool costs extra, unless you take the '인피니티풀 2인 포함' rate (+50k).
skybay-gyeongpo.highlights: The 20th-floor infinity pool looks over Gyeongpo beach and the lake. The hotel sits between the sea and Gyeongpo Lake.
skybay-gyeongpo.drawbacks: In-room jacuzzis are not available. The sauna costs 15,000 and closes the first Wednesday of each month. It is big and busy.

st-johns-gangneung.name: St. John's Hotel Gangneung
st-johns-gangneung.room_for_3: Superior Twin (2/3) and Superior Family Twin (2/4): extra guests stay free up to the room maximum, with extra bedding at 22,000 per night. Superior Bunk Twin is 4/4.
st-johns-gangneung.price_note: Live on yeogi (member price) and mom-mom, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Superior Twin (no ocean view): 138-155k Mon-Thu, 176k Fri Oct 23, 267k Sat Oct 24. Partial-ocean Gorgeous Twin: 148-182k weekdays, 206k Fri, 298k Sat. Bunk Twin (4/4): 215-253k weekdays and Fri, 377-385k Sat. Budget about 22k more for proper 3rd bedding.
st-johns-gangneung.highlights: The best-value big hotel on the beach. It is a walk to Chodang sundubu village and Gangmun beach, and has a year-round heated Pine infinity pool.
st-johns-gangneung.drawbacks: A huge, busy property. The Ocean infinity pool is summer-only. Rooms are not cleaned on 2-night stays (towels and water are still supplied). The pool costs extra.
st-johns-gangneung.image_query: St John's Hotel Gangneung Gangmun beach

woljeongsa-templestay.name: Woljeongsa Templestay (Odaesan)
woljeongsa-templestay.room_for_3: Shared ondol rooms by gender. Three adults of mixed gender may be split.
woljeongsa-templestay.price_note: About 70-90k per person per night including temple meals, so roughly 210-270k for 3 people. Based on typical 2024-25 rates; not verified.
woljeongsa-templestay.highlights: The 4am chanting, monk-led tea, the fir-forest walk at dawn, and vegetarian temple food.
woljeongsa-templestay.drawbacks: Very basic floor bedding, strict hours, and alcohol forbidden.

osaek-greenyard.name: Osaek Greenyard Hotel
osaek-greenyard.area: Osaek, Seo-myeon (at the Jujeongol trailhead, 647 m elevation)
osaek-greenyard.room_for_3: Hotel Deluxe 25평 (3/3), Hotel Family 30평 (4/4), Grand Family 35평 (5/5). Extra persons cost 20,000 each.
osaek-greenyard.price_note: Live on mom-mom (Yanolja) and yeogi, Oct 6, 2026, 3 adults. Deluxe 25평 'Special Offer' (room only, random room assigned): 123-130k Mon-Thu, 189k Fri Oct 23. Regular Deluxe: 159-163k weekdays. The '온캉스' package with onsen and jjimjilbang included: about 205k weekdays, or 287k Fri for a Family 30평. Sat Oct 24: SOLD OUT on both platforms.
osaek-greenyard.highlights: Korea's only carbonated-alkaline compound spring (renovated Apr 2024), at the foot of Jujeongol gorge, the classic Seorak foliage valley. It is the nearest thing to a mountain onsen hotel and the cheapest Seorak base.
osaek-greenyard.drawbacks: Dated rooms. The signature carbonated pool is cool, not hot (you sit about 5 minutes until bubbles form), so it feels unlike a Japanese onsen. The hotel is 25-30 minutes from Sokcho, and buses are sparse.
osaek-greenyard.booking: mom-mom.net, yeogi.com (property 7362), phone +82-33-670-1004. greenyard.co.kr did not respond on Oct 6, 2026.

ragung.name: Gyeongju Ragung Hotel (Lagung)
ragung.room_for_3: All 16 suites are base 2 / max 4, with 1 double bed + 1 futon (ondol). The 3rd adult pays 30,000 KRW on site. Extra bedding is 25,000 KRW if available. No extra beds.
ragung.price_note: LIVE Yanolja, Oct 6, 2026, Wed Oct 21 for 3 adults: Suite Madang-type 170,000 (2 left) or Suite Numaru-type 170,000 (2 left), Royal Suite (indoor hot-spring bath) 240,000 (1 left). Add 30,000 for the 3rd adult on site, so 200,000 / 270,000 for 3, plus 25,000 if a 3rd bedding set is wanted. The cheaper 'walk-in special' (165,000; surcharge if arriving by car) is sold out. Tue Oct 20, Thu Oct 22, Mon Oct 19 and Fri Oct 23 are ALL SOLD OUT. Free cancellation until Oct 14 17:00. No breakfast is sold (reviews say it was suspended). Drip-bag coffee is included.
ragung.highlights: Confirmed operating in 2026: 901 Yanolja reviews (4.6), including Jul 2026 and '3 days ago'. Every suite has a private hot-spring bath (outdoor; the Royal Suite also has an indoor one), with slippery-soft onsen water, warm ondol rooms and a hanok courtyard. This is the closest Korean analog to the Izu ryokan. Bookable in English via NOL World (world.nol.com NC-11074).
ragung.drawbacks: Only Wed Oct 21 is available, with 5 rooms left. No breakfast or dinner, unlike a Japanese ryokan. Some reviews mention poor soundproofing, stiff doors and some dust in the outdoor tub. Needs a taxi or bus from Gyeongju Station or downtown (about 15-20 min). Kakao rating 3.3 (9 ratings) vs Yanolja 4.6 (901).

gurume-resort.name: Gurume Resort (Andong hanok resort)
gurume-resort.area: Andong Folk Village area, near Woryeonggyo

rakkojae-hahoe.name: Rakkojae Hahoe (Andong)

rakkojae-hahoe.drawbacks: Expensive; remote (bus 246 or taxi ~30,000 KRW from Andong Station).

jirye-artists-colony.name: Jirye Artists' Colony

jirye-artists-colony.highlights: Remote lakeside head-family house, very quiet; traditional meals on request.
jirye-artists-colony.drawbacks: Needs car/taxi; no public transport; limited English.

hakindang.name: Hakindang
hakindang.room_for_3: Ondol rooms in a 1908 aristocrat's house; some take 3-4

hakindang.highlights: Historic designated hanok with garden; most refined stay in Jeonju.
hakindang.drawbacks: Floor bedding; shared walls; limited rooms.

lahan-hotel-jeonju.name: Lahan Hotel Jeonju
lahan-hotel-jeonju.highlights: Modern hotel with rooftop/hanok-village views; easy fallback if hanok stays are full.

templestay-golgulsa.name: Golgulsa Templestay (Sunmudo)
templestay-golgulsa.room_for_3: Shared ondol dorm/rooms on floor mats, generally gender-separated; a mixed group of 3 friends can ask for one room
templestay-golgulsa.price_note: For 3 people: ~70,000-90,000 KRW per adult per night incl. temple meals (typical 2025 rates for experience/relaxation programs; not verified 2026).

templestay-bulguksa.name: Bulguksa Templestay
templestay-bulguksa.price_note: ~70,000-100,000 KRW pp/night typical; mainly weekend programs; not verified 2026.

templestay-bulguksa.drawbacks: Programs mostly Sat-Sun and Korean-language; book early.

templestay-haeinsa.name: Haeinsa Templestay

templestay-haeinsa.drawbacks: Out of the way between Gyeongju and Jeonju.

templestay-beomeosa.name: Beomeosa Templestay
templestay-beomeosa.highlights: Easiest templestay to reach by transit; good if trip includes Busan.

templestay-naksansa.name: Naksansa Templestay
templestay-naksansa.highlights: Seaside cliff temple (Hongnyeonam), sunrise over East Sea; pairs with Seoraksan foliage (peak forecast ~Oct 25 2026 per weatheri).
templestay-naksansa.drawbacks: Opposite side of the country from Gyeongju/Andong/Jeonju.

podo-hotel.name: Pinx Podo Hotel

grand-josun-jeju.name: Grand Josun Jeju

skypark-central-myeongdong.name: Hotel Skypark Central Myeongdong

oakwood-premier-coex.name: Oakwood Premier Coex Center

mercure-ambassador-hongdae.name: Mercure Ambassador Seoul Hongdae

ragung-gyeongju.name: Ragung Hanok Hotel

ananti-cove.name: Ananti at Busan Cove

rakkojae-andong.name: Rakkojae Andong Hahoe

seongyojang.name: Seongyojang Hanok Stay
seongyojang.room_for_3: Ondol rooms in a 300-year-old aristocratic manor; some rooms fit 3-4.
seongyojang.highlights: Authentic yangban manor with lotus pavilion; affordable heritage stay near Gyeongpo/Chodang.

hanwha-seorak-sorano.name: Hanwha Resort Seorak Sorano + Seorak Waterpia
hanwha-seorak-sorano.room_for_3: Condo-style family rooms with kitchenette (bed + floor bedding).
hanwha-seorak-sorano.price_note: Estimate; late October is Seorak foliage peak - weekends spike and sell out.
hanwha-seorak-sorano.highlights: Seorak hot-spring water park/spa (outdoor hot spring baths with Ulsanbawi view), 15 min to Seoraksan.

cheoksan-hotspring-hotel.name: Cheoksan Hot Spring Resort (rooms)
cheoksan-hotspring-hotel.area: Nohak-dong, Gwangwang-ro 327 (about 10 minutes' drive from the Seorak entrance)
cheoksan-hotspring-hotel.room_for_3: Twin (3/4), Ondol (4/5), Ondol Family (3/4, check-in from 18:00), Twin Family (3/4), Hwangto Ondol (4/5). The KTO listing says rooms have private tubs fed with natural hot-spring water. Extra persons cost 15,000 each.

kolon-gyeongju.price_note: LIVE Yanolja Oct 6, 2026: OPEN. Wed Oct 21, Premier Super Twin 171,000 room-only, 194,000 with breakfast for 2 + sauna for 2, or 271,000 with breakfast for 4. Premier Ondol (renovated 2025) 193,000 + 11,000 for the 3rd person. Oct 20 from 122,000; Oct 22 from 194,000. Breakfast 45,000 per adult.
kolon-gyeongju.highlights: Confirmed operating; walk to Bulguksa at dawn; 'Moonlight pocha' terrace with unlimited beer and makgeolli 19,900.
kolon-gyeongju.drawbacks: Far from downtown night sights; sauna 22,000 (50% off for guests).

nine-tree-dongdaemun.name: Nine Tree by Parnas Seoul Dongdaemun
nine-tree-dongdaemun.area: Euljiro 4-ga / Dongdaemun (224 Eulji-ro), 2 subway stops from Jongno and Myeongdong
nine-tree-dongdaemun.room_for_3: Family Room (twin + full), sleeps 3 adults, 1 room
nine-tree-dongdaemun.price_note: LIVE Booking.com, Oct 16-21 (5 nights, 3 adults): 315,662 average per night before tax = 1,578,310 + 10% = 1,736,141 total (about 347k per night). With breakfast: 439,109 per night before tax. Free cancellation before Oct 13, 2026; no prepayment.
nine-tree-dongdaemun.highlights: A live, budget-fitting replacement for Nine Tree Myeongdong 2 (same brand, has a true family room for 3). Location rated 9/10 (1,626 reviews).
nine-tree-dongdaemun.drawbacks: Dongdaemun/Euljiro rather than Jongno. Prices for Oct 17-21 alone were not checked separately.
nine-tree-dongdaemun.image_query: Nine Tree Premier Dongdaemun family room

4rest-stay-jongno.name: 4rest Stay Jongno
4rest-stay-jongno.room_for_3: Deluxe Suite or Family Suite, max 3, breakfast included
4rest-stay-jongno.price_note: LIVE Booking.com, Oct 16-21 (5 nights, 3 adults): Deluxe Suite 1,475,638 with taxes (non-refundable), or 340,491 per night + 10% = 1,872,701 (free cancellation before Oct 9, 2026). Family Suite: 1,586,696 non-refundable.
4rest-stay-jongno.highlights: Rated 9.1, location 9.5. Walk to Changdeokgung, Insadong and Ikseon-dong.
4rest-stay-jongno.drawbacks: Small property. The refundable rate's cancellation deadline is Oct 9, which is soon.

the-prima-jongno.name: The Prima Hotel Jongno Insadong
the-prima-jongno.price_note: LIVE Booking.com, Oct 16-21 (5 nights, 3 adults): Deluxe Twin 383,835 per night + 10% = 2,111,093 total (free cancellation before Oct 9); Triple 429,895 per night + 10% = 2,364,423.
the-prima-jongno.highlights: Best location among the live options (9.6), walking distance to Gyeongbokgung.
the-prima-jongno.drawbacks: About 0.4M more than Nine Tree Dongdaemun.

gwangalli-planet16.name: Gwangalli-Planet16 (Planet 16 Gwangan Hotel)
gwangalli-planet16.room_for_3: Deluxe Triple Room with Sea View (twin + full), max 3, 1 room
gwangalli-planet16.price_note: LIVE Booking.com, Fri Oct 23 to Sun Oct 25 (2 nights, 3 adults): 183,379 per night = 366,758 + 10% tax = 403,434 total. Free cancellation before Oct 20. Single nights (Thu, Fri or Sat alone) were NOT bookable, which suggests a 2-night weekend minimum.
gwangalli-planet16.highlights: Rated 9.4, location 9.8. Walk to the Gwangalli M Drone Light Show on Sat Oct 24. The cheapest live 3-person Busan option for Fri+Sat.
gwangalli-planet16.drawbacks: 'Sea view' is the listing's wording; whether you can see Gwangan Bridge from the room is not confirmed. No spa or onsen (pair it with a Cimer, Hurshimchung or Spa Land day visit).
gwangalli-planet16.image_query: Gwangalli beach hotel sea view triple room

jagalchi-hoe.name: Jagalchi Market hoe (pick-your-fish sashimi upstairs)
jagalchi-hoe.why: Freshest raw fish, the closest substitute for sushi omakase. Autumn: jeon-eo (gizzard shad), flatfish.

millak-raw-fish-centre.name: Millak Raw Fish Town / Millak Waterfront
millak-raw-fish-centre.why: Hoe with a Gwangan Bridge view, before or after the drone show.

haeundae-amso-galbi.name: Haeundae Amso Galbi
haeundae-amso-galbi.booking: Long waits; go at opening (about 11:30) or late
haeundae-amso-galbi.why: Legendary marinated cow-beef galbi, a decades-old Haeundae institution.

geumsu-bokguk.name: Geumsu Bokguk (Haeundae flagship)
geumsu-bokguk.why: Busan's classic hangover-cure breakfast; a refined, Japanese-adjacent dish (fugu).

milmyeon.name: Gaya Milmyeon or Choryang Milmyeon
milmyeon.why: Busan-only noodle dish born of wartime refugees.

ssiat-hotteok-eomuk.name: BIFF Square ssiat hotteok and eomuk (fish cake)
ssiat-hotteok-eomuk.why: Iconic Busan street snacks. Samjin Eomuk's Yeongdo flagship is near Huinnyeoul.

cheongsapo-jogaegui.name: Cheongsapo grilled clam shacks
cheongsapo-jogaegui.why: Seaside clam barbecue at the end of the Sky Capsule ride.

tongyeong-oysters-chungmu-gimbap.name: Tongyeong oysters and Chungmu gimbap (e.g., Ttungbo Halmae Gimbap)
tongyeong-oysters-chungmu-gimbap.why: Fresh oyster season opens in October; oyster dishes plus Tongyeong's signature gimbap.

manseok-dakgangjeong.name: Manseok Dakgangjeong
manseok-dakgangjeong.booking: Walk-in; takeaway boxes about 20,000-25,000 KRW for a medium box.
manseok-dakgangjeong.why: The single most famous Sokcho snack.

abai-sundae.name: Abai Village sundae and Hamheung naengmyeon (e.g. Danchon Sikdang, Sinda Sinda)
abai-sundae.type: North Korean refugee food: stuffed-squid sundae, cold noodles
abai-sundae.why: This food is the heritage of the refugee village.

bongpo-meoguri.name: Bongpo Meoguri Jip
bongpo-meoguri.type: mulhoe (spicy cold raw-fish soup) and seafood bowls
bongpo-meoguri.booking: Walk-in, with a long lunch queue.
bongpo-meoguri.why: The Sokcho classic for fresh raw fish, a casual counterpoint to sushi omakase.

dongmyeong-red-crab.name: Red snow crab (hongge) restaurants at Dongmyeong port, or the Jungang market basement fish floor
dongmyeong-red-crab.type: steamed red snow crab, sashimi cut to order
dongmyeong-red-crab.booking: Walk-in. Prices are by weight, so ask first.
dongmyeong-red-crab.why: The closest experience to an omakase-style seafood splurge. Autumn is crab season.

chilsung-shipyard-cafe.name: Chilseong Shipyard (cafe in a 1952 wooden-boat shipyard)
chilsung-shipyard-cafe.why: A hip industrial-heritage café on the lake.

terarosa-sacheon.name: Terarosa Coffee factory (Gujeong)
terarosa-sacheon.why: Gangneung is Korea's coffee town, and this is the pilgrimage roastery.

gangneung-jungang-market.name: Gangneung Jungang Market & Wolhwa Street (night market)
gangneung-jungang-market.type: market: dakgangjeong, crab croquettes, mulhoe, hotteok
gangneung-jungang-market.why: Lively evening grazing near Gangneung Station.

odaesan-sanchae.name: Odaesan mountain-vegetable set meals (Sanchae jeongsik) by Woljeongsa, e.g. Odaesan Sikdang / Bibong Sikdang
odaesan-sanchae.why: Healthy, seasonal food in the spirit of temple cuisine.

yangyang-songi.name: Yangyang pine mushroom (songi) dishes, e.g. songi hot pot or grilled songi with hanu beef
yangyang-songi.why: Korea's matsutake. The season runs through mid to late October, depending on rain. Prices vary hugely, and raw songi can cost 100,000+ KRW/kg.

yoseokgung.name: Yoseokgung
yoseokgung.type: Royal/aristocratic hanjeongsik course in a hanok next to the Choi family house
yoseokgung.booking: Reserve by phone/Naver; recommended for dinner
yoseokgung.why: Closest to a ryokan kaiseki dinner: many small seasonal dishes in a hanok, then walk to lit Woljeonggyo.

dosol-maeul.name: Dosol Maeul
dosol-maeul.type: Home-style hanjeongsik in a hanok yard
dosol-maeul.why: Great-value Korean set meal near Daereungwon.

gyochon-gimbap.name: Gyori Gimbap
gyochon-gimbap.booking: Walk-in; sells out, often closed Wed (low confidence)

hwangnam-ppang.name: Hwangnam-ppang (original shop)
hwangnam-ppang.why: Classic Gyeongju souvenir/snack, like Kamakura's hato sable.

andong-jjimdak-alley.name: Andong Jjimdak Alley (Andong Gu-sijang)
andong-jjimdak-alley.type: Braised soy-garlic chicken with glass noodles
andong-jjimdak-alley.why: Andong's must-eat; one large + one half portion suits 3.

kkachigumeongjip.name: Kkachigumeongjip
kkachigumeongjip.type: Heotjesabap (mock ancestral-rite meal) and salted mackerel
kkachigumeongjip.why: Andong Confucian-culture food before the night bridge walk.

gajok-hoegwan.name: Gajok Hoegwan
gajok-hoegwan.area: Jungang-dong (10 min walk from Hanok Village)

samcheon-makgeolli.name: Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley
samcheon-makgeolli.type: Makgeolli kettle with ever-growing anju spread
samcheon-makgeolli.why: Izakaya-like evening; each kettle brings more side dishes.

dombedon.name: Dombedon
dombedon.why: Classic black-pork grill, sets 59,000 (2 ppl) to 88,000 (3 ppl); 11:00-23:00 daily. Kagoshima kurobuta analog.

donsadon.name: Donsadon
donsadon.why: Famous thick-cut pork grilled on charcoal; ~KRW 25,000-30,000 per serving (2025-era, unverified 2026).

geumdonga.name: Geumdonga
geumdonga.why: Staff direct-flame grilling, sets/platters KRW 52,000-65,000; 11:00-22:30; near Saebyeol/Arte Museum.

myeongjin-jeonbok.name: Myeongjin Jeonbok
myeongjin-jeonbok.why: East-loop lunch near Bijarim; abalone stone-pot rice ~KRW 16,000-20,000 (unverified 2026).

ujin-haejangguk.name: Ujin Haejangguk
ujin-haejangguk.why: Iconic Jeju breakfast before an early flight.

jamae-guksu.name: Jamae Guksu
jamae-guksu.why: Jeju's signature noodle dish; average bowl KRW 12,000-15,000 (2026).

negeori-sikdang.name: Negeori Sikdang
negeori-sikdang.why: Seogwipo hairtail specialist; braised whole silver hairtail is the group dish (price unverified 2026).

haenyeo-house-seongsan.name: Village haenyeo houses (e.g., Seongsan Ilchulbong haenyeo-ui-jip)
haenyeo-house-seongsan.type: haenyeo-caught seafood: abalone porridge, sea urchin, octopus, conch
haenyeo-house-seongsan.why: Raw-seafood-by-the-sea experience; the closest Jeju analog to sushi omakase freshness.

noryangjin-hoe.name: Noryangjin market sashimi dinner (pick live fish, eat upstairs)
noryangjin-hoe.why: The best substitute for sushi omakase. Autumn jeoneo (gizzard shad) and daeha (prawns) are in season.

mingles.name: Mingles (modern hansik, Michelin 3-star)
mingles.booking: Catchtable or the restaurant site, weeks ahead. Price is approximate and unverified for 2026.
mingles.why: The omakase-style splurge in Korean form: a chef's tasting menu built on jang (fermented sauces).

onjium.name: Onjium (Joseon court cuisine research kitchen)
onjium.booking: Catchtable. Hard to get. Price approximate.
onjium.why: Seasonal Joseon court cuisine above the palace wall, a kaiseki analog.

gwangjang-crawl.name: Gwangjang Market crawl: Soonhee-ne bindaetteok, Buchon Yukhoe, mayak gimbap

mongtan.name: Mongtan (straw-fired galbi, Korean BBQ)
mongtan.why: The most famous BBQ in Seoul. Near the War Memorial.

tosokchon.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
tosokchon.why: A classic warming dish after Gyeongbokgung or Inwangsan.

myeongdong-kyoja.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
myeongdong-kyoja.why: An iconic, cheap and quick Myeongdong meal.

jinokhwa-dakhanmari.name: Jinokhwa Halmae Wonjo Dakhanmari
jinokhwa-dakhanmari.why: Communal hotpot (a whole chicken for about 30,000, shared). Good for a cool night.

chimaek-hangang.name: Chimaek picnic at a Han River park
chimaek-hangang.area: Yeouido, Banpo or Mangwon Hangang Park
chimaek-hangang.booking: Delivery app or nearby chicken shop
chimaek-hangang.why: A uniquely Seoul ritual. October weather is ideal.

suwon-galbi.name: Suwon galbi (Bon Suwon Galbi or Yeonpo Galbi)
suwon-galbi.booking: Walk-in, or a Naver reservation for Bon Suwon
suwon-galbi.why: The day-trip meal on a Suwon visit.

sosuheon.name: Sosuheon
sosuheon.type: sushi omakase - high (2 Michelin stars 2026, new)
sosuheon.booking: Phone +82 10-9694-3368 (self-managed; Korean-speaking; ask hotel concierge). 8 seats.
sosuheon.why: Seoul's only 2-star sushi counter (2026), in a hanok - the closest to a top Tokyo omakase. Chef Park Kyung-jae (ex-Sushi Kojima). Dinner ~KRW 500,000 (Korean report; lunch price not found).

sushi-kanesaka-seoul.name: Sushi Kanesaka Seoul
sushi-kanesaka-seoul.type: sushi omakase - high (1 Michelin star 2026, new)
sushi-kanesaka-seoul.booking: Phone 02-559-7627 or hotel site; all seats pre-booked; 9 seats. Lunch 12:00 (LO 12:30), dinner 18:00 (LO 20:00); Saturday dinner two seatings 17:30/20:00.
sushi-kanesaka-seoul.why: Official 2026 prices: lunch KRW 230,000-280,000, dinner KRW 330,000-380,000 (depends on chef). Edomae lineage of Ginza Kanesaka; hotel booking is easiest for foreigners.

sushi-matsumoto.name: Sushi Matsumoto
sushi-matsumoto.why: Japanese chef Mizuho Matsumoto (ex-Sushi Cho); traditional Edomae with strong tsumami. 2026 price not found (₩₩₩₩ tier; expect ~KRW 250k+ lunch / 350k+ dinner).

sushi-cho.name: Sushi Cho (The Westin Josun Seoul)
sushi-cho.booking: Westin Josun website or phone; English-speaking hotel staff.
sushi-cho.why: Classic hotel sushi counter, easiest high-end booking for foreigners. Reported dinner omakase KRW 340,000, lunch ~KRW 140,000+ (aggregator, date unclear).

sushi-chohi.name: Sushi Chohi
sushi-chohi.why: Value counter: lunch from KRW 45,000, dinner from KRW 110,000 (2026 article).

sushi-jinsu.name: Sushi Jinsu
sushi-jinsu.why: Lunch omakase KRW 45,000 with free corkage (2026 blog).

sushi-sora.name: Sushi Sora (Gwanghwamun / Mapo / Daechi / Seocho)
sushi-sora.why: Reliable entry-level counter: lunch KRW 50,000-60,000, dinner KRW 100,000-110,000 (list date unclear; likely 2024-25).

iwa-busan.name: Iwa
iwa-busan.why: Chef holds a patent for fish aging; best value Michelin-listed omakase in Busan. Lunch ~KRW 80,000; dinner ₩₩₩.

sushi-nee-busan.name: Sushi Nee (L7 Haeundae)
sushi-nee-busan.why: Lunch KRW 60,000, dinner KRW 110,000; parties up to 7 - easy for 3.

sushi-ima-busan.name: Sushi Ima
sushi-ima-busan.why: One of Busan's top sushi counters; dinner KRW 180,000.

mori-busan.name: Mori
mori-busan.booking: Phone +82 51-731-9889 (CatchTable also reported). Dinner Tue-Fri 19:00, Sat-Sun 17:00; closed Mon.
mori-busan.why: Kaiseki by a Japan-trained Korean chef and his Japanese wife using Busan seafood - the best substitute for an Izu ryokan dinner. Prix fixe ~KRW 250,000 (reported).

born-and-bred.name: Born and Bred
born-and-bred.type: hanu (Korean beef) omakase / BBQ - Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best 2026 #56
born-and-bred.booking: Basement chef's tasting via CatchTable, 2-3 months ahead; phone +82 2-2294-5005. Closed Tue.
born-and-bred.why: The sushi-omakase experience translated to hanu: counter, chef-paced cuts. Chef's tasting KRW 380,000; 2F a la carte ~KRW 70,000/150g sirloin.

umok.name: Umok
umok.why: Counter hanu omakase KRW 99,000 (room 180,000) - Dec 2024 prices, likely higher now.

bicena.name: Bicena
bicena.why: Korean tasting 81 floors up - pair with Seoul Sky. Lunch ~KRW 170,000 (third-party).

kwonsooksoo.name: Kwonsooksoo
kwonsooksoo.why: Traditional-leaning Korean fine dining with jang and banchan focus; from ~KRW 200,000+ (third-party).

le-dorer-busan.name: Le DORER
le-dorer-busan.why: Busan's newly starred Korean tasting menu (chef Kim Chang-uk); price not verified.

noryangjin.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
noryangjin.type: hoe (raw fish) market - buy downstairs, eat upstairs
noryangjin.why: Tsukiji-style experience: pick live fish, have it sliced, eat at a 2F restaurant (sangcharim setting fee ~KRW 5,000-6,000 pp). Aug 2026 farmed flatfish KRW 22,800/kg wholesale; seasonal moksum platters ~KRW 50,000 for 2. In Oct: daeha prawns, kkotge, jeoneo.

jagalchi.name: Jagalchi Market
jagalchi.why: Korea's biggest fish market: buy on 1F, eat on 2F (table fee ~KRW 5,000 pp). Hoe platter for two ~KRW 30,000-60,000 (2026). Overcharging controversies in 2024-25 - agree price per kg first; go past the first row of stalls.

millak-raw-fish-center.name: Millak Fishermen's Live Fish Market
millak-raw-fish-center.why: Buy fish on 1F, eat upstairs facing Gwangan Bridge's light show - the best hoe night in Busan. Flatfish ~KRW 30,000/kg; 2-person set ~KRW 40,000-45,000; setting fee ~KRW 6,000 pp (recent blogs).

gijang-daebyeon.name: Daebyeon Port / Gijang Market
gijang-daebyeon.type: seafood (anchovy, sea-squirt, grilled eel, Gijang snow crab tanks)
gijang-daebyeon.why: Small port near Haedong Yonggungsa for hoe and grilled kkomjangeo (hagfish) - fishing-village lunch like Kamakura's Koshigoe shirasu. Gijang market sells (mostly imported/red) crab year-round.

gwangjang-market.name: Gwangjang Market (bindaetteok, yukhoe, mayak gimbap)
gwangjang-market.why: Seoul's essential food market: mung-bean pancakes (Soonhee-ne ~KRW 5,000-6,000), beef tartare (Buchon Yukhoe, Michelin Bib), makgeolli. Avoid stall price-gouging (some 2023-24 controversies).

geumdwaeji.name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
geumdwaeji.why: Cult samgyeopsal/ribs over briquettes - the Korean BBQ benchmark.

euljiro-nogari.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley / Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha
euljiro-nogari.why: Plastic-stool tent bars - the Korean answer to yokocho/izakaya alleys.

ssangdungi-gukbap.name: Ssangdungi Dwaeji Gukbap
ssangdungi-gukbap.why: Busan's signature comfort food. Michelin Bib alternatives: Jeongjitgan (Saha-gu). Price estimate ~KRW 10,000-12,000.

gaegeum-milmyeon.name: Gaegeum Milmyeon
gaegeum-milmyeon.why: Classic milmyeon (Michelin Bib in past editions). Price estimate.

samjin-eomuk.name: Samjin Eomuk (Yeongdo flagship)
samjin-eomuk.why: Busan fish-cake institution since 1953; croquette-style eomuk. Pair with Huinnyeoul village.

biff-ssiat-hotteok.name: BIFF Square ssiat hotteok stalls
biff-ssiat-hotteok.why: Fried pancake stuffed with brown sugar and seeds - Busan's iconic street snack, next to Jagalchi.

hwangnam-bread.name: Hwangnam Bread (main shop)
hwangnam-bread.why: Since 1939; Gyeongju's omiyage (like Kamakura's hato sable). Box of 20 ~KRW 20,000 (pre-2026).

gyori-gimbap.name: Gyori Gimbap
gyori-gimbap.why: Famous egg-heavy gimbap near Woljeonggyo bridge.

chodang-halmeoni-sundubu.name: Chodang Halmeoni Sundubu
chodang-halmeoni-sundubu.why: Seawater-set tofu, a Gangneung specialty; Donghwa Garden next door does jjamppong sundubu. Price estimate.

dancheon-sikdang.name: Dancheon Sikdang
dancheon-sikdang.why: Classic Abai-village sundae shop (featured on 1 Night 2 Days). Price estimate.

jeonju-makgeolli-alley.name: Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley
jeonju-makgeolli-alley.why: Order a kettle (~KRW 20,000-30,000/table) and dishes keep coming - Jeonju's izakaya equivalent.

jeju-black-pork.name: Donsadon / Sukseongdo (Jeju black pork)
jeju-black-pork.why: Jeju black pork - only if Jeju is in the plan. Price estimate.

gwangalli-m-drone-light-show-forest-s-me.name: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show: 'Forest's Melody'
gwangalli-m-drone-light-show-forest-s-me.dates: Sat Oct 24 2026 (also Oct 17 'Dimensional Station' with lasers)

dongnae-eupseong-history-festival.name: Dongnae Eupseong History Festival (32nd)
dongnae-eupseong-history-festival.notes: Reenactment of the 1592 Battle of Dongnae Fortress, Dongnae tug-of-war, held near Oncheonjang (Hurshimchung). Overlaps only Oct 17-18, which are probably Seoul days.

jeonpo-coffee-festival.name: Jeonpo Coffee Festival
jeonpo-coffee-festival.notes: Only useful if they start the trip in Busan.

lalala-festival.name: LaLaLa Festival (10th)
lalala-festival.notes: Listed on a festival calendar; venue and content unverified.

busan-jagalchi-festival.name: Busan Jagalchi Festival
busan-jagalchi-festival.notes: Seafood festival at Korea's biggest fish market. The closest Busan analog to a Tsukiji-style seafood morning. Overlaps only if they are in Busan Oct 17-18.

gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.name: Gyeongbokgung Starlight Night Walk (foreigner-only sessions)
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.dates: Program runs Sep 2 - Oct 24 2026 (Wed-Sun, paused Sep 30 - Oct 4). Oct 21 (Wed), 22 (Thu), 23 (Fri), 24 (Sat) are FOREIGN VISITORS ONLY.
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.times: Two sessions nightly: 18:30 and 19:40 (approx. 2 hours). Route: Sojubang royal kitchen (royal-style dosirak meal), Jibokjae, Hyangwonjeong pavilion, with traditional music/performance.
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.cost: Not confirmed for 2026. 2024-2025 price was KRW 60,000 pp including the royal meal; assume about KRW 60,000.
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.booking: Korean sessions were a lottery (Aug 14-20 2026) run by the Korea Heritage Agency (kh.or.kr). The foreigner-session booking channel for 2026 is unconfirmed. In past years foreigner sessions were sold first-come through Interpark's global site (now NOL World). Check kh.or.kr and NOL World now; seats are tiny in number and may already be gone.
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.notes: This is the best palace night program during the trip, and its foreigner dates fall exactly inside it. It is the closest thing to a ryokan-style kaiseki evening in a historic setting. The Gyeongbokgung general night opening (Sep 2 - Oct 2) and the Changdeokgung Moonlight Tour foreigner nights (last one Oct 11) are both over before the trip.
gyeongbokgung-starlight-night-walk.confidence: high (dates and foreigner-only nights from the official royal palace calendar); low (price and foreigner booking channel)

changgyeonggung-mulbit-yeonhwa-night-med.name: Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' night media-art (autumn)
changgyeonggung-mulbit-yeonhwa-night-med.times: Evening, around Chundangji pond (exact session times not captured; palace is open until 21:00)
changgyeonggung-mulbit-yeonhwa-night-med.cost: Not confirmed. Expect palace admission KRW 1,000 plus possibly a program fee.
changgyeonggung-mulbit-yeonhwa-night-med.booking: Reservation opened Sep 11 2026 at 11:00 (Korea Heritage Agency/NOL Ticket). Foreigner access unconfirmed; check for remaining or cancelled slots.
changgyeonggung-mulbit-yeonhwa-night-med.notes: Media-art light show reflected in Chundangji pond and the glasshouse (Daeonsil). It pairs well with an evening at Changgyeonggung, which is open to 21:00 anyway.

gyeongbokgung-saenggwabang-royal-tea-des.name: Gyeongbokgung Saenggwabang royal tea & dessert program (autumn)
gyeongbokgung-saenggwabang-royal-tea-des.dates: Sep 2 - Oct 26 2026, daily except Tuesdays (palace closure day)
gyeongbokgung-saenggwabang-royal-tea-des.cost: 2025 price was about KRW 15,000 pp (2026 not confirmed)
gyeongbokgung-saenggwabang-royal-tea-des.booking: Lottery Aug 13-20 2026, then remaining or cancelled seats on NOL Ticket. Foreigners can try NOL Ticket for leftover seats.
gyeongbokgung-saenggwabang-royal-tea-des.notes: Royal-court teas and traditional sweets inside Gyeongbokgung. A daytime analog of a Japanese tea-house experience.

deoksugung-night-at-seokjojeon.name: Deoksugung 'Night at Seokjojeon' (autumn)
deoksugung-night-at-seokjojeon.dates: Sep 9 - Oct 18 2026, Wed-Sun. Only Sat Oct 17 and Sun Oct 18 fall in the trip.

tips: [busan] Best fit for the Kamakura feel: base 2-3 nights in Haeundae or Gwangalli. Spend one day on Dalmaji-gil, the Sky Capsule to Cheongsapo, the Beach Train to Songjeong and Haedong Yonggungsa; one day on Yeongdo (Huinnyeoul and Taejongdae), Jagalchi, Gukje Market and the Songdo cable car; Igidae plus Gwangalli at night.
[busan] Put Busan late in the trip (e.g., Oct 21-24) so you catch the drone show on Sat Oct 24 at Gwangalli, then take a late-morning KTX to Seoul and AREX to ICN on Sun Oct 25 for the 21:55 flight.

[busan] For the onsen-ryokan analog, choose between Paradise Hotel Busan (Cimer outdoor sea-view hot spring, in the city) and Ananti Cove (Water House, quiet clifftop resort). Hotel Nongshim plus Hurshimchung is the budget onsen-town option, with no sea view.
[busan] Book the Sky Capsule the moment your date opens; weekdays are far easier. One capsule fits all 3 (55,000 KRW).
[busan] Use Naver Map or KakaoMap (Google Maps walking directions are weak in Korea) and Kakao T for taxis. A T-money card covers the metro, buses and the Donghae Line.

[busan] Budget sketch for Busan per person: 3 nights at about 350k KRW per night for 3 = about 350k each; activities (Sky Capsule + Beach Train + cable car + spa + X the Sky) about 90k; transport within Busan about 30k; KTX Seoul-Busan return about 120k. Total about 590k KRW, roughly US$410-420 at about 1,400 KRW/USD (exchange rate is an assumption).

[events] No Korean public holidays fall in Oct 16-25 2026. Nearby holidays: Chuseok Sep 24-26 (substitute Mon Sep 28), National Foundation Day Sat Oct 3 (substitute Mon Oct 5), Hangul Day Fri Oct 9. Expect normal weekday crowds and weekend peaks on Oct 17-18 and 24-25.

[events] Weekly closures to plan around: Gyeongbokgung TUE (Oct 20); Jongmyo TUE (Oct 20); Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung MON (Oct 19); Leeum MON; National Museum of Korea open every day in the window (late nights Wed and Sat to 21:00). Good Monday plan: Gyeongbokgung + Bukchon + NMK. Good Tuesday plan: Changdeokgung Huwon + Changgyeonggung + Deoksugung.
[events] Best special program in the window: Gyeongbokgung Starlight Night Walk foreigner-only nights Wed Oct 21 - Sat Oct 24 (18:30 / 19:40). Check booking immediately.
[events] Seoul Eulalia Festival (Haneul Park) Oct 17-23 and Mapo Naru Shrimp Festival (Oct 16-18) are next to each other; Sun Oct 18 is the ideal combo day (jet-lag friendly, outdoors, free).
[events] Wear hanbok for free entry to all palaces and Jongmyo.
[events] Gwangalli drone show is Saturdays only: Oct 17 or Oct 24, at 19:00 and 21:00. Plan the Busan leg to include a Saturday night if possible.
[events] Gangneung Coffee Festival Oct 21-25 is the event to anchor a Gangwon coast leg (Gangneung is about 2 h by KTX from Seoul Station; Sokcho/Seoraksan about 1 h north by bus).
[events] Banpo Moonlight Rainbow Fountain runs until Oct 31 (12:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00). Sunday Oct 18/25 adds the car-free Jamsu Bridge festival underneath.
[events] Hahoe Village and Andong are quiet after the Maskdance Festival (ended Oct 4). Andong is still worth it for the village and Byeongsan Seowon, not for events.

[foliage] Put the Gangwon mountains (Seoraksan, Odaesan) on weekdays Mon Oct 19-Thu Oct 22: that is where peak color will be during the trip, and weekdays avoid cable-car sellouts and expressway jams.
[foliage] Order that matches the color front: Odaesan first (peak ~Oct 16-20), then Seoraksan valleys (Oct 20-27), then Gapyeong/Hwadam (Oct 23-25+).
[foliage] Use Seoul's Haneul Park silver grass festival (Oct 17-23, open until 21:00) for an easy jet-lag-day activity on arrival day or an evening.
[foliage] For Seorak Cable Car: be at the ticket booth at opening, take the printed boarding time, and hike to Biseondae (1 h each way) while waiting.
[foliage] Hwadam Botanic Garden must be booked online in advance for Oct 23-25 (no on-site tickets); book entry and monorail together.
[foliage] Temple admission fees at Sinheungsa, Woljeongsa, Bulguksa, Haeinsa etc. have been free since May 2023, so foliage hikes cost almost nothing except transport and cable cars.
[foliage] KNPS autumn wildfire-prevention trail closures normally start Nov 15 (to Dec 15), so they do not affect Oct 17-25; individual high-ridge sections can still close for weather.
[foliage] Check real-time foliage at KMA's 'famous mountain foliage' observation page and the KNPS/Seoraksan live cams the evening before each mountain day.
[gangwon] Do Seorak on a weekday. Mon Oct 19 to Fri Oct 23 is ideal, with peak color and far fewer jams than Sat/Sun.
[gangwon] For Seorak, buy cable car tickets first, then hike Biseondae while waiting for your assigned boarding time.
[gangwon] The best 'Kamakura' day is Naksansa at sunrise or morning, then Hajodae, Hyuhyuam and the Jukdo/Ingu surf cafés, ending at Sokcho's Jungang market.

[gangwon] The best 'onsen' substitutes nearby are Cheoksan Hot Spring (an outdoor bath in the pines, nude, single-sex) or Seorak Waterpia (outdoor hot-spring pools, swimsuit). Neither is a true ryokan. The Seongyojang hanok stay is the traditional-lodging pick.

[gangwon] Suggested 3-night east-coast loop: Seoul to Gangneung by KTX (2 h). Gangneung for one night (Gyeongpo, Ojukheon, Seongyojang, Anmok, Chodang). Bus to Sokcho or Yangyang for two nights (Naksansa, Seorak on a weekday, market). Then either bus back to Seoul, or return to Gangneung and take the KTX-Eum 09:36 down the coast to Gyeongju or Busan.
[gangwon] Odaesan fits as a stop between Seoul and Gangneung: get off the KTX at Jinbu, walk the fir path, and continue to Gangneung the same evening.

[gangwon] Transport for 3 people over this segment is roughly: KTX Seoul to Gangneung 27,600, bus Gangneung to Sokcho about 7,500, local buses and taxis about 30,000, and either bus Sokcho to Seoul about 25,000 or KTX-Eum Gangneung to Gyeongju 34,300. That is under about 100,000 KRW per person.
[gangwon] Admissions are cheap: Seorak, Naksansa and Woljeongsa are free since 2023. The cable car (16,000) is the main paid item, plus small fees at Ojukheon (3,000) and Seongyojang (5,000).
[heritage] Best Izu-ryokan analog: one night at Ragung (private outdoor hot-spring bath in every hanok suite). Pair with a downtown hanok (Hwangnamguan) night so you can walk the lit sites.
[heritage] Gyeongju night loop (all walkable, ~2.5 km): Daereungwon -> Cheomseongdae -> Gyerim -> Woljeonggyo/Gyochon -> Donggung & Wolji. Wolji closes entry 21:30.
[heritage] Bulguksa/Seokguram: go at 09:00 on a weekday (Mon-Thu), not Saturday. Both free.

[heritage] Andong works as a train-linked add-on: Seoul Cheongnyangni -> Andong (KTX-Eum ~2 h) -> Gyeongju (KTX-Eum ~1 h), or reverse. Saturday Oct 24 julbul fire show in Hahoe is the autumn highlight if the itinerary allows Andong on the final Saturday (but return flight is Sun 21:55 from ICN, ~4 h by train+AREX from Andong).
[heritage] Use Kakao T for taxis (foreign cards accepted); taxis are cost-effective split three ways for Bulguksa, Golgulsa and Yangdong.

[jeju] Weather (Jeju City normals): October mean high 21.6°C / low 15.7°C, 95 mm rain over ~6.7 days, 173 h sunshine; late October trends cooler and windier. Bring a windbreaker; Hallasan plateau is ~8-10°C colder.
[jeju] Silver grass (eoksae) on Saebyeol, Sangumburi, Ttarabi and Yongnuni peaks mid-Oct to early Nov - the trip dates are prime.
[jeju] Tangerine picking is open in October but fruit is still greenish; fully orange orchards from mid-November.

[jeju] Drive clockwise on a 2-3 day loop: west (Saebyeol, Arte Museum, Sanbangsan/Yongmeori, hot spring) -> south (Jusangjeolli, Olle 7, Seogwipo market) -> east (Seongsan sunrise, Udo, Bijarim, haenyeo).
[jeju] Without a car: base in Seogwipo (south) and Jeju City; use limousine 600/800 + taxis + one 8-h taxi tour day (~KRW 164,000-200,000 per car).
[jeju] If arriving from Busan, PUS-CJU is ~1 h; leave Jeju to GMP on Sat Oct 24 evening (or a Sun Oct 25 morning flight, giving ~10 h buffer before the 21:55 ICN departure).

[jeju] Rough 2-night Jeju cost per person: flights KRW 120,000-220,000 + car/taxi KRW 90,000-150,000 + lodging KRW 140,000-200,000 + admissions/hot spring KRW 40,000-60,000 = KRW 390,000-630,000 (≈US$280-450 at ~KRW 1,400/US$).

[logistics] KTX/SRT merged on Sep 1 2026: SRT brand is gone (trains now 'KTX-Sancheon'), fares cut ~10% on high-speed routes (Seoul-Busan 59,800 -> 54,400), and Seoul, Yongsan and Suseo departures are all searchable in one app, Korail+ (renamed Korail Talk). The SRT app/website closed Aug 31 2026.

[logistics] From Oct 1 2026 Korail tickets go on sale 2 months before departure at 07:00 (was 1 month). As of Oct 6 every train for Oct 17-25 is already bookable: buy now, especially Saturday/Sunday trains and the 3-a-day Donghae Line KTX-Eum.

[logistics] Foreigners: book on korail.com (English 'foreigner' reservation) or Korail+ app in English. Overseas cards sometimes fail at 3-D Secure or ask for a Korean phone number; fall back to korail.com desktop, station ticket counters/machines, or resellers (Trip.com, Klook, 12Go, LACHA) that accept foreign cards for a small markup. Korail says Visa/Master/UnionPay plus WeChat/Alipay support is being developed.
[logistics] Korail+ lets you cancel free within 10 minutes of purchase; after that small fees apply, rising close to departure.
[logistics] Rail fares for the likely itinerary per person: Seoul->Gyeongju 44,500 + Gyeongju->Busan 10,100 + Busan->Seoul 54,400 = 109,000 KRW (~US$81). For 3 people ~327,000 KRW (~US$244).

[logistics] Dawn arrival (05:15 Sat Oct 17): booking the night of Oct 16 so the room is ready at ~07:00 is the reliable option for 3 jet-lagged adults. Without it, ask the hotel for luggage drop + early check-in (rarely guaranteed before 12:00-15:00 on a Saturday).

[logistics] Getting into Seoul at dawn: a taxi (~65,000-80,000 total incl. tolls, ~US$17-20 each) is door-to-door and as cheap as 3 AREX Express tickets plus a subway/taxi transfer. AREX all-stop (~4,750) is the budget option.
[logistics] Air Premia is understood to use Incheon Terminal 1. Confirm on the e-ticket/app the week of travel, since several carriers changed terminals in 2025-2026.

[logistics] Last day (21:55 departure Sun Oct 25): Air Premia does not participate in Seoul Station City Airport Terminal check-in, so bags travel with you. Leave bags at the hotel (free) and pick up, or use T-Luggage lockers/counters (Seoul Station, Myeongdong, Hongdae, Jongno 3-ga, Jamsil, Suseo, Gimpo; 09:00-22:00; ~6,000-13,000 KRW per large bag). Leave central Seoul by ~17:30 to be at T1 by ~19:00.

[logistics] T-Luggage also delivers bags from Seoul stations to Incheon airport (listed as T2) for 20,000 KRW weekday / 29,000 KRW weekend per bag; book a day ahead (cancellations after 18:00 the day before are non-refundable). Check if T1 delivery is offered for Air Premia.
[logistics] Busan luggage: ZimCarry (Busan Station based, 1544-8215) offers storage, hotel/station delivery and KTX luggage shipping; handy on the Busan travel day.

[logistics] Transit cards: a T-money card (3,000-5,000 KRW at convenience stores) works on subways, buses and many taxis nationwide (Seoul, Busan, Gyeongju, Gangneung). WOWPASS is a prepaid debit card with built-in T-money, top-up by foreign card or cash machine; good for foreigners whose cards fail in Korean apps. Top up T-money with cash only at machines/convenience stores.

[logistics] Seoul subway base fare is 1,550 KRW (card) since mid-2025; buses ~1,500. Seoul's Climate Card tourist pass (unlimited Seoul subway/bus, roughly 1-day 5,000 to 7-day 20,000 KRW plus card) only pays off on heavy-transit Seoul days and does not cover AREX to Incheon; T-money/WOWPASS is simpler for this itinerary.
[logistics] Foreign credit cards (Visa/Mastercard; Amex less so) are accepted almost everywhere, including taxis and markets; carry some cash for street food and small market stalls.
[logistics] Taxis: Kakao T accepts foreign phone numbers and overseas cards; Kakao's English app k.ride and Uber also work in Seoul and Busan. Seoul taxi base fare is 4,800 KRW.
[logistics] Maps: use Naver Map (English UI) or Kakao Map for walking/transit directions; Google Maps lacks walking/driving directions in Korea. Papago for translation (camera mode for menus).
[logistics] Restaurant reservations: CatchTable Global (English, foreign phone and card OK) is the main way to book omakase/fine dining as a foreigner; Naver booking often needs a Korean number.

[logistics] eSIM/data: get a tourist eSIM (KT/SKT/LG U+ or Airalo-type, roughly 25,000-45,000 KRW for 8-10 days unlimited) or a physical tourist SIM with a Korean number if you want Kakao T/CatchTable verification and delivery apps.

[logistics] Entry: US citizens are K-ETA-exempt through Dec 31 2026, so no K-ETA is needed for Oct 17. Instead each traveler must file the free Korea e-Arrival Card online (e-arrivalcard.go.kr) within 3 days before arrival (paper cards were replaced from Jan 1 2026). Optional: a K-ETA (10,000 KRW, valid 3 years, k-eta.go.kr only) replaces the e-Arrival Card and covers future 2027+ trips.
[logistics] Tipping is not customary in Korea (restaurants, taxis, hotels); service charges are included at upscale hotels.

[logistics] Tax refunds: look for 'Tax Free' stores; immediate refund at the register for purchases of 15,000-under 1,000,000 KRW per receipt (up to ~5,000,000 KRW total per trip), show passport. Larger purchases: refund kiosks at Incheon before security.

[logistics] No public holidays fall on Oct 17-25 2026 (Chuseok was Sep 24-26; Hangul Day Oct 9), but autumn foliage weekends make Saturday/Sunday trains and buses to Gangneung/Sokcho and Gyeongju busy.

[seoul] Where to base: Jongno (Anguk, Insadong, Jongno 3-ga, Ikseon-dong) is the best single base for these travelers. You can walk to Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Jongmyo, Bukchon, Ikseon-dong, Gwangjang and the Jongno-3ga or Euljiro nightlife. Book 1-2 nights in a Bukchon hanok (Rakkojae) as the ryokan analog, then move to a 2-bedroom serviced residence (Somerset Palace) or a Myeongdong/Euljiro hotel. If they want nightlife over culture, base at Hongdae instead, which has a direct AREX all-stop train.

[seoul] For the 05:15 Saturday arrival: AREX or a limousine bus runs from about 05:15-05:40. Booking the Oct 16 night means the room is ready at 07:00. Otherwise leave bags at the hotel or at Seoul Station lockers or T-Luggage and start at Gwangjang or Noryangjin for breakfast (Noryangjin's live section runs 24 h).

[seoul] Plan around closing days. MONDAY Oct 19: Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung, Leeum, the War Memorial and Namsangol are closed, and DMZ tours skip the 3rd Tunnel. Good Monday picks are the National Museum, Gyeongbokgung, Jongmyo, Noryangjin, Seongsu or a Suwon/Nami day trip. TUESDAY Oct 20: Gyeongbokgung and Jongmyo are closed.
[seoul] Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden online 6 days ahead at 10:00 KST (21:00 US Eastern the evening before). Autumn slots sell out in minutes. On-site tickets go on sale at opening.
[seoul] Hanbok means free entry to all palaces and Jongmyo, which saves 1,000-3,000 each. The bigger value is the photos in autumn colors.

[seoul] Seoul foliage timing: 2026 forecasts put Bukhansan's first color around Oct 15-18 and the peak around Oct 28 - Nov 1. In the city the palace ginkgos peak late Oct to early Nov. Expect early-to-mid color on Oct 17-24. Silver grass (Haneul Park) is at its best then.
[seoul] Sunset is about 17:55 on Oct 17 and about 17:47 on Oct 24. Time the Inwangsan hike, Seoul Sky and Haneul Park around it.
[seoul] Get a T-money or WOWPASS card on arrival, and install Naver Map (Google Maps walking directions are poor in Korea), Kakao T (taxis), Catchtable (restaurant bookings) and Papago (translation).

[seoul] Budget sketch for the Seoul portion: about 250,000-450,000 KRW per night for 3 in a mid-range triple or 2-bedroom. Paid sights are cheap (palaces 1,000-3,000; Secret Garden 8,000; Seoul Sky about 29,000; N Seoul Tower 21,000; DMZ tour about 75,000; Starlight Tour 60,000).

[seoul] Airbnb and short-term rentals: since 2026, unregistered listings can no longer be booked, and Airbnb requires a business registration number. Only 'foreign-tourist urban homestay' (외국인관광 도시민박업, host must live on site), hanok-experience businesses and licensed lodging are legal. Officetel 'apartments' are illegal and risk last-minute cancellation. Prefer hotels, serviced residences and registered hanok stays.

[vibe] Booking sushi/hansik as foreigners: CatchTable Global app takes foreign cards and no Korean phone number; many top counters (Sosuheon, Sushi Matsumoto, Onjium, Mori, Iwa) manage bookings by phone only - ask your hotel concierge to call, or DM on Instagram.
[vibe] Expect strict no-show rules: typical 50% charge within 3 days and 100% within 24 h; deposits charged at booking on CatchTable.
[vibe] Lunch omakase is 30-50% cheaper than dinner at the same counter (e.g., Sushi Kanesaka Seoul lunch KRW 230k vs dinner 330k).
[vibe] Korean sushi tiers in 2026: entry KRW 50k-100k, mid 100k-200k, high-end 200k-500k per person (dinner).

[vibe] Best Izu-ryokan substitute is usually two pieces: an ocean-view hot-spring hotel (Paradise Busan/Ananti) + a kaiseki-like dinner (Mori in Busan, Mingles/Onjium/Bicena in Seoul) - Korea has few true all-in-one ryokans.

[vibe] Hoe markets: buy fish by weight on the ground floor, then pay a per-person setting fee (KRW ~5,000-6,000) upstairs plus extra for maeuntang spicy fish stew; confirm the price per kg before the fish is killed.

[vibe] For the 'Kamakura day' do: Blueline Sky Capsule Mipo->Cheongsapo (morning) - Daritdol Skywalk - Beach Train to Songjeong - taxi to Haedong Yonggungsa - Gijang/Daebyeon hoe lunch - Ananti Cove or back to Haeundae.
[vibe] Pair Naksansa + Abai Village + Sokcho market with a Seoraksan foliage day; Seorak hot-spring resorts make it ryokan-ish.
[vibe] Gangneung is the easiest Seoul day trip that scratches the seaside-town itch (KTX ~1h50 from Seoul Station).

resolutions.followup-donghae_line_and_canonical_rail: (1) Donghae-line KTX-Eum from Gangneung: 752 dep 09:36 arr Gyeongju 12:30 (2h54) / arr Bujeon 13:36; 754 dep 14:56 arr Gyeongju 17:44 / Bujeon 18:50; 756 dep 18:35 arr Gyeongju 21:22 / Bujeon 22:29. Fares 34,300 (Gangneung-Gyeongju) and 46,800 (Gangneung-Bujeon), adult general seat. Plus ITX-Maeum 1822 dep 05:46 arr Gyeongju 09:08 (24,800) / Bujeon 10:49 (34,900). Source: train.asamaru.net timetable for Oct 7-13 2026, identical every day that week (high confidence for that week; medium-high for Oct 21-23 because no timetable revision is announced, but the specific dates and live seat availability could NOT be read: korail.com search is a JavaScript app that does not render without a browser session). The Gyeongju arrival estimate of 12:20 is wrong: use 12:30. The service originates at Gangneung (news: 'departs Gangneung, stopping at Jeongdongjin, Mukho, Donghae, Samcheok, Uljin, Yeongdeok, Pohang, Gyeongju, Taehwagang to Bujeon'; high confidence). (2) The Donghae-line KTX-Eum started Dec 30, 2025, with 3 round trips a day (high confidence; Dec 15 2025 press reports). logistics.json's 'Dec 30 2024' is a year off. heritage.json's 'Dec 20 2024' refers to the Jungang-line KTX-Eum (Cheongnyangni-Andong-Gyeongju-Bujeon) starting to stop at Gyeongju. That is a different service and both statements can be true. (3) The booking window is 2 months before departure from Oct 1, 2026 (high confidence; SBS Biz Sep 20 2026 and Wikitree, a MOLIT/Korail announcement). The 1-month figure is the old rule. The opening hour (07:00) is the long-standing Korail practice and was not restated in the articles (medium). The point is moot for this trip: Oct 17-25 is already inside even the old 1-month window, so every train is on sale NOW and the group should book today, especially the 3-a-day KTX-Eum and the foliage-season weekend trains to Gangneung. (4) Canonical fares after the Sep 1 2026 KTX-SRT merger (about a 10% cut on high-speed KTX routes, guaranteed for 3 years): Seoul-Gyeongju 44,500 (KTX; 44,000 on KTX-Sancheon, 44,600 on KTX-Eum). heritage's 49,300 is the pre-cut fare. Gyeongju-Busan Station 10,100 (heritage's ~11,000 is pre-cut). Seoul-Busan 54,400 (was 59,800). Seoul-Gangneung 27,600, unchanged by the cut (standing 23,500). AREX Express: official fare 13,000 adult (walk-up 'regular fare' 18,500/19,100 is the theoretical undiscounted price). 11,000 is only a third-party voucher price (Klook/Trip.com/Waug), so plan with 13,000 and treat 11,000 as an optional saving. All high confidence. (5) The Gangneung-Samcheok Sea Train (바다열차) is NOT running: it was retired after its last run on Dec 26, 2023 (old rolling stock, no budget). Gangwon mentions a revival only as a future plan (July 2026). For a coastal ride, use the regular Donghae-line KTX-Eum, ITX-Maeum or Nuriro between Gangneung, Jeongdongjin and Samcheok, sitting on the left/east side heading south. High confidence.

resolutions.followup-gyeongbokgung_starlight_foreign: Treat the Starlight Night Walk as a long shot. Do not pin the itinerary to it. Creatrip is the only sales channel for the Oct 21-24 foreigner-only sessions (NOL World is not used in 2026). The live Creatrip page (spot 13949, checked Oct 6, 2026) shows isSoldOut=true for every session. There are 8 sessions in total, 2 per night, with at most 38 people each, so about 304 seats overall. Each person can buy at most 2 tickets, so a group of 3 needs two separate bookers. You cannot buy on the day. Sales for each date close at 23:59 KST two days before. Cancellations get a full refund up to 3 days before and no refund after that, so released seats mostly reappear before each date's free-cancel cutoff. They tend to come back 1-2 at a time, which makes 3 seats in one session unlikely. The session times are settled at 18:20-20:10 and 19:30-21:20 (Creatrip listing, Korea Times, Korean press). The 18:30/19:40 times in events.json are wrong. The price is 60,000 KRW per person (US$44.81 on Creatrip, or $42.12 for members). Ticketlink general sessions do not run Oct 21-24, because those nights are foreigner-only. The only general nights in the trip window are Sat Oct 17 and Sun Oct 18. They were sold by lottery in August and then first-come from Aug 28, they are in Korean, and they are almost certainly gone. The fallback is confirmed and is good. Changgyeonggung is open 09:00-21:00 (last entry 20:00, closed Mon). It runs the 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' media-art night on Wed-Sun, Oct 7 - Nov 1, with pond-show sessions at 19:00, 19:30 and 20:00 (about 16 min each). That show costs 1,000 KRW including admission, via Ticketlink (up to 4 per person) or Creatrip for foreigners. The rest of the light route can be seen with normal admission. Deoksugung is open 09:00-21:00 (closed Mon). Under the weekly 'Culture Day' policy, every Wednesday is free at Deoksugung since Aug 2026 and at Changgyeonggung, Changdeokgung (not Huwon) and Jongmyo since Oct 2026. Gyeongbokgung is not included yet. So Wed Oct 21 is a free palace evening. Confidence: high on sold-out status, times, price and rules; medium on Mulbit availability (not checked live) and on Wednesday-free details.

resolutions.followup-seorak_cablecar_heullimgol_bus_: (1) Seorak Cable Car: the official site's live feed, read 12:15 KST Wed Oct 7 2026, shows hours of 08:30-17:30 today and tomorrow and 08:00-17:30 on Fri Oct 9 (Hangeul Day). Hours are set day by day, so expect about 08:00/08:30-17:30 for Oct 19-23. 17:30 is the close (ticket sales and last boarding). Adult round trip is 16,000 KRW and confirmed on the official 2026 fare table. Round trip only; there is no hiking trail down from the top. Tickets are sold only on the day at the 1st-floor counter or kiosk, with no advance booking. Each ticket is printed with a boarding time. The site shows no per-person limit (the only '1 ticket per person' rule is for the Sokcho-resident discount). A full refund is possible up to 10 min before boarding; after that, a time change or refund costs 20%. There is no official data on weekday sell-out times. On Oct 7 midday (a weekday, before peak) the wait was only 19 minutes. At peak, waits of 1-3 h are common, and on weekends the day's slots can be fully allocated by around midday. Plan to be at the counter by 08:00-08:30 on a weekday. Confidence: high for fare and sales rules, medium-high for hours, low for sell-out timing. (2) Heullimgol: it is OPEN for autumn 2026 and a reservation IS required, Oct 1-Nov 30 2026. The 5,000/day cap is correct (gangwon.json was right) and applies to the 3.1 km one-way section from the Heullimgol Visitor Center to Yongso junction. It is split into hourly slots of about 1,000 each: 08:00-15:00 in October, 09:00-14:00 in November. One booking covers up to 10 people. Online booking (reservation.knps.or.kr, Korean site) closes at 14:00 the day before. Leftover places can be registered on site at the Heullimgol Visitor Center. Hiking without a booking can draw a fine (200,000 KRW for a first offence, up to 500,000), and no-shows get booking bans. The reopening date was Sep 8 2022 (planned for Sep 6 but delayed by Typhoon Hinnamnor), after a closure from Aug 2015 that followed a fatal rockfall. foliage.json's '2024' is wrong; gangwon.json's 'Sep 6 2022' is the planned date. I found no 2026 rockfall closure, though the trail is closed on the day in rain or strong wind. Foreigners: KNPS's English/foreigner portal lists only shelters and campsites, not trail reservations. The Korean site normally requires Korean mobile or i-PIN identity verification, so online booking with a foreign phone is unlikely to work (unverified). The realistic routes are on-site leftover registration at the Heullimgol Visitor Center, which is very likely available on a weekday given the 5,000 cap, or a booking made by a Korean contact or the hotel. The booking-open date is not published; it closes at 14:00 the day before. Juongol from Osaek out and back (to Yongso Falls) needs NO booking, and two-way walking is allowed there. The reservation and the one-way rule apply only to the Heullimgol section, and walking up it in reverse is forbidden. Confidence: high (KNPS service guide + Oct 5 2026 Maeil Shinmun + Sep 2026 Travel News). (3) Buses after the 9% cap rise on Oct 1 2026, adult weekday fares. Seoul Express Bus Terminal (Gangnam) to Sokcho: standard 18,700 / deluxe (udeung) 24,300 / premium 31,500 / late-night about 29,100, about 2h35-3h, 45 departures a day 06:00-23:30. Dong Seoul to Sokcho: deluxe 22,800 / premium 29,600, about 2h16-2h26, 15 a day. Gangneung to Sokcho intercity: mostly 8,400 (direct, about 1 h), with 10,800 on slower 1h40-1h46 runs. The 7,800 fares on 2 runs look like pre-rise data that has not been updated. These figures come from asamaru timetable mirrors dated Oct 2-7 2026, because kobus.co.kr refused connections and was not checked directly. Foreign cards: Kobus has accepted foreign-issued Visa/Mastercard since Aug 2024 (the year comes from the Korea JoongAng Daily article on KTO plans; not seen directly). The T-money intercity site has an English version (intercitybuse.tmoney.co.kr) with a foreign-card option reported. Klook sells express-bus tickets as a fallback. Terminal kiosks and counters take foreign cards and cash. Confidence: medium-high for fares, medium for card acceptance.
